title: chore: release 22 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.42.0` → `0.43.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.42.0` → `0.43.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.42.0` → `0.43.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.42.0` → `0.43.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.42.0` → `0.43.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.42.0` → `0.43.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.42.0` → `0.43.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.42.0` → `0.43.0` | breaking |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.31.10` → `0.31.11` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-proof` | npm | `0.2.4` → `0.2.5` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-tsp` | npm | `0.2.0` → `0.2.1` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-capability-client` | npm | `0.2.3` → `0.2.4` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.15.0`) | `0.14.0` → `0.15.0` | breaking |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go/proof` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/proof/v0.3.1`) | `0.3.0` → `0.3.1` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go/didcomm` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/didcomm/v0.4.1`) | `0.4.0` → `0.4.1` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go/capabilityclient` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/capabilityclient/v0.3.1`) | `0.3.0` → `0.3.1` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go/specs` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/specs/v0.3.0`) | `0.2.0` → `0.3.0` | breaking |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.13.0` → `0.14.0` | breaking |
| `trust_tasks_proof` | pub.dev | `0.2.3` → `0.2.4` | patch |
| `trust_tasks_https` | pub.dev | `0.3.2` → `0.3.3` | patch |
| `trust_tasks_didcomm` | pub.dev | `0.2.2` → `0.2.3` | patch |
| `trust_tasks_capability_client` | pub.dev | `0.2.2` → `0.2.3` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the
  tag, which *is* the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,
  `tag-dart` pushes the tag, and `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: fix(rs,go,dart)!: validate the payload as received on the typed consume paths
body:
**Stacked on #1385.** This PR is based on `fix/rs-preserve-presence` and merges after #1385. Once #1385 merges, retarget it to `main`. @stormer78, this is the follow-up to the typed-consume gap noted on #1385. Under `PayloadPolicy::Validate` (and the Go and Dart equivalents), the typed consume paths now validate the payload as it was received, not the decoded and re-encoded payload. ## The gap `docs/runtime-parity.md` (from #1385) records the rule that a `null` on an optional member whose schema has no null form is refused by payload-schema validation, not by typed decoding. Three of the typed consume paths didn't follow it, because they validated the payload *after* decoding it into the generated type and re-encoding it: - Rust `consume_inbound::

`: `serde_json::to_value(&doc.payload)` - Go `ConsumeInbound[P]`: `json.Marshal(doc.Payload)` - Dart `consumeInbound`: `payloadToJson(doc.payload)` Concrete case: acl/update 0.3 with `"purposes": null`. That schema has no null form for `purposes`. All three typed decoders read the `null` as absent. The re-encoded payload then omits the member, so validation passes and a document the schema refuses is accepted. Rust's `consume_dispatched` and TypeScript's `consumeInbound` already validated the payload as received and refused it. This gap predates #1385. ## The fix Each typed path now validates the received payload whenever the received document is in hand and the document being consumed is a reading of it. The fix adds no new API, because each library already carries the received document for proofs and the item-11 digest: - **Rust:** the `ProofPolicy` bound with `with_received` (`VerifyReceived`, `RejectIfPresentReceived`, `AcceptUnverifiedReceived`). `GuardedConsumer::consume_body` already binds it, so the DIDComm, DIDComm v1 and TSP consumers get the fix as they stand. Inside `consume_core`, the received-document check now runs before item 2, and a private `ReceivedPayload` tells it which payload to validate. - **Go:** `ConsumeOptions.Received`, checked with the existing `isReadingOf`. `ConsumeReceived` already sets it, so the `tsp` and `didcomm` consumers get the fix too. - **Dart:** the `received` argument, checked the same way the proof and digest code already check it (same `id` and `type`). The HTTPS, DIDComm and TSP packages already pass it. They build against the published core, so they pick this up with the next core release. Without the received document, a typed path still has only the re-encoding to validate. The docs say to pass it whenever the received JSON is in hand. ## Forwarding tradeoff A later version routed forward along `extends` carries members the implemented schema refuses (`additionalProperties: false`). Validating its received payload as it stands would refuse every forwarded document. So the received payload is validated as received **only for a document of the implemented version**. A forwarded document is validated with its received payload pruned to the members the implemented schema knows, which is exactly what `consume_dispatched` does: - Rust prunes with `extension::prune_forward` against `P::PAYLOAD_SCHEMA` (`Reading::Forward`). - Go re-reads the received bytes with `ReadForSpecWith` and the caller's `Extends` lookup. - Dart re-reads `received` with `readForVersion` and the caller's `extendsIndex`. A forbidden `null` on a member the implemented version knows is still refused on a forwarded document. A member only the later version declares is pruned before validation, as on the dispatched path. ## Behavioural change for consumers A document that passed only because its re-encoding dropped something the schema refuses is now refused `malformedRequest` by the typed paths, when the received document is supplied. The main case is a forbidden `null` on an optional member. The `!` in the title is for this: no signature changes, but a consumer can observe the difference. A producer that sends such a `null` needs to stop sending it. The change is recorded in `docs/runtime-parity.md`, `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` and the Rust, Go and Dart package docs. No version bumps, no changelog entries, no `SPEC.md` edits, and no spec changes, so nothing was regenerated. **Interim workaround** until a release carrying this: a typed consumer validates the received payload itself before decoding. In Rust that's `P::validate_value(&received["payload"])`. In Go and Dart, run your validator on the received payload. ## Tests - **Shared vector** `fixtures/consume/received-payload.json` (described in `fixtures/consume/README.md`): six cases through each runtime's typed consume function. Each case checks the verdict and the exact payload handed to the validator. They cover the implemented version with a value, absent, and with a forbidden `null` (refused); a later version read forward with an added member (accepted, validated pruned); a later version with a forbidden `null` on a member the implemented version knows (refused); and a `null` on a member only the later version declares (pruned, accepted). It runs in: - `trust-tasks-rs/tests/received_payload_vectors.rs`, which also checks the bundled `jsonschema` engine agrees under `validate`; - `trust-tasks-go/trusttasks/received_payload_vectors_test.go`; - `trust-tasks-dart/test/received_payload_vectors_test.dart`; - `trust-tasks-ts/test/received-payload-vectors.test.ts`, which passes with no TypeScript change. - **Rust:** the pinned `the_typed_path_does_not_see_a_forbidden_null` in `tests/member_presence.rs` is now `the_typed_path_refuses_a_forbidden_null`. It expects `malformedRequest` on acl/update 0.3 `"purposes": null` with the received document bound. A new `without_the_received_document_the_typed_path_cannot_see_it` pins the unbound fallback. - **Go:** `TestWithoutReceivedTheForbiddenNullIsNotSeen` pins the same refusal with `Received` set and the fallback without it. The core module cannot import the generated `specs` module, so the vector's payload type uses the same `*T` / `omitempty` shape as acl/update's `Purposes`. - **Dart:** a test on the generated acl/update 0.3 type (`"purposes": null` refused `malformedRequest` with `received`), plus the no-`received` fallback. ## Checks run Local (`brendan-nvme`): - `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean. - `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-rs --all-targets --features acl,validate -- -D warnings`: clean. - `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features acl,validate`: all passed, 0 failed. - `cargo doc -p trust-tasks-rs --no-deps --features validate,acl` with `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`: clean. - Go: `gofmt -l`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` in `trust-tasks-go`: all green. - Dart: `dart format`, `dart analyze lib/src test` (no issues) and the full `dart test` in `trust-tasks-dart`: all passed. - TypeScript: the `trust-tasks-ts` test build, then the full `node --test`: 291 passed, 0 failed. Builder (`bam-llm-server-builder`), all on head `f7e71905e`, exit 0, 32 minutes: - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: clean. - `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --features trust-tasks/all-specs`: 74 suites, 4,991 passed, 0 failed. - `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate,all-specs --all-targets`: 27 suites, 4,511 passed, 0 failed. This includes the flipped `member_presence` tests and `received_payload_vectors`. - `npm ci && npm run check`: green. Bindings conformance agrees across all 1,431 specifications, and the runtime defaults, package lists, release lists and doc facts all agree.

title: fix(rs,go,dart)!: validate the payload as received on the typed consume paths (#1398)
body:
fix(rs,go,dart)!: validate the payload as received on the typed consume paths (#1398) * test(rs): show generated payload types losing member presence on a round trip An optional array decodes [] as absent and re-encodes it absent; an optional nullable member decodes null as absent (acl/update 0.3's "label: null clears it" becomes "leave it unchanged"); an optional {"type": "null"} member is written back as null when absent. The trust-tasks-rs tests round-trip acl/show 0.3 and acl/update 0.3; the trust-tasks-build tests pin the field shapes on a fixture module. Both fail until the generator keeps presence. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * fix(rs): keep an optional member's presence in generated payload types typify renders an optional array or map as a bare Vec/Map skipped when empty, an optional member whose schema admits null as an Option skipped when None, and an optional {"type": "null"} member as () with #[serde(default)]. Decoding then re-encoding a document therefore turned [] and {} into an absent member, an explicit null into an absent member, and an absent null-only member into null -- changing the meaning wherever a schema tells those states apart (acl/update: "null clears it, omitted leaves it unchanged"; vta/app-state/put: "a present-and-null value is not the same as omitting the member"). A new trust-tasks-build pass rewrites those fields after typify: - optional array / map: Vec -> Option> (and the map types) - optional, admits null: Option -> Option> - optional null-only: () -> Option<()> Each reads through a per-module presence::present helper (deserialize_with) that maps any present value, null included, to Some, and is skipped only when None. The builder's field and setter follow the new type. Nullable members are found on the schema typify sees, tagged through their description and read back off the field's doc comment; the wire schema (PAYLOAD_SCHEMA) is captured before and carries no tag, and generation fails if the tag survives. Members with a declared default, and required members, are unchanged. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * fix(rs): regenerate the Rust modules so payload types keep member presence Output of cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen and cargo fmt --all with the presence pass: 446 modules change. Optional arrays and maps become Option> / Option>, optional nullable members Option>, each reading through the module's presence::present helper. The hand-written runtime follows the new types without changing what it puts on the wire: the discovery responders read an absent patterns list and an empty one alike (the spec treats both as ["*"]), and the consume tests build acl responses with redacted_fields: None. The member_presence test now also checks decode-then-inspect and the builder. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * test(rs): read rooms/keys/chain 0.2 links through its new Option in anyof_required_members The optional links array is now Option>, so the round-trip test compares its length through the Option. The document it round-trips is unchanged. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * docs(rs): describe how generated payload types keep absent, empty and null apart Field shapes (Option>, Option>, Option<()>), what the builder setters now take, and how to send an explicit null. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * docs: add a runtime-parity row for absent, empty and null payload members Rust and TypeScript keep all three states. Go and Dart keep [] but fold an optional null into absent, and drop the key of a null required nullable member. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * fix(rs): allow clippy::type_complexity on the generated spec tree A builder keeps each field as Result, so an optional map member that now keeps its presence (vta/dids/get 0.1 and vta/dids/list 0.1 methodDetails, Option>>) trips the lint under --all-features. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * fix(rs,build): refuse a null on an optional member that has no null form Every optional member now reads through one of two helpers: `present` where the schema admits `null` (as before), and `not_null` everywhere else, so a forbidden `null` (acl/update 0.3 `"purposes": null`) is refused instead of being read as absent. The field type of such a member is unchanged. Whether a schema admits `null` is now decided over every keyword that can restrict it (`type`, `const`, `enum`, `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`, `$ref`, a `not` of exactly `null`); anything those do not settle is taken to admit it, so a `null` the schema accepts is never refused. A `true` member is rewritten to `{}` in typify's copy so it can carry the tag, and becomes `Option>` like `{}`. The repository's own modules name one crate-private copy of the helpers (`crate::specs::presence` in trust-tasks-rs), which adds no public API; an application's modules keep a per-module copy of only the helpers they use, so they need nothing new from the runtime's `__private`. The enum-variant refusal now says why: a member of the same name elsewhere admits null, and a variant's fields carry no doc to read the tag back from. The fixture gains an intrinsic `default: []` and `default: null`, a `true` member, and every field-shape assertion now runs for both targets. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * fix(rs): regenerate the Rust modules after the rebase onto main, with strict optional-member decoding Regenerated with `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`, never merged by hand. The modules main added since the branch base (credential-exchange/present 0.2, auth/step-up approve-request 0.6, the vta/dids next versions) take the presence shapes; every module reads its optional members through crate::specs::presence and drops its per-module helper. No existing module's field types change. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * test(rs): refuse a forbidden null on acl/update 0.3, and round-trip an empty map acl/update 0.3 purposes, approve, keys and ext have no null form and now refuse one. vta/did-templates/update 3.2 template.defaults keeps {} apart from absent and refuses null. The builder test notes that show's entry is required, so its None is the member's null rather than the optional-member rule. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * docs: describe strict optional-member decoding and intrinsic defaults docs/packages/rust.md: a forbidden null is refused, how null-admission is decided, true members, the shared and per-module helpers, and that a default equal to typify's intrinsic one is rewritten like no default. docs/runtime-parity.md: the Rust cell and the decision note say what each runtime does with a forbidden null. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * fix(build): satisfy clippy::needless_bool in admits_null Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * test(build): drop a single-element loop in the member-presence fixture test Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * fix(rs): regenerate the Rust modules after the rebase onto main (#1373) The vtc/rooms/community versions main added were generated without the member-presence pass. Regenerated with `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`; nothing hand-merged. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * fix(build): fail generation where a nullable member's null handling cannot be read back Strict decoding refuses a null on an optional member whose schema has no null form. Two paths could still refuse a null the schema admits: - a tagged member typify renders as a bare Vec or map skipped when empty (a type-less `{"additionalProperties": ...}`) fell through to `not_null`; it is now a generation error, like the enum-variant case; - a tag typify dropped left the field on `not_null` silently. Each tag now carries its own id, and generation fails on any id not read back off a field (a required enum-variant field of that name accounts for it). Also: a schema nested past the depth bound counts as admitting null, the admits_null doc states the 2020-12 `$ref` reading, unit cases cover allOf, a non-null const, an enum and a type array without null, a oneOf with no null branch and a reference cycle, and a fixture test checks that the emitted and the hand-written refusal messages are the same text. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * fix(rs): rename the shared member-presence helpers to specs::__presence `crate::specs::presence` shared a namespace with the generated family modules, so a future spec family named `presence` would not compile. A slug segment starts with a letter, so no family can be called `__presence`. Regenerated with `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`; the generated change is the helper path only. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * docs: describe the generation errors and the 2020-12 $ref reading for member presence Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * fix(build): account for an unread nullable tag by a variant field only under a oneOf or anyOf branch A required enum-variant field accounted for every unread tag of its name across the module, so a struct member whose description typify dropped could hide behind a same-named field of an unrelated enum and refuse a null its schema admits. mark() now records whether each tag sits under a oneOf / anyOf branch (or on an object whose own oneOf / anyOf typify merges its members into), and only those tags can be accounted for by a variant field or make an optional variant field ambiguous. The unread-tag error now suggests a remedy, and the bare-collection error names the owning struct. Unit tests build the generated items by hand and cover the unread-tag error, the variant exemption and its masking case, the ambiguous optional variant field, and the branch recording. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * docs(rs): give the remedy for each member-presence generation error Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * fix(rs): regenerate the Rust modules added on main with the presence pass Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * fix(build): read a null on an optional member with no null form as absent, not refuse it Drop the not_null helper and the deserialize_with it put on every optional member whose schema has no null form. A non-nullable optional member is left as typify renders it, and a non-nullable optional array or map becomes Option> / Option with no helper, so a null reads as absent there. Refusing such a null is payload-schema validation's job, as in the TypeScript, Go and Dart runtimes; the per-field refusal cost about 2 GiB of compiler memory on the prebuilt tree. Kept: present, the absent/empty/null field shapes, the per-tag ids, the unread-tag, ambiguous-variant-field and bare-collection generation errors, and the oneOf/anyOf variant exemption. Their rationale is now that a wrong guess would lose a null the schema accepts. The fixture test comparing the emitted and hand-written refusal messages is removed with the refusal. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * fix(rs): regenerate the Rust modules without the not_null refusal cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all: removes the 14,689 deserialize_with = "crate::specs::__presence::not_null" attributes, and nothing else. The hand-written specs::__presence keeps only present; its unit test now pins that a null without a null form reads as absent. tests/member_presence.rs: the strict-null tests become tests of the decided behaviour. A forbidden null decodes as absent and re-encodes without the member (acl/update 0.3 purposes, approve, keys, ext; acl/show 0.3 redactedFields; the vta did-templates defaults map). Validating the received payload refuses it: ValidatedPayload::validate_value, and consume_dispatched with PayloadPolicy::Validate. The typed consume_inbound validates the re-encoded payload and does not see it; that is pinned too. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * docs: record that a forbidden null is refused by schema validation, not by typed decoding runtime-parity.md: a separate, decided row for a null on an optional member with no null form, in all four runtimes. It records the typed consume paths (Rust consume_inbound::

, Go ConsumeInbound[P], Dart consumeInbound), which validate the re-encoded payload and so miss it, as a todo that predates this change. The absent/empty/null row keeps only the Go and Dart write-side question as Needs decision. rust.md and the PayloadPolicy doc say the same. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * docs: record that an optional array or map's forbidden null now decodes as absent typify's bare Vec / map refused a null at decode; the presence pass makes it Option> / Option, where serde reads null as None. That is a loosening a typed consumer can observe, so say so in rust.md's migration notes and in the runtime-parity row. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * fix(rs,go,dart)!: validate the payload as received on the typed consume paths With a payload-validating policy, Rust consume_inbound::

, Go ConsumeInbound[P] and Dart consumeInbound validated the payload decoded into the typed payload and re-encoded. A typed decode reads a null on an optional member whose schema has no null form (acl/update 0.3 "purposes": null) as absent, so the re-encoding passed and the document was accepted. Each now validates the received payload whenever the received document is in hand (Rust: the ProofPolicy bound with with_received; Go: ConsumeOptions.Received; Dart: received) and the document being consumed is a reading of it. A document of the implemented version is validated as received; a later version read forward along extends is validated with its payload pruned to the implemented schema, as consume_dispatched prunes a forwarded payload. Without the received document the typed paths still validate the re-encoding. A document previously accepted for a forbidden null is now refused malformedRequest. Adds the shared vector fixtures/consume/received-payload.json, run by all four runtimes, and flips the pinned Rust test to expect the refusal. Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller * docs: record that the typed consume paths validate the payload as received Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller --------- Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore Co-authored-by: Glenn Gore

Changelog

## `vti-specs-vtc`

## [0.8.3](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-specs-vtc-v0.8.2...vti-specs-vtc-v0.8.3) — 2026-11-27 ### Added - **vtc**: Vtc/directory/query/0.2 answers the member's entry ([#2827](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2827)) * feat(vtc): vtc/directory/query/0.2 answers the member's entry The portal names a room's authors by DID with vtc/directory/query, but every other directory read is addressed by entry: the member's picture (images/get), their entry with shared groups (entries/show), and their card page. Without the entry it could name an author but not show their picture or open their card. query/0.2 (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1383) is served beside 0.1 by the same authority — any entry, or the member portal's delegated key as its member — and answers `entryId`, the member's directory entry (`directory::read::QueryAnswer`). It is answered only where 0.1 answers at all: where the projection shows the caller the member's DID, to the member, or to an administrator; everyone else gets the same notFound as no member, with no entry. 0.1 is unchanged. Pinned from a local build of the spec PR; re-pin from trusttasks.org once it publishes. - **vtc**: Administrators set a community room's record members — replies and reactions ([#2824](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2824)) * feat(vtc): administrators set a community room's record members — replies and reactions A community-owned room's profile was written with its label and description only, so a room meant as a conversation started with replies and reactions off, and turning them on took a member holding `curate`. The community holds `admin` in every room it owns; its administrators now set them. Serves vtc/rooms/community create/0.6, update/0.5 and get/0.6 beside the earlier versions (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1373): - create/0.6 `recordMembers` is written into the profile with the label and description (item 12), echoed and audited; absent is none. - update/0.5 `recordMembers` (the whole set) or `removeRecordMembers`; a set compares as a set, and a record-members-only change re-writes the profile. Neither given, the read-back's set is carried over as before. - get/0.6 answers what the profile listed at the community's last write — never a pending request's set (item 6). - `rooms::community_profile` keeps a requested set in a new `RecordMembersRecord` (`room-record-members:`) until a write carries it; a set requested while a write is in flight keeps the room pending. Unknown values are never refused. The console's room form gains a "Replies and reactions" box beside Watch signals: ticked on create (sends kind, inReplyTo, writtenAt), shown and editable on a room's page, sent on edit only when it changed and keeping any other member a curator listed, with a note about members on an older reader. `cnm rooms create|update` take `--replies-and-reactions`, `--record-member` and (update) `--no-record-members`; `cnm rooms get` prints them.
## `vta-sdk`

Unknown values are never refused. The console's room form gains a "Replies and reactions" box beside Watch signals: ticked on create (sends kind, inReplyTo, writtenAt), shown and editable on a room's page, sent on edit only when it changed and keeping any other member a curator listed, with a note about members on an older reader. `cnm rooms create|update` take `--replies-and-reactions`, `--record-member` and (update) `--no-record-members`; `cnm rooms get` prints them. - **vtc**: The portal names a room's authors as the member directory shows them ([#2822](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2822)) In a room used for chat, an author the wallet's reading gives no name was shown by the last segment of their did:webvh (`airport-electric`), which reads as a name but is only a path the DID's owner chose. ## `vtc-client`
## [0.49.1](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vtc-client-v0.49.0...vtc-client-v0.49.1) — 2026-11-27 ### Added - **vtc-client**: Room tasks ask the newest version the host serves ([#2834](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2834)) `vtc-client` asked `rooms/records/put/0.3`, `get/0.3`, `list/0.6`, `rooms/create/0.2` and `rooms/watch/0.1`, each superseded. It now asks `put/0.5`, `get/0.4`, `list/0.8`, `create/0.3` and `watch/0.2`, and asks again at the version before only when the host answers `unsupportedType` (one helper, `room_task_newest`), so a host that predates a version still answers. Every request still carries only what all those versions accept, so the older answers mean the same. `put_cleartext_record` is new: an open room's record checked against `put/0.5`, so it may carry `kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt` and `editedAt` (and 0.4's `file`). It falls back only to a version whose schema accepts the record as given; a record that needs 0.5 gets an older host's refusal back rather than being sent without its reply or kind. `put_cleartext_record_v3` is deprecated in its favour. `put_sealed_record_with_blobs` asks the newest put too; its answer is read against the version that gave it and returned as the same published type, since every version answers the same members. Read retries on `429` now also cover `get/0.4`, `list/0.8` and `info/0.4` and `0.5` (the last two were missing). The admin-action test fixture names `acl/change-role/0.2`, the version the VTC serves.
## `vta-cli-common`
## [0.67.1](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-cli-common-v0.67.0...vta-cli-common-v0.67.1) — 2026-11-27 ### Fixed - **rooms**: Pnm reads a room's file at rooms/records/get/0.3, as its other reads do ([#2837](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2837)) `pnm rooms file get` asked only rooms/records/get/0.2. It now asks get/0.3 through rooms/keys/act/0.11 and falls back to get/0.2 only when the host or the VTA answers unsupportedType, and the member-name read gains the same fallback. Every answer is read as the generated type of the version that gave it. get/0.4 is not asked: no published rooms/keys/act version (0.8–0.12) lists it, so a VTA cannot relay it, and its one addition is a purpose of use these reads do not name. The "only unsupportedType falls back" decision is now one function, `newest_answer`, under test.

## [0.35.3](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vtc-service-v0.35.2...vtc-service-v0.35.3) — 2026-11-27 ### Added - **vtc**: The room's member card shows the member's picture and opens their directory card ([#2829](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2829)) The portal now asks the directory about a room's authors at vtc/directory/query/0.2, whose answer names the member's directory entry. The wallet now replies, reacts and watches a room (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#454); the portal uses all three, feature-detected, so an older wallet keeps today's chat. - Reply: a message's actions (hover or focus; a tap on a phone) offer Reply; the composer names what is answered and sends it as `putMessage`'s `replyTo`. - React: a small picker of reactions; a reaction chip the member added is theirs to take back (`unreact`). Counts, authors and "yours" are the wallet's reading; the page counts nothing. The wallet confirms each one. - A room whose profile does not list what a reply or reaction needs answers `recordMembersNotListed` and writes nothing: the page says so, stops offering both, and offers the words as a plain message. - Live: `room-live.ts` watches the room through the wallet, reads it again when told it moved and tells the watch what it read; while the wallet cannot watch it reads on a 20-second timer while the tab is visible, and watches again with backoff after a close. It now reads as a chat, in the portal's own tokens, light and dark, down to a phone's width. - The chat is the page: a window-high card whose header carries the room's name, its tier and what the community sees, with a back arrow. The room's DID, epoch, storage and who the member posts as are folded under "About this room". - Messages: another author's on the left under their name and initials once per run, the member's own on the right in the brand's tint. It starts on a message only when the wallet has `putMessage`; an older wallet is offered only a note. Every write still goes through the wallet, which shows it to the member first. - Every name in the chat goes through `speakerOf` and the directory's cards: messages, reactions, rewrites, the drawer's "By", and "you post as" (the member's own DID is now looked up too). - The member card no longer says "As the community's directory shows them to you". It adds a copy button for the DID, and opens upward when there is no room below, kept inside the window. A room of notes and files keeps the records list and its Add panel. - **vtc**: The portal names a room's authors as the member directory shows them ([#2822](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2822)) In a room used for chat, an author the wallet's reading gives no name was shown by the last segment of their did:webvh (`airport-electric`), which reads as a name but is only a path the DID's owner chose. Only the DID is sent, never the room. Keyring shows a room record with text and no title as an ordinary chat message, so a portal member could not answer a conversation going on in Keyring. The compose panel now has a Note / Message switch. It starts on Note, as asked, and remembers the member's last choice in this browser. Message is one box: Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line. It writes through the wallet's new rooms.putMessage (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#453), which writes the text with no title and kind "message" where the room takes it, confirmed in the wallet's window like any write. A wallet without putMessage is offered notes only. The conversation scrolls in its own window, sized to the screen and opened at the newest message. It follows new messages while the member is at the bottom, or when the newest one is their own, and never pulls them down from something older they scrolled up to read. Only the layout changes: the order is still the wallet's, so the portal, the wallet and Keyring show the room alike. ### Documentation - **vtc**: The portal's room chat may write without a window under the wallet's session grant ([#2836](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2836)) OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#457 adds a second bounded exception to "every page write is confirmed": messages and reactions while the one page holds the room open through its watch. The portal needs no code change (the page contract is unchanged); the portal-rooms rule now names the grant and says to keep the watch held for exactly as long as the room is shown, since its closing ends the grant. - **vtc**: The portal's reactions may run under the wallet's reaction grant ([#2833](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2833)) OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#455 lets a member grant a portal, in a reaction's own confirm, 30 minutes of reacting in one room without a window. The portal rooms entry said the wallet confirms every reaction; it now says so except under that grant, which the page can neither request nor see. ### Fixed - **vtc**: The portal's room stops re-reading itself in a loop ([#2835](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2835)) In a live room the page re-read the conversation over and over. After each change the page told the wallet's watch the highest version it had read — the highest record it shows. But the page's records are not every record: reactions, member names, edits and withdrawals are folded into the messages they concern. Once the room's newest record was one of those (a reaction, say), the version acknowledged sat below the room's, the host fired again at once for a room already past it, and the page read, acknowledged the same stale version, and was fired again — forever. The watch's `changed` event carries the room's `latestVersion`. The page now acknowledges the highest of that, what it read and what it holds, and starts a renewed watch from it too. - **vtc**: The portal's live room keeps reading while its watch says it is armed ([#2830](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2830)) "Live" in a portal room is derived from the wallet's watch events and drops on any other event (R6.2). But a watch can stop delivering without saying so — a wedged mediator session in the wallet, a host that lost the watch — and then the page showed "Live" and missed updates for up to the watch's one-day lease. A hidden tab's timers are also throttled to about once a minute, which lets the wallet's service worker be put to sleep between pings. While the watch reports itself armed, the page now also reads the room every five minutes, and at once when the tab is seen again, and tells the watch what it read. A broken delivery costs minutes, never the lease. - **vtc**: The portal key may look a member up by DID, so a room's authors get their names ([#2825](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2825)) The member portal names a room's authors with vtc/directory/query/0.1 ([#2822](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2822)), signed with the key the member delegated `vtc/directory` to at sign-in. The other directory reads accept that key as its member; this one did not. It was handled beside the community's other reads through `member_signer`, which knows only ACL entries, so the portal key was refused with permissionDenied ("the signer holds no entry in this community"). The portal reads a refusal as "no name", so every author stayed a DID, even one whose card the viewer could open. The handler now accepts the delegated key as its member while the session lives (`member_portal::delegation::accept`, as `directory_tasks` does), and authorizes any other signer as before. The projection, and so what the answer may show, is the member's own.

title: docs(hcp): design and plan the VTA as an HCP provider over the hcp/* Trust Tasks, before any code
body:
## What and why

This adds a design and a plan for the Human Context Protocol (HCP 2.0-draft-3,
[loyalagents/hcp-spec](https://github.com/loyalagents/hcp-spec) at `b790561`) in the VTA. No code is included.
It opens early so the design can be read before any code PR, in the design → plan → tasks order the other notes
use.

- `docs/05-design-notes/hcp.md` is the design. HCP operations are carried as the `hcp/*` Trust Tasks, served
  by a `vta-hcp` subsystem behind an `hcp` feature that is off by default. The note also covers:
  - why that carriage cannot be claimed in `conformsTo`, so the HTTP Binding is built beside the same handlers;
  - the roles: Keyring as the person's consent surface, and an agent client admitted with no ACL entry through
    a zero-authority hook;
  - consent through task-consent rather than step-up (VTI-APV-004, 005, 008, 011, 013, 017);
  - sender-bound, hashed, opaque tokens behind one per-request check;
  - fail-closed audit, with revocation as the exception (VTI-AUD-003 to 006);
  - revocation with acknowledged notices on `PushReissuer`'s schedule;
  - the OAuth Authorization Service as an optional sidecar, with the VTA as the only owner of the token store
    (one-time mint tickets, mTLS between them);
  - the decisions, the divergences and where each is recorded, and the editor questions.
- `docs/05-design-notes/hcp-plan.md` gives milestones V0 to V3, aligned with Keyring's agent-connect tiers.
  Each milestone has a runnable demo and an exit check. The plan also covers what runs in parallel, the
  cross-repository dependencies and the risks.
- `docs/05-design-notes/hcp-tasks.md` is the V0 checklist: acceptance, verify and files for each task.
- `tasks/hcp-demo-plan.md` is the V0 demo week.
- `docs/README.md`: two Part V lines.

Depends on the `hcp/*` family, now merged on trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf `main` (#1380, with #1381 and
#1382: 28 tasks at `0.1`, `draft`, framework `0.6.0`) and released in `trust-tasks-rs` 0.42.0, `trust-tasks-build`
0.3.0 and `@openvtc/trust-tasks` 0.31.10. The design, plan, checklist and demo plan follow those specifications and
cite them by path; where V0 narrows or departs from them, `hcp.md` §12 says so (notably the registration at first
approval, the suite's question 52). The gate "no HCP code on `main` before the family's first release" is met. V0
runs from a fork branch that is never merged.

Not in this PR:
- any code;
- the VTI specification texts the design lists (Appendix F entries, a `VTI-HCP-*` proposal, and an Appendix H
  change making the DTG purpose IRIs canonical, with the bare names kept as deprecated aliases). They go to
  dtgwg-vti-spec separately.

Not run: no code changed. `python3 scripts/check-docs.py` passes.

## Requirements

Cited, none implemented: VTI-ACL-001, VTI-ACL-109, VTI-APV-004, VTI-APV-005, VTI-APV-008, VTI-APV-011,
VTI-APV-013, VTI-APV-017, VTI-AUD-003, VTI-AUD-004, VTI-AUD-005, VTI-AUD-006, VTI-TRN-002, VTI-TRN-029,
VTI-OPS-020, VTI-OPS-021, VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-026, VTI-OPS-092.

## Backport

none

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main`
- [x] No `version =` edits in any `Cargo.toml`
- [x] Tests cover the change; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean (docs only:
  no code changed; `scripts/check-docs.py` passes)


## Related

- trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1380: the `hcp/*` suite (28 tasks), with trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1381 (declared unchecked rules) and trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1382 (demos) stacked on it.

body:
docs(hcp): design and plan the VTA as an HCP provider over the hcp/* Trust Tasks, before any code (#2823)

* docs(hcp): design the VTA as an HCP provider over the hcp/* Trust Tasks

The VTA has no HCP code, and the HCP work needs a design the maintainer can
read before any code PR. This note is that design (step 0 of the plan).

It covers what HCP 2.0-draft-3 is and why the Trust Task carriage cannot be
claimed in conformsTo (HCP 1.5, 18.1, A.3), so the HTTP Binding is built
beside the same handlers; the roles (the VTA as Provider, Keyring as the
person's consent surface, an agent client with no ACL entry, an optional
OAuth sidecar); authority (opaque sender-bound hashed tokens, a VerifiedGrant
from one per-request check); consent through task-consent rather than
step-up (VTI-APV-004, 005, 011, 013, 017); fail-closed audit (VTI-AUD-002 to
006); revocation with acknowledged notices on PushReissuer's schedule (HCP
6.2, 9.9); the sidecar rule, with the VTA as sole owner of the token store
and mTLS between them; the decisions with their reasons; and each divergence
(VTI-ACL-001, VTI-TRN-002, VTI-TRN-029, and the HCP readings) with where it
is recorded.

Not run: no code. scripts/check-docs.py passes.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(hcp): plan HCP as milestones V0 to V3 aligned with Keyring's tiers

The plan, its V0 task checklist and the demo-week plan, companions to
docs/05-design-notes/hcp.md, and the Part V index lines for the design and
the plan.

hcp-plan.md orders the work as runnable milestones aligned with Keyring's
agent-connect tiers: V0, the demo, on a fork branch never merged to main
against an unpublished pin; V1 (directives, hardening with HTTP parity first,
the context plane); V2 (the full HTTP Binding and the First-Party claim); V3
(profiles, Provider Interop through the OAuth sidecar, Agent Interop from
vta-mcp). It gives each milestone a runnable demo and an exit check, maps
what runs in parallel, lists the cross-repository dependencies (the hcp/*
suite's release, the Rust presence fix, Keyring, the DTG registry's purpose
IRIs, openvti-starter images, Appendix F) and the risks.

hcp-tasks.md is the V0 checklist with acceptance, verify and files per task.
tasks/hcp-demo-plan.md is the demo week: the script, the MODE=tunnel
environment in portable terms, the day plan and the go/no-go checks.

Not run: no code. scripts/check-docs.py passes.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(hcp): the design and plan cite HCP at its public commit and carry the decisions as decided

A review of the HCP design, plan, checklist and demo plan against the
sources they cite found citations that did not say what the notes claimed,
and decisions written as still open.

Sources:
- HCP is linked at loyalagents/hcp-spec, with normative citations pinned to
  commit b790561.
- The hcp/* family is described as it is proposed to dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf:
  one pull request from feat/hcp-suite (28 tasks), with two stacked on it,
  pinned for V0 as frozen at X0.

Decisions now stated as decided:
- Purpose IRIs are the DTG registry's
  https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/purpose/<name>/<n>, with the draft
  entries task-execution/1 and personalisation/1 named (decision 9, X5).
- The directive action URI for "answers other people" is on a
  Keyring-controlled domain (new decision 16; N8 keeps the extension-point
  question).
- MODE=tunnel for the demo (new decision 17).
- The sidecar's one-time mint ticket is in decision 14.

New: the proposed Appendix H change (DTG IRIs canonical, bare names kept as
deprecated aliases mapped before the exact comparison, VTI-ACL-109), as a
third X1 text and in the dependency table.

Corrections against the code and the specifications:
- Step-up is not self-approve only: step_up.rs also serves a named
  approver. The reason it is unusable stays VTI-APV-005.
- PushReissuer re-signs only when a retry would fall outside the acceptance
  window. A5 makes the notice a fresh document on every attempt.
- VTI-APV-013 (presentation derived from the digested octets) and
  VTI-OPS-021 (same document rules on every transport) are cited for what
  they say. VTI-AUD-002 is dropped from the fail-closed claim, and
  VTI-AUD-004 is cited as tamper evidence.
- HCP citations: the 4-hour default (6.1.3, with expiresIn from the suite);
  purposes are absolute URIs (6.1.5.2); rate limiting (6.2.1) versus
  delaying or conditioning (6.2.3); the 1-hour cap (6.2.3, 7.6); modality
  and acr come from 6.1.6, not 8.1; Management Client credentials (3.2.3,
  5.4, 6.1.9); 9.3 is a plain Bearer token; HCP Client is 3.2.3's name.
- The 300-second hold is the VTA's policy; the specification leaves it to
  the provider.
- The divergence cross-references point to §12, not §11. The notice
  divergence gets editor question N10, where the note had said only "an
  editor question".
- transport-harness is a feature, not a crate.
- The "read from knowledge" line is replaced by a plain statement of which
  RFCs were not re-read.

hcp-tasks.md gains X1, X2 and X5, which V0's exit check needs (now 15
tasks).

Not run: no code. scripts/check-docs.py passes.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(hcp): the design and plan diagrams align in a fixed-width font and fit 100 columns

- hcp.md, the two-paths diagram: the box's sides ran through only its first
  and last rows, and its text sat outside the box. It is redrawn as one
  closed box.
- hcp.md, the architecture diagram: the agent client's label touched its
  border, and the enclave edge's arrow was one column off the mediator's
  stem. The HTTP-clients arrow is cut to fit 100 columns. The caption now
  says that those clients include the conformance suite and third-party
  resource requests, which never pass through the sidecar.
- hcp-plan.md, the milestone diagram: tightened to 93 columns (it was 102).
- hcp-plan.md, the V0 parallel map: C0's branch now leaves from under A1,
  which it depends on, not from the arrow into A2. The map now fits 100
  columns (it was 101).

Not run: no code. scripts/check-docs.py passes.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(hcp): the design takes the decisions on the hcp/* suite review

The review of the design beside the hcp/* suite raised points where the
two disagreed or Keyring needed an answer. The design now takes them:

- Keyring's governance tasks omit accessToken in V0; the VTA checks that
  the proven issuer is the enrolled admin DID, and refuses any other
  issuer permissionDenied. The suite carries this as a working
  assumption pending HCP confirmation (its question 56).
- The consent request carries parentThreadId equal to the held thread,
  and Keyring checks it against the scanned threadId. consent_request.rs
  sets no thread member today, so this is listed as A3 work.
- A hold not approved in time is denied, not reopened: decline, timeout
  and an unknown person get the same permissionDenied, and an ended
  thread is remembered.
- The token expires with its grant (no refresh in 0.1).
- Refusals use the suite's wire codes, hcp:invalidToken and
  permissionDenied; scope-denied is HCP's HTTP name, not a code here.
- The HCP effect kinds and detail shapes are published for Keyring's
  checklist. V0 has no narrowing at approval: approve as asked, then
  narrow with governance tasks.
- A key swap never moves a grant; disconnect revokes both the grant and
  any ACL entry.
- Held replies in vta-sdk and a dedicated vta-mcp HCP tool, keeping the
  token out of the model's context (HCP 10.5), are listed as V1 work;
  vta_call refuses hcp/* until then.
- vta/memory stays beside the HCP entry store in V0; a bridge is
  deferred. vta-mcp is a client bridge, and governance is not held in V0.

The plan, the V0 checklist (A2, A3, A8, A9) and the demo plan follow.

Not run: no code. scripts/check-docs.py passes.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(hcp): the consent path is described as the code at 3ee07a12 has it

Each point was re-read against vta-service at 3ee07a12 (vta-service
0.83.0, the openvti-starter pin):

- Step-up is self-approve only. initiate_self_step_up names the caller
  as the approver, and the ACL entry's stepUp.approver and
  stepUp.require are stored but gate nothing. The step-up row and §5.1
  no longer claim a named approver.
- §5.2 shows how the consent request reaches Keyring: the route from
  approver_mediator, the push engine's TSP, then DIDComm, then REST, a
  single doorbell (the DeviceBinding gateway, else the mediator wake),
  and no send at all when there is no route. Whether the starter's
  mediator serves the wake task is stated as not verified.
- The decision proof must be made for assertionMethod
  (task-consent/decision/0.2), so the admin DID needs an assertionMethod
  key.
- The hold's 300 s is the producer's own expiry, stated apart from the
  policy gate's 900 s pending lifetime, the push's 300 s deliver_by and
  the 600 s consent grant.
- The someone-else-approves row says that PDP-raised consent needs
  [policy] enforcement, which is off by default, and that the HCP
  producer does not go through the PDP.
- The demo plan names 3ee07a12 (or a later main) as the VTI baseline,
  not keyring-wallet's f7b78e29d, which lacks receipts and the wake.

Not run: no code. scripts/check-docs.py passes.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(hcp): the design follows the hcp/* specifications as merged and released

The hcp/* family is now merged on trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf main
(#1380-#1382) and released (trust-tasks-rs 0.42.0, trust-tasks-build 0.3.0,
@openvtc/trust-tasks 0.31.10). This brings the design in line with it, citing
each specification by path:

- Sources: the family's status and release, its CONVENTIONS.md (family error
  codes) and QUESTIONS.md; TSP 1.0 under binding tsp/0.3.
- Tokens: tokenExpiresAt equals the grant's expiresAt, with the 24-hour and
  health_context caps; a request proof on every token-carrying request
  (question 53); every hcp/* proof for authentication; the three family codes
  as CONVENTIONS.md section 1 defines them.
- Management: accessToken OPTIONAL on the 18 governance requests and on
  hcp/entries/create (question 56, with 37); entries/create is not a
  governance task.
- The hold: hint.retryAfter in seconds, another issuer refused
  permissionDenied, a changed payload malformedRequest, subjectHint ignored,
  the same grant with a newly minted token within the hour, never cancelled.
- Registration at first approval stated as a divergence from
  hcp/grants/request's MUST refuse an unregistered issuer (question 52), with
  the issuer VID recorded as the notice VID.
- Query: relevance order (HCP 7.3), not recency; maxEntries default 5.
- Revocation: grant.revoked within 60 seconds, idempotent repeats, a notice
  only to a client holding disclosed entries, abandonment on a non-retryable
  error, the summary's delivered/abandoned/none values.
- Discovery: trust-task-discovery from V0, no HCP discovery document before
  V2, the VID anchor and binding rules.
- N1-N10 mapped to the suite's questions 44-52 and 16; a table of where V0
  narrows or departs from the specifications.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(hcp): the plan, checklist and demo plan follow the released hcp/* suite

- The suite's first release and the Rust presence fix are out together

body:
Bumps the npm group with 1 update in the /trust-tasks-ts-capability-client directory: [@openvtc/trust-tasks](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/tree/HEAD/trust-tasks-ts). Bumps the npm group with 1 update in the /trust-tasks-ts-proof directory: [@openvtc/trust-tasks](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/tree/HEAD/trust-tasks-ts). Bumps the npm group with 1 update in the /trust-tasks-ts-tsp directory: [@openvtc/trust-tasks](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/tree/HEAD/trust-tasks-ts). Updates `@openvtc/trust-tasks` from 0.31.2 to 0.31.3
Changelog

Sourced from @​openvtc/trust-tasks's changelog.

0.31.3 — 2026-11-19

Specifications

  • vtc/rooms/community: A community-owned room states and changes its signal delay (create 0.5, update 0.4, get 0.5) (#1336)

A room a member owns states its signal delay at rooms/create 0.3 and its administrators change it at the host with rooms/signal-delay/set 0.1. A room the community owns could do neither: the community is both the holder of admin and the host, and vtc/rooms/community/create and update carried no such member, so every community room waited a randomised few seconds before each rooms/changed signal however its members used it.

  • create 0.5 takes an optional signalDelay (absent = randomised), records it in the room's host record and always echoes it. A none create is audited with the create.
  • update 0.4 takes an optional signalDelay, applied to the host record with the other details, together or not at all; a change of the delay alone is a change (audited, details timestamps move) that needs no profile write. It touches no watch.
  • get 0.5 always serves the room's signalDelay.
  • Both writes refuse signalDelayNotPermitted when the community's governance as host keeps the delay everywhere, applying nothing.
  • A surface offering none SHOULD say what it gives up.

Links to create 0.4, update 0.3 and get 0.4 move to the new versions.

title: feat(go-bindings)!: keep absent, null and a value apart in optional nullable members
body:
Stacked on #1375 (`feat/go-nullable-core`). Until `fix/go-required-nullable` merges, this branch also carries copies of that fix's commits; they drop out when C is rebased (step 3 of the release order below).

**What changed:** both Go generators now render an optional member whose schema admits `null` as
`trusttasks.Nullable[T]` tagged `omitzero`. They are `scripts/build-go-bindings.mjs` for the
prebuilt tree and `cmd/trust-tasks-gen` for the per-module generator, and each was changed
independently. The prebuilt packages are regenerated, and `specs/go.mod` requires core v0.14.0.

**Why:** a pointer collapses `null` into absent, so a Go client could not send `acl/update`'s
"clear the label". A `oneOf` with `null` stays `json.RawMessage` and is not affected. A non-nullable
optional member is still a pointer.

**Breaking (Go generated types):** an optional member whose schema admits `null` is now
`trusttasks.Nullable[T]` (tag `omitzero`) instead of `*T`.
- Build one with `trusttasks.Value(v)` or `trusttasks.Null[T]()`, and read it with `Get`, `IsNull`
  or `IsSet`.
- A required nullable member stays `*T` and keeps its key when nil (it writes `null`).
- For a plain slice or map, only `Null()` writes `null`: on `acl/*` `allowedKeys`, `Value(nil)`
  writes `[]`, which means no keys.
- Requires core v0.14.0.
- The next Release PR makes this core 0.15.0 and `specs` 0.3.0.

**Tests:**
- Both generators are pinned with probe schemas.
- `specs/smoke/nullable_members_test.go` and its siblings round-trip `acl/update` 0.3, `vtc/registry/records/list` 0.2 and `acl/grant`
  0.1's `allowedKeys` (absent, `null`, `[]`, and `Value(nil)` writing `[]`).
- `specs/smoke` refuses a case-variant member in `vtc/join-requests/list` 0.2's `decision` (a
  `Nullable` over a struct), through both `CheckMemberNames` and a `Document` decode.
- The generator equivalence test passes over every bundle.
- `npm run check-bindings` agrees, and the Go bindings and examples show no drift.

**Docs:**
- `docs/packages/go.md` rule 3 and the `CLAUDE.md` index line name the `Nullable` exception.
- `docs/runtime-parity.md` is updated.
- The `go.yml` comment on the `specs` job no longer counts the smoke tests.

**Before merge:** this PR waits for the core v0.14.0 tag (see below). Until then CI's `specs` job
fails with `missing go.sum entry`.

## Release order

1. Merge `fix/go-required-nullable`, A and B, in any order. **Do not merge a Release PR between
   them**: only A's `go!` turns B into 0.14.0, and C pins v0.14.0.
2. Merge the Release PR. `publish-go` tags core `trust-tasks-go/v0.14.0` and `specs`
   `trust-tasks-go/specs/v0.2.0` (and a minor each for `proof`, `didcomm` and `capabilityclient`).
3. Rebase C onto main. `--onto origin/main d4f405b85` drops everything at or below that commit:
   C's copies of the `fix/go-required-nullable` commits, and A's and B's commits. **It is correct
   only once A, B and `fix/go-required-nullable` are all on `origin/main`** (step 1). Run earlier,
   it would silently drop A or B from C.
   ```sh
   git fetch origin
   git rebase --onto origin/main d4f405b85 feat/go-nullable-bindings   # was 2e7c1dbf1, then 402170bac
   cd trust-tasks-go/specs
   go get github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go@v0.14.0
   go mod tidy
   cd ../..
   npm run build-go-bindings && git status --short   # regenerate; the drift must be empty
   ```
   Amend `go.sum` into `build(go-specs): require the core release that carries trusttasks.Nullable`,
   then push. CI's `specs` job goes green.
4. Merge C. The next Release PR carries core 0.15.0 and `specs` 0.3.0.

title: feat(go-bindings)!: keep absent, null and a value apart in optional nullable members (#1376)
body:
feat(go-bindings)!: keep absent, null and a value apart in optional nullable members (#1376)

* build(go,go-specs,go-proof,go-didcomm,go-capabilityclient)!: require Go 1.24

Raise the `go` directive from 1.22 to 1.24 in the core, specs, proof,
didcomm and capabilityclient modules and in the two Go examples
(consumer-app-go, getting-started-go). tsp stays at 1.27, the floor it
inherits from affinidi-tsp-go. The go.yml matrices that prove the floor
move from ["1.22", "stable"] to ["1.24", "stable"], and the comments, the
dependabot note, go.md and the go.mod the generator and smoke tests write
for their throwaway modules say 1.24.

1.24 is the first release whose encoding/json honours `omitzero`, which an
optional member that admits null needs in order to be a comparable struct
that is still left out when absent.

A consumer whose toolchain is older than 1.24 and that runs with
GOTOOLCHAIN=local (a distribution's Go, a pinned CI image) can no longer
build these modules; with the default GOTOOLCHAIN=auto the go command
fetches 1.24 itself. Go supports only its two newest releases, and 1.22
and 1.23 are long out of support.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(go): add trusttasks.Nullable

Nullable[T] is an optional member whose schema admits null, with three
states: absent (the zero value), null (Null[T]()) and a value (Value(v)),
read with IsSet, IsNull and Get. acl/update 0.3 is the case that needs
all three: an absent label leaves it unchanged, "label": null clears it.

It is a struct with unexported fields, so Nullable[T] compares with ==
whenever T does. IsZero reports absent, so a member tagged `omitzero`
(Go 1.24 and later) is left out; null writes null and a value writes the
value. An absent Nullable that reaches MarshalJSON (a member without
`omitzero`; `omitempty` never omits a struct) is an error rather than a
null, which would turn "leave it unchanged" into "clear it".
UnmarshalJSON reads null as null and anything else as a T.

Nothing uses it yet; the generators move to it separately.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(go): check member names inside a trusttasks.Nullable

CheckMemberNames stopped at any type that decodes itself, and Nullable is
a json.Unmarshaler, so a case-variant member inside one went unchecked:
{"step":{"x":"a","X":"b"}} was refused behind a *step and accepted, read
as x = "b", inside a Nullable[step]. Nullable decodes a non-null member
with a plain encoding/json decode of T, which matches names without
regard to case, so the check has to follow it there.

Nullable now tells the walk its T through an unexported method, and the
walk enters it before the Unmarshaler short-circuit, skipping null. The
tests cover a struct, a slice of structs and a map of structs, each
refused as the same member behind a pointer is.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(go): write a nil slice or map in a trusttasks.Nullable as empty, never null

Value(nil) with a slice or map T wrote null, as encoding/json writes a nil
slice. With Null() there to say null, that mapping is only a trap: on
acl/* allowedKeys null (like absent) means every key and [] means none,
so Value(filtered) with nothing left in filtered granted every key. Only
Null() writes null now; Value(nil) writes [] or {}.

The type doc says so, warns against a Nullable behind a pointer, nested
or as a map value (each fails silently, and a test pins each), and its
example uses a local type rather than the acl/update payload, whose
Nullable member only exists once the prebuilt packages adopt it.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(go): leave a self-encoding T's nil value to T in a trusttasks.Nullable

The nil-to-empty rule chose by kind alone, so it overrode T's own
encoding: Value(json.RawMessage(nil)) wrote [] where RawMessage writes
null, Value([]byte(nil)) wrote [] where an empty []byte writes "", and a
named slice with its own MarshalJSON lost it. Each can make a document
schema-invalid or change what it says.

The rule now applies only to a plain slice or map: not []byte, and with
no MarshalJSON or MarshalText on T or *T. Anything else writes a nil
value as encoding/json writes T. The type doc says so, and a test covers
RawMessage, []byte, and named types encoding through MarshalJSON (on the
value and on the pointer) and MarshalText.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* test(go): show a required nullable member losing its null on marshal

A required member whose schema admits null is generated with omitempty, so
a nil pointer drops the key and the document fails its own schema's
required. vta/contexts/update-did 1.2's did is the case: a null did means
"no DID of its own", and Go writes the member out entirely.

specs/smoke drives the prebuilt package through a marshal and a round trip,
and trust-tasks-gen's test checks the tags the per-module generator emits.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>
(cherry picked from commit f4dae312c4f65dc302871a41d06a74c5cf4bba38)

* fix(go): write a required nullable member's null instead of dropping its key

Both Go generators (scripts/build-go-bindings.mjs for the prebuilt packages,
and trust-tasks-gen for an application's own) tagged a member omitempty when
it was optional or nullable. On a required nullable member, a pointer so that
nil can stand for null, that dropped the key whenever the value was null, and
the document failed its own schema's required.

omitempty now goes exactly on optional members. The field types are
unchanged: a required nullable member is still a pointer.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>
(cherry picked from commit cd1d110b4c7eab3071330296252a102797728cfc)

* fix(go): regenerate the prebuilt packages so required nullable members keep their key

Five fields lose omitempty: did in vta/contexts/update-did 1.1 and 1.2, and
requirementsDigest in vtc/vetting/hidden/{publish,show,withdraw} 0.1. Their
types are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>
(cherry picked from commit c4781081f02c60770ef475c9e007e165ab6a14b0)

* docs(go): describe how generated payload types write a required nullable null

go.md: omitempty goes on optional members only, so a nil required nullable
member writes null; an optional nullable member still folds null into
absent, which is an open decision. runtime-parity.md gains the row for
absent, empty and null payload members, with Go's required-nullable cell
fixed. The specs job's comment now counts the four packages specs/smoke
drives.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>
(cherry picked from commit 87c87801501f3d37f136c4aed6cfde46f2f1a09f)

* test(go): show an optional nullable member losing null against absent

An optional member whose schema admits null has three states: absent,
null and a value. acl/update 0.3 reads an absent label as "leave it
unchanged" and "label": null as "clear it". The generated field is *T
with omitempty, so null and absent both decode to nil and nil writes
neither: a Go client cannot send the clear.

These tests describe the fix: generated-code round trips on acl/update
0.3 and vtc/registry/records/list 0.2 (through specs/smoke, which the
core's smoke driver now copies with those two packages), and the
per-module generator's field types, a trusttasks.Nullable[T] tagged
omitzero. They fail until both generators emit it.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(go)!: generate trusttasks.Nullable for optional members that admit null

Both Go generators (scripts/build-go-bindings.mjs for the prebuilt
packages, trust-tasks-gen for an application's own) gave an optional
member whose schema admits null a *T with omitempty. Null and absent both
decoded to nil, and nil wrote neither, so a Go client could not send
acl/update 0.3's "label": null ("clear the label") as distinct from an
absent label ("leave it unchanged").

Such a member is now a trusttasks.Nullable[T] tagged omitzero: absent,
null and a value each survive a decode and an encode, and the member
compares with == when T does. omitzero needs Go 1.24, the modules' floor;
omitempty never omits a struct. Required nullable members stay *T without
omitempty, every other optional member stays a pointer, and a member
rendered as json.RawMessage is untouched. The prebuilt generator imports
the runtime into a shared package that needs it for this.

This changes the type of every such field: code that reads or writes it
as a pointer no longer compiles.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(go-specs)!: regenerate the prebuilt packages with trusttasks.Nullable

npm run build-go-bindings with the generator change: 263 optional
members whose schema admits null, in 128 files, move from *T with
omitempty to trusttasks.Nullable[T] with omitzero (223 strings, 16
integers, 10 slices, 6 maps, 4 booleans, 4 objects). Nothing else
changes.

The tree needs a core with trusttasks.Nullable, which no published core
has yet; see the next commit for the requirement.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* build(go-specs): require the core release that carries trusttasks.Nullable

The regenerated tree uses trusttasks.Nullable, which the core gains in
the release after v0.13.9: v0.14.0, since the Go 1.24 floor raise
releases the core as a breaking (minor) change. Until that tag exists
this module does not resolve, and the specs job in go.yml fails, so this
change merges only after the core release. Then run
`go get github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go@v0.14.0
&& go mod tidy` here to write go.sum (it still holds v0.13.3's sums) and
check the version the Release PR actually assigned.

Locally the tree builds against this checkout's core through a go.work
outside the repository (GOWORK=/path/to/go.work, using trust-tasks-go and
trust-tasks-go/specs); no replace is committed.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(go): describe trusttasks.Nullable for optional nullable members

go.md's "optional members are pointers" note now says how an optional
member that admits null is generated (a trusttasks.Nullable[T] tagged
omitzero), how to build, read and compare one, and that the specs module
builds with it only once a core carrying the type (v0.14.0) is released,
with a go.work outside the repository until then. The runtime-parity row
moves Go to "yes, kept", and the website's Go library card says the
same.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* test(go-specs): check member names inside a Nullable decision and round-trip acl allowedKeys

Two properties of trusttasks.Nullable on real generated packages. A
vtc/join-requests/list 0.2 response whose decision carries both "code"
and "Code" is refused, through CheckMemberNames and a Document decode, as
the same member behind a pointer is. acl/grant 0.1's allowedKeys keeps
absent, null and [] apart through a round trip, and a nil slice set as a
value writes [], not the null that would grant every key.

The core's smoke driver copies the two packages these import.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(go): state the Nullable exception to optional pointers and its nil-slice rule

docs/packages/go.md's rule 3 and the CLAUDE.md index line now name the
Nullable exception to "optional members are pointers"; the pointer rule
for nullable members applies to required ones only; Value(nil) with a
slice or map writes [] or {}, only Null() writes null; the member-name
check enters a Nullable; and a Nullable belongs only in a struct field
tagged omitzero. runtime-parity.md says the same, and the go.yml comment
on the specs job no longer counts the smoke tests.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(go): name the Nullable exception in the README's absent-is-not-empty section

The section said every optional member is a pointer, and cited acl/grant's
allowedKeys as one. An optional member that admits null is now a
trusttasks.Nullable, acl/grant 0.1's allowedKeys among them.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* build(go-specs): require the core release that carries trusttasks.Nullable, and regenerate over main

- specs/go.sum for core v0.14.0.
- The hcp packages added on main regenerated: optional nullable members are trusttasks.Nullable.
- hcp-demo-go requires core v0.14.0, its internal/tasks is regenerated, and the
  disclosure's language is trusttasks.Value("en").

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: trust-tasks-tsp-v0.42.0
body:
### Added

- **tsp**: The TSP libraries implement binding tsp/0.3, and Rust refuses a TSP draft as UnsupportedTspVersion ([#1393](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1393))

* fix(ts-tsp)!: speak TSP 1.0 on @openvtc/vti-tsp-js 0.4

  @openvtc/trust-tasks-tsp now seals and opens TSP 1.0 (YTSP-BAA, HPKE-Base)
  messages, the version the Rust trust-tasks-tsp crate (affinidi-tsp 0.5), the
  VTA and Keyring speak. It moves @openvtc/vti-tsp-js from ^0.2.0, which spoke
  only the Rev 2 draft, to ^0.4.0.

  For consumers:
  - A peer on a TSP draft (Rev 2 or Rev 3) can no longer exchange messages with
    this package. Its message is refused from the version marker, before sender
    resolution, as a TspEnvelopeError with the new failure kind
    unsupportedTspVersion. TSP has no version negotiation.
  - PackKeys and UnpackKeys (re-exported from vti-tsp-js) no longer take
    senderEncryptionKey: HPKE-Base does not use the sender's X25519 key.
    SenderPublicKeys.encryptionKey stays; it is what a reply is sealed to.
  - New export TSP_VERSION ("1.0").

  Tests open a TSP 1.0 message packed by the Rust affinidi-tsp 0.5.0 and refuse
  a Rev 2 message packed by vti-tsp-js 0.2.0; test/fixtures.ts records how each
  was produced.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.42.0
body:
### Added

- **hcp**: Add the hcp/* specifications, carrying the Human Context Protocol (HCP 2.0-draft-3) as Trust Tasks ([#1380](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1380))

* feat(hcp): carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 query, grant revoke and revocation notice as Trust Tasks

  Add the hcp/* protocol family (SPEC §9.4) with three draft 0.1 specs
  targeting framework 0.6.0, each carrying one Human Context Protocol
  2.0-draft-3 operation:

  - hcp/entries/query: Query (HCP 5.2.1). The HCP access token travels
    opaquely in `accessToken`; the result's `timestamp` is renamed
    `respondedAt`; `categories` gets a framework bound of 256.
  - hcp/grants/revoke: Revoke grant (HCP 6.2, 9.2), destructive and acting
    for the Authorizing Principal, with an empty response for HCP's 204.
  - hcp/grants/revoked: the revocation notice (HCP 6.2.3, 9.9). The SET
    claims map to the envelope, and an empty response carries RFC 8935's
    202. The notice is signed with a provider VID key that the provider's
    JWKS must also publish.

  HCP's invalid-token condition maps to the family code hcp:invalidToken.
  Shared shapes (common, context entry, disclosure, directive) live in
  specs/hcp/_shared/0.1. They were written from the CC BY 4.0 HCP text,
  with attribution, not copied from HCP's schema files. HCP's kebab-case
  enum values are allowlisted as external.



### Fixed

- **rs,build**: Keep absent, empty and null apart in generated payload types ([#1385](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1385))

* test(rs): show generated payload types losing member presence on a round trip

  An optional array decodes [] as absent and re-encodes it absent; an
  optional nullable member decodes null as absent (acl/update 0.3's
  "label: null clears it" becomes "leave it unchanged"); an optional
  {"type": "null"} member is written back as null when absent. The
  trust-tasks-rs tests round-trip acl/show 0.3 and acl/update 0.3; the
  trust-tasks-build tests pin the field shapes on a fixture module. Both
  fail until the generator keeps presence.



### Specifications

- **auth/oob**: DeviceEnrol: a client asks for scoped, long-lived access to a person's VTA, approved from their wallet ([#1386](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1386))

* spec(auth/oob): copy the versions deviceEnrol changes, unchanged

  _shared 0.1 to 0.2, request 0.2 to 0.3, claim 0.2 to 0.3, identify 0.1
  to 0.2, prove 0.3 to 0.4, grant 0.3 to 0.4, respond 0.3 to 0.4 and
  redeem 0.2 to 0.3, copied byte for byte so the next commit shows only
  what the new versions change. The copies still carry their old version
  numbers and $ids; this commit does not build on its own.

- **vtc/directory/query**: 0.2 answers the member's directory entry ([#1383](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1383))

* spec(vtc/directory/query): 0.2 answers the member's directory entry

  A caller that meets a member by their DID (the author of a record in a data
  room, the signer of a document) can read their projection with
  vtc/directory/query, but every other directory read is addressed by entry:
  the member's picture (images/get), their entry with shared groups
  (entries/show), and the card a member surface opens. Without the entry
  identifier such a caller can name the member but not show their picture or
  open their card.

  0.2 = 0.1 + a required `entryId` (directory-card `EntryId`) on every answer,
  never on a notFound or in a refusal's details. The notFound rule is now
  stated normatively: an answer is given only where the projection shows the
  caller the member's DID, to the member themselves, or to an administrator,
  so the identifier links the named DID only to an entry that caller could
  already open; Security & Privacy says so. Targets framework 0.6.0.

  All four libraries regenerated.

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in

- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.
