title: Add a RAHP documentary assessment of the SEDI Implementation Guide
body:
## Purpose

Addresses #71, following the RAHP Task Force decision of 25 November 2026 to examine the Utah State-Endorsed Digital Identity (SEDI) Implementation Guide and Conformance Framework. This pull request provides a worked documentary assessment of an external digital identity design and evaluates the applicability of RAHP beyond the Decentralized Trust Graph (DTG) context.

## Assessment scope and source

The assessment uses a retained contributor-supplied archive of 18 PDFs and three toolkit documents from the [SEDI Implementation Guide](https://sedi.utah.gov/implementation-guide/) and [SEDI toolkit](https://sedi.utah.gov/bring-sedi-to-your-state/#kit). The guide is a working draft interpreting Utah Code Title 63A, Chapter 20. Its source bytes are identified by SHA-256, not by an independently authenticated publisher release. The assessment does not determine legal compliance, certify implementations or establish operational assurance.

## What this pull request delivers

| Assessment component | Coverage |
| --- | ---: |
| Indexed requirements | 142 |
| Detailed documentary examinations | 141 |
| Numbered assessment objectives | 703 |
| Affected participant context groups | 10 |
| Assessment-local risk hypotheses | 31 |
| Constructed scenarios | 47 |
| Selected requirements with explicit objective-control mappings | 7 (32 objectives) |
| Consolidated open review propositions | 12 |

The examination covers physical and digital service equivalence, privacy and surveillance, identity proofing, credential lifecycle, delegated authority, cryptographic and organisational security, actor-specific obligations, and conformance across interacting components. The constructed scenarios examine plausible failure conditions and human harms; they are not reports of observed incidents.

The twelve review propositions distinguish existing design protections, source observations, interpretations, recommendations, proposed treatment authorities and evidence necessary for resolution. They remain open pending accountable review. The selected objective-control mappings are proposed controls and evidence activities, not executed deployment assurance tests.

## Review material

- [Assessment overview](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/blob/f835ef5817fe736710b59bd4b69339a0c995e378/review/examples/sedi/README.md)
- [Consolidated review propositions and recommendations](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/blob/f835ef5817fe736710b59bd4b69339a0c995e378/review/examples/sedi/synthesis.json)
- [Requirement coverage register](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/blob/f835ef5817fe736710b59bd4b69339a0c995e378/review/examples/sedi/requirement-coverage.json) and [coverage conventions](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/blob/f835ef5817fe736710b59bd4b69339a0c995e378/review/examples/sedi/COVERAGE.md)
- [Review handover and reproduction instructions](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/blob/f835ef5817fe736710b59bd4b69339a0c995e378/review/examples/sedi/REVIEW-HANDOVER.md)
- [Acceptance evidence and limitations](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/blob/f835ef5817fe736710b59bd4b69339a0c995e378/review/examples/sedi/ACCEPTANCE-EVIDENCE.md)
- [Retained source manifest](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/blob/f835ef5817fe736710b59bd4b69339a0c995e378/review/examples/sedi/archive-manifest.json)

## Validation and reproducibility

The documented author-side execution verifies all 21 substantive archive members and exercises both the consolidated examination and the bounded service-equivalence candidate. The focused regression suite reports 32 passing tests; strict completeness checks reject incomplete source or analytical metadata. title: feat(examples): add the HCP-over-Trust-Tasks demos in TypeScript, Go, Dart and Rust
body:
### What and why

This PR adds four ports of one demonstration: the Human Context Protocol (HCP 2.0-draft-3 @ `b790561`) run end to
end as Trust Tasks over TSP. It is the first working HCP implementation over Trust Tasks, and it exercises the
`hcp/*` specs added in the suite PR. Three parties run in one process: a toy in-memory HCP Provider, a Context
Client (a booking agent) and a Management Client (the person's app). Each party has its own did:key and TSP keys.
Every document is built with the generated types, signed, and sealed as a TSP message. The receiving end runs
SPEC §7.2 on it: the proof is verified over the document as received and the payload is validated against its
schema before anything acts on it. Nothing touches the network. The keys are demo-only.

The flow:

1. **Discover:** `trust-task-discovery`.
2. **Grant request:** `hcp/grants/request`. The provider holds it with a next step while the person decides; the
   person approves, and the resubmission gets the grant, with a token that lives as long as the grant.
3. **Query:** `hcp/entries/query`, under the grant's token.
4. **Revoke:** `hcp/grants/revoke`.
5. **Query again:** it fails at once with `hcp:invalidToken`.
6. **Revocation notice:** `hcp/grants/revoked`, deduplicated on `noticeId`.
7. **Decline:** a new grant request is held, the person declines, and the resubmission gets the fixed
   `permissionDenied`. No grant is issued.
8. **Expired hold:** a new grant request is held and the person does not decide. Once the hold's lifetime passes, the
   resubmission gets the same `permissionDenied`; a late approval changes nothing, and the thread is never
   reopened. A new request on a new thread is put to the person again.

The tests also cover the carriage rules:

- A token presented from another VID gets `permissionDenied`.
- A resubmission must carry the held payload.
- A resubmission after approval gets the same grant.
- Each reply is checked before it is used.
- The hold's hint is read against its schema, and a hint that fails is ignored.

### What's included

- **The four ports:** `examples/hcp-demo-ts`, `examples/hcp-demo-go`, `examples/hcp-demo-dart` and
  `examples/hcp-demo` (Rust). Each has a README and its own `trust-tasks.lock`, pinning `hcp/entries/query`,
  `hcp/grants/request`, `hcp/grants/revoke` and `hcp/grants/revoked` by digest, with the vendored bundles.
  `examples/hcp-demo-ts/SCENARIO.md` records the scenario and each port's transport differences.
- **One golden transcript,** `examples/hcp-demo-ts/transcript.golden.txt`. Every port's tests compare its run
  with it byte for byte, so the four ports produce the same documents in the same order.
- **The client honours `retryAfter`, read the same way in every port.** Before resubmitting a held grant request,
  each port's client validates the next step's hint, with its own JSON Schema engine, against `NextStepHint` from
  the pinned `hcp/grants/request` schema, and waits, on the demo clock, the `retryAfter` it gives, as
  `hcp/grants/request` asks. A hint that is absent or fails is ignored, never an error, and the client waits a
  default of 5 seconds. The demo provider sends `retryAfter: 1` to keep the run short.
- **The token lives as long as the grant.** Every port's provider sets `tokenExpiresAt` to the grant's `expiresAt`,
  as `hcp/grants/request` now says, so a query late in a four-hour grant does not fail on a one-hour token.
- **The hold ends as the spec says.** A hold is `pending`, then `approved`, `declined` or `expired`. Its lifetime is
  300 seconds, a demo policy counted from the held request's `issuedAt`, and applies only while the person has not
  decided. An ended thread gets the fixed `permissionDenied` and is never reopened. The clock is injected, so the
  hold's lifetime takes no real time.
- **18 tests in every port,** listed in SCENARIO.md. Test 14 registers a second client and has it resubmit on the
  Context Client's held thread: it is refused with `permissionDenied`, and the hold's `issuer` and state are
  unchanged. Tests 15 to 18 are new: 15 reads hints against `NextStepHint` (1 and 3600 are used; none, 2.5, 0,
  "5", 3601, an extra member, `{}` and `null` fall back to 5 seconds); 16 checks that `tokenExpiresAt` equals the
  grant's `expiresAt`; 17 checks the decline (the exact `permissionDenied` payload, the hold `declined`, a late
  approval changing nothing, one grant); 18 checks the expired hold (both refusals exact, the hold `expired`, the new
  thread `pending`, one grant, and a resubmission exactly 300 seconds after the held request still held).
- **TSP version.** Every port speaks TSP 1.0 (`YTSP-BAA`, HPKE-Base, signed) under binding `tsp/0.3`: Rust
  through `affinidi-tsp` 0.5, TypeScript through `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js` 0.4 (via the in-tree `@openvtc/trust-tasks-tsp`,
  since #1387), Go through `affinidi-tsp-go` v0.2.0 and Dart through `affinidi_tsp` 0.2 (no override, since #1388).
  The ports exchange no TSP bytes with each other, so the golden transcript does not depend on the TSP version.
- **After main's generator changes** (#1385, #1378, #1379): the Go demo's `internal/tasks` is regenerated (a
  required nullable member keeps its key), and the Rust demo reads a query's optional `categories` as
  `Option<Vec<_>>`. All four ports pass 18/18 against the golden transcript.
- **CI:** each port runs in its language's example job (`ts.yml`, `go.yml`, `dart.yml`, `rust.yml`), and
  dependabot and the advisories job cover the new dependency manifests. The Rust port is a workspace member,
  excluded from `cargo package`.
- **`npm run check-demo-bundles`,** which runs in `deploy.yml` after `check-bundles`. It checks that each demo
  lock records `https://trusttasks.org` and pins the digests `specs/` builds, and that the vendored bundles match.
  Tests are in `scripts/test-checks/demo-bundles.test.mjs`, and the check is documented in DEVELOPMENT.md.

### Assumptions pending HCP confirmation

The demos follow the `hcp/*` specs and add no assumptions of their own. The ones they rely on are listed in the
suite PR:

- the grant request channel and client identity (21, 22);
- naming the person (23);
- collecting a held outcome, and a hold that ends undecided (39);
- a decline answered with `permissionDenied` (25);
- the revoked-grant error (2);
- the token binding, its required request proof and its error code (22, 53, 49).

The toy provider registers its one client up front. Registering at first approval (question 52) is not
demonstrated. The Management Client still sends its token on revoke; a request with no token from an enrolled
Management Client (question 56) is not demonstrated either.

### Known limitations

- **A demonstration, not a reference provider.** The store is in memory, the keys are fixed, and there is one
  client and one person.
- **Go:** the port generates its task types into `internal/tasks` with `go generate`, and CI fails if they drift
  from the lock. It follows the module rules (no `_` directories, one package per directory).
- **Dart:** the port generates into `lib/trust_tasks` from the lock. Its format check runs at the pubspec's SDK
  floor.
- Any generator presence fixes ship in their own PRs, and the demos do not depend on them.
- `hcp-demo-go` requires `trust-tasks-go` v0.13.3, the version current `main` released, so that `go mod tidy` leaves
  it unchanged. The demo still builds against the local module through its `replace` directives.

### Merge order and stacking

This PR is stacked on the `hcp/*` suite PR (`feat(hcp)`) and needs it merged first; retarget this PR to `main`
after that. It is independent of the uncheckedRules PR (`feat(build)`), and the two can merge in either order.

### Test evidence

All run fresh on this tip, 40a332862, with the `trust-tasks` CLI and every library built from this tree. This
round answers Alberto L's follow-up review (thank you, Alberto): it merges the suite's review-round changes,
re-pins the demos, and adds the token lifetime, the hint check and steps 7 and 8.

- **TypeScript:** the four library packages build. `npm run all` in `hcp-demo-ts` generates, builds, runs the
  demo and passes its tests (18/18).
- **Go:** `go generate` leaves `internal/` unchanged. `gofmt` and `go vet` are clean, `go run .` passes, and
  `go test` passes (18/18).
- **Dart:** `dart pub get` runs, generating from the lock succeeds, and `dart analyze --fatal-infos` is clean on the
  generated code (`lib/trust_tasks/` is git-ignored, so there is no committed output to diff). The format check
  passes, `dart run` passes, and `dart test` passes (18/18).
- **Rust:** `cargo run` and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-example-hcp-demo` pass (18/18).
- **`trust-tasks check`:** passes in all four demo directories.
- **Golden transcript:** regenerated from the TypeScript port for the `retryAfter` wait. The only changes are
  `retryAfter` 5 → 1, every instant from the resubmission on one second later, and the proofs over those
  documents. All four ports match it byte for byte.
- **Locks:** the `hcp/entries/query` pin and vendored bundle were refreshed in all four ports for the review fixes
  (its request proof is now REQUIRED). After the suite's schema-scan fixes (merged in with a merge commit), the
  `hcp/grants/request`, `hcp/entries/query` and `hcp/grants/revoke` pins and bundles are refreshed again in all four
  ports (a requested purpose's `description` is now REQUIRED, and the schema descriptions label the framework
  bounds), with the Go port's `internal/tasks` regenerated to match. Each port's provider now reads the purpose's
  description directly instead of falling back to its code. The golden transcript is unchanged: the demo's request
  already carried a description.
- **After the earlier merges** (the maintainer's corrections, then the suite with `main` ccb265eeb and the
  `clippy::unit_arg` allow): no `hcp/*` schema the demos pin changed, so the locks and the golden transcript were
  unchanged.
- **After this round's suite merge:** the `hcp/entries/query`, `hcp/grants/request` and `hcp/grants/revoke` pins and
  bundles are refreshed in all four ports (`accessToken` is optional on revoke, and the hold hint has a schema);
  `hcp/grants/revoked` is unchanged. The Go port's `internal/tasks` is regenerated, and the Rust and Go revoke
  handlers read the now optional token. The golden transcript changes only where this round meant it to: step 2's
  `tokenExpiresAt` moves from 11:00:06 to 14:00:06, the grant's expiry, with that response's proof, and steps 7
  and 8 are appended. Every other line is unchanged, and all four ports match it byte for byte.
- **Rust demo lint:** `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean and `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-example-hcp-demo
  --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- **Repository checks:** `npm run check-demo-bundles` passes, and `npm run test:checks` passes (85/85).
- **Terminology pass and TSP 1.0** (on 4731d1e57, after merging the suite's terminology commits, 7263be15a): the four
  `hcp/*` pins and bundles are refreshed in all four ports (descriptions and the family error-code meanings only),
  with the Go port's `internal/tasks` regenerated. Step 8 is named an expired hold in every port, as
  `hcp/grants/request` calls it; the golden transcript changes only in that step's label, and all four ports match
  it. The Go demo now requires `affinidi-tsp-go` v0.2.0 and the Dart demo `affinidi_tsp` ^0.2.0 (SDK floor 3.10).
  Re-run: TypeScript 18/18, Go `go vet` clean and 18/18, Dart `dart analyze --fatal-infos` clean, format check at
  3.10 clean and 18/18, Rust 18/18 with clippy `-D warnings` clean; `npm run check`, `check-demo-bundles` and
  `test:checks` (85/85) pass; `trust-tasks check` passes.

### Not changed

`SPEC.md` is untouched. There are no version bumps and no `CHANGELOG.md` entries.

title: feat(examples): add the HCP-over-Trust-Tasks demos in TypeScript, Go, Dart and Rust (#1382)
body:
feat(examples): add the HCP-over-Trust-Tasks demos in TypeScript, Go, Dart and Rust (#1382)

* feat(hcp): carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 query, grant revoke and revocation notice as Trust Tasks

Add the hcp/* protocol family (SPEC §9.4) with three draft 0.1 specs
targeting framework 0.6.0, each carrying one Human Context Protocol
2.0-draft-3 operation:

- hcp/entries/query: Query (HCP 5.2.1). The HCP access token travels
  opaquely in `accessToken`; the result's `timestamp` is renamed
  `respondedAt`; `categories` gets a framework bound of 256.
- hcp/grants/revoke: Revoke grant (HCP 6.2, 9.2), destructive and acting
  for the Authorizing Principal, with an empty response for HCP's 204.
- hcp/grants/revoked: the revocation notice (HCP 6.2.3, 9.9). The SET
  claims map to the envelope, and an empty response carries RFC 8935's
  202. The notice is signed with a provider VID key that the provider's
  JWKS must also publish.

HCP's invalid-token condition maps to the family code hcp:invalidToken.
Shared shapes (common, context entry, disclosure, directive) live in
specs/hcp/_shared/0.1. They were written from the CC BY 4.0 HCP text,
with attribution, not copied from HCP's schema files. HCP's kebab-case
enum values are allowlisted as external.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(hcp): name hcp/* owners in CODEOWNERS and cite the family as a carries example

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for hcp/*

Generated by trust-tasks-codegen (plus cargo fmt), build-ts-bindings, build-go-bindings and build-dart-bindings. Adds the hcp Cargo feature.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): match the hcp/_shared and query schemas to HCP 2.0-draft-3

Checked member by member against HCP 2.0-draft-3 (schemas/2.0-draft-3 and the
specification text, b790561):

- Directive: directiveId, action, effect, text, setBy and createdAt are
  required (HCP 6.4).
- Disclosure: version, content, assertion, classification, standing and
  useUntil are required, and id, subject, record and schema are refused
  (HCP 7.4); provenance on request carries no identifiers (HCP 7.4.1).
- Entry: type is an array, schema is the HCP entry URI, content names its
  profile, record carries version and provenance (HCP 4.2).
- Minimization report requires method (HCP 7.5); the query response example
  uses a registered method and carries version and standing.
- Query request: categories has no minItems and purposeDescription no
  minLength, as in HCP 5.2.1.

The rules HCP states with if/then/else or contains (General Context value,
VC Evidence content, confidence only for model-inferred assertions, one
content evidence item, ContextEntry in type, credential shape, proposal only on
contradicts) are written into the descriptions instead: the Rust generator
(typify) supports neither keyword.

Allowlists the HCP enum values the casing lint flags, and HCP's evidence
verification.at member for the wire-conventions lint. Adds invalid-example
fixtures for each corrected rule a validator can check.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): correct the hcp/* spec prose against HCP 2.0-draft-3

- Drop claims HCP does not make: that query text is as sensitive as content
  or is not logged (HCP 8.2 has no member for it), and that a Management
  Client token cannot query (HCP 5.1, 5.2.1, 7.4).
- Directives are present in every result to a Context Client (HCP 6.4), and
  only a client that claims to follow them must.
- Give the full nine-error table of HCP 5.5, including idempotency-conflict,
  version-conflict and credential-invalid, and scope-denied's "the entry does
  not exist"; quote invalid-token's own condition and say that reading a
  revoked grant's evidence as invalid is this specification's reading (6.2.2).
- Revoke: a delegate revokes within the delegation's scope (HCP 17.5); a
  Context Client token on the same HTTP DELETE relinquishes (HCP 9.4.6); notice
  goes only to a client holding disclosed entries with an endpoint (6.2.2).
- Revoked: the client stops using its copies and passes none on, with the
  legal-obligation exemption (HCP 6.2.2, 6.2.5); HCP does not require
  deletion. "5 attempts" (HCP 9.9), asymmetric signing, and the iat-versus-
  retry tension and delegation-end case flagged as open questions.
- Citations: relevance ordering is 7.3, the method is declared in discovery
  (19.3), cryptosuites per 14.5.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for hcp/*

Generated by trust-tasks-codegen (plus cargo fmt), build-ts-bindings, build-go-bindings and build-dart-bindings from the corrected hcp/_shared and hcp/entries/query schemas.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): take the approved working assumptions, each marked pending HCP confirmation

Each hcp/* spec gains a 'Pending HCP confirmation' section that lists, by the
number of the question put to the HCP editors, the reading it takes where HCP
2.0-draft-3 is silent, and every sentence that relies on one links to it.

- A request under a revoked grant gets hcp:invalidToken (question 1).
- hcp/grants/revoke: revoking an already-revoked grant succeeds idempotently
  with the empty response; an unknown grantId, or one the caller cannot see,
  gets permissionDenied with the same text (question 2).
- hcp/grants/revoked: every delivery attempt reuses the id but carries a fresh
  issuedAt and proof, a declared departure from HCP 9.9; a client that already
  accepted the notice answers idConflict (SPEC 7.2 item 11), which the
  provider records as the acknowledgement (question 3).
- hcp/grants/revoked: an optional reason (revoked | delegation-ended) announces
  a grant ended with its delegation, with revokedAt the instant it ended
  (HCP 17.6, question 4); delegation-ended is allowlisted as an HCP value.
- A Management Client may query and receive whole entries (question 5); a
  re-delivered query causes no second context.read event (question 6).
- Providers do not claim the carriage in conformsTo and advertise it through
  trust-task-discovery (question 7).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for hcp/grants/revoked reason

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): send each hcp/grants/revoked delivery attempt as a fresh document with a stable noticeId

Replace the retry rule for hcp/grants/revoked 0.1 (question 3, still pending
HCP confirmation). Each delivery attempt is now a fresh Trust Task document
with a new id, issuedAt and proof, so the framework's duplicate-execution and
idConflict rules (SPEC 7.2 item 11, 8.4) apply normally and HCP's 300 s
freshness check applies to each attempt's issuedAt.

- Add the required payload member noticeId (a urn:uuid), carrying the SET's
  jti (HCP 9.9): minted per notice and the same on every attempt.
- The client deduplicates on noticeId and answers a repeat with the normal
  empty acknowledgement without acting twice; the provider treats that
  acknowledgement as delivery success (HCP 6.2.3).
- Drop the reading of idConflict as an acknowledgement.
- Field mapping: jti becomes noticeId; HCP's same token on every attempt
  becomes a fresh document per attempt with a stable noticeId.
- Examples carry noticeId, with a new later-attempt example; invalid fixtures
  for a missing and a malformed noticeId.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for hcp/grants/revoked noticeId

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP 2.0-draft-3 context plane as Trust Tasks

Adds hcp/entries/{get,create,revise,withdraw}, hcp/grants/{read-own,relinquish}
and hcp/shares/report at 0.1 (draft, framework 0.6.0), each carrying the HCP
Core context operation of the same name (HCP 5.2.2 to 5.2.8), with valid
examples and invalid fixtures. Adds the shared grant and entry-write schemas,
written from the HCP text with attribution, and bounds two request-reachable
arrays in the shared entry schema.

Maps version-conflict and credential-invalid to hcp:versionConflict and
hcp:credentialInvalid, and HCP's idempotency key to the document id. Points
HCP leaves open are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions C1 to C7).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): add the shared HCP governance objects (standing rule, delegation, audit event, export, grant)

New hcp/_shared/0.1 schemas written from HCP 2.0-draft-3 (6.1.5, 6.3, 8.2, 5.4.1, 17.2). grant.schema.json is the phase-2 draft, needed by hcp/grants/list. Directive arrays gain a maxItems framework bound, now that hcp/import makes them request-side. HCP's kebab-case values and its verbatim timestamp/at members are allowlisted, attributed to HCP.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP standing-rule and directive operations (list, set, remove)

hcp/rules/{list,set,remove} and hcp/directives/{list,set,remove} 0.1 carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 6.3, 6.4, 9.4.14 and 9.4.15. Open points are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions 7, 13, 14, 26).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP entry governance operations (hard delete, confirm or reject, change categories, restrict purposes)

hcp/entries/{hard-delete,confirm,set-categories,restrict-purposes} 0.1 carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 5.4.2, 3.8, 4.7.3, 4.2.1, 4.2.6, 9.4.5, 9.4.9 and 9.4.10, with hcp:versionConflict for expectedVersion. Open points are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions 7, 16, 20).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP audit log, disclosure summary and delegation operations

hcp/audit/read, hcp/disclosures/summary, hcp/delegations/{list,end} 0.1 carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 8.3, 8.6, 9.4.7, 9.4.12, 9.4.13, 9.5 and 17. Open points are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions 4, 7, 13, 14, 15, 21, 22, 25).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP export, import and list grants operations

hcp/export, hcp/import and hcp/grants/list 0.1 carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 5.4.1, 5.4.3, 6.1.5, 9.4.6, 9.4.8 and 9.4.11. Export and import are bounded at the registry's 16 MiB document ceiling, with hcp:exportTooLarge. Open points are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions 7, 14, 17, 23, 24).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): add hcp/grants/request 0.1, a Trust-Task grant request held with a next step while the person decides

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): answer a Context Client's hcp/grants/list with its own grant only, as HCP 9.4.6 does over HTTP

A Context Client presenting its own token is listed only the grant under
which that token was issued, with authorizingPrincipal.delegation withheld
(HCP 17.4), instead of being refused with permissionDenied. Marked pending
HCP confirmation.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): mark the delegate confirmation and purpose-removal readings pending HCP confirmation

hcp/entries/confirm reads HCP 17.4 as letting a delegate confirm or reject
an entry within the delegation's scope, where HCP 3.8 names the Context
Subject; hcp/entries/restrict-purposes returns the entry without
classification.permittedPurposes once the narrowing is removed. Both were
stated without a mark; each now carries one and a Pending HCP
confirmation entry, beside the hcp/grants/list Context Client reading.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): cite the renumbered list of questions for the HCP editors

The questions put to the HCP editors are now one list, 1 to 36, grouped by
specification. Every pending HCP confirmation reference in the hcp/* specs
and schemas cites the new numbers, and each Pending HCP confirmation
section lists them in order. Phase 2's lettered questions take numbers, and
the rules and directives list descriptions no longer cite the duplicate 23.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for the hcp/* suite

Generated by trust-tasks-codegen (plus cargo fmt), build-ts-bindings,
build-go-bindings and build-dart-bindings, once, for the context plane,
the governance plane, hcp/grants/request and the fixes on top of them. The
new specs fall under the existing hcp Cargo feature.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): mark the carriage of governance operations outside the HTTP Binding pending HCP confirmation

HCP 2.0-draft-3 carries governance operations only over its HTTP Binding
(1.6, 5.4, 9.1, 10.1). The 18 governance specs now say so in Conformance
and Authorization and under "What HCP requires that a document cannot

title: feat(build): declare the rules a payload schema does not check (uncheckedRules) and check the declarations
body:
### What and why

Some rules cannot be written in a payload schema in a form every library generator accepts. The Rust generator
(typify) rejects `if`/`then`/`else` and `contains`. A rule like "an entry's `type` includes `ContextEntry`", or
"exactly one of `ref` and `entryId`", therefore lives in a member's `description` and in the prose, where a document
can break it and still validate. The first HCP implementation over Trust Tasks (the `hcp/*` family, carrying HCP
2.0-draft-3 @ `b790561`) has many such rules, which come from HCP's own JSON Schemas.

This PR adds an OPTIONAL `uncheckedRules` front-matter field. Each entry gives a JSON Pointer `member` into
`payload.schema.json`, the `rule`, and its `source`. The `hcp/*` specs use it to list, in one place, every rule
their schemas state but do not check.

It also widens the HCP drift check from the suite PR, after Alberto L's review found 64 differences from HCP's own
schemas that the member-by-member comparison could not see: bounds, patterns, formats and closed objects. A second,
independently written mode now compares those, every difference made on purpose is documented with its reason, and
both modes run in CI.

### What's included

- **The field:** `uncheckedRules` in `specs/spec.meta.schema.json`, documented in CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md and
  DEVELOPMENT.md.
- **Pointer check:** `build-registry.mjs`, through `scripts/lib/unchecked-rules.mjs`, fails the build on a `member`
  that does not resolve to a schema. The pointer follows `$ref`, including into `_shared/` schemas. A map of
  schemas, an array or a keyword value is rejected, so the list cannot drift from a restructured schema.
- **Cross-check:** every `description` reachable from a payload schema that says "not checked by the schema" or
  "a validator does not check it/them" must have an entry at or under it. The build fails otherwise and names the
  pointer to declare. The tree passes with no exemptions.
- **Declarations:** 114 rules across 16 `hcp/*` specs, with `hcp/entries/query/0.1` as the worked example. They
  include the standing-rule rule (`operators`, `requires`, or both, HCP 6.3) wherever the shared `StandingRule`
  is reached, and the `ext["vnd.trusttasks.hcp-carriage"]` member on the `hcp/import` response.
- **Tests** in `scripts/test-checks/unchecked-rules.test.mjs`: `$ref` cycles and the hop limit, a missing
  `$anchor`, malformed JSON, container pointers, the cross-check, and the `build-registry.mjs` wiring.
- **The drift check's second mode:** `npm run check-hcp-drift -- --hcp <hcp-spec checkout> [--mode
  members|constraints]`, both modes by default. The constraints mode (`scripts/lib/hcp-drift-constraints.mjs`) has
  its own walker and `$ref` resolution and shares only the mapping file with the members mode, as DEVELOPMENT.md
  asks of the checks. Over the same map it compares bounds (`minLength`, `maxItems`, `minimum` and the rest),
  `pattern`s, `format`s, closed objects (`additionalProperties` or `unevaluatedProperties: false` on one side only)
  and unions (a choice of scalar shapes on one side, one merged shape on the other). 13 fixture tests are in
  `scripts/test-checks/hcp-drift-constraints.test.mjs`.
- **Its allowlist,** `scripts/lib/hcp-drift-constraints-allowlist.json`: 104 entries and 2 pattern pairs that accept
  the same strings, each with a reason and a `ref` to the spec's field mapping or the editors' question. A stale
  entry fails. Alberto's 64 are all accounted for:
  - 56 non-empty bounds: 54 are documented one by one (what the member names, why an empty value names nothing,
    and the field mapping's "Where this payload is stricter" paragraph). The other 2 no longer exist, because
    `hcp/import` now keeps only HCP's constraints. The mode also found 10 more documented non-empty bounds and 10
    that HCP's own pattern, enum or `contains` already makes redundant; each has its own entry.
  - 4 merged unions (`Category`, `Directive.action`, `hcp/directives/set`'s action, `Delegation.relationship`), and
    the 3 copies inside `hcp/import`'s export.
  - 2 dropped formats: `hcp/import`'s audit `purpose` is documented (the imported shape keeps only HCP's
    constraints, question 42), and the shared `AuditEvent.purpose` now carries `format: uri` in the suite, so it is
    no longer a difference.
  - 2 closed request roots (`hcp/entries/create`, `revise`), documented with the field mapping's wording, as are
    the other 14 closed roots.

  Size caps the carriage adds where HCP sets none, and `hcp/import`'s 16 MiB document bounds, are documented as
  classes, so a cap HCP does set, or a looser one, is still reported.
- **The CI job** "hcp/* schemas match HCP's" in `checks.yml` runs both modes on every change, unfiltered. It takes a
  blobless clone of `loyalagents/hcp-spec` and reads HCP's schemas at the commit the specs' `carries.reference`
  pins, so a change to HCP's head cannot turn it red; a change here is a change to our schemas, the map or the
  allowlists. Action SHAs are pinned. DEVELOPMENT.md's CI-check table and CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md describe it.

### Known limitations

- **Source-only for now.** The registry data does not emit the field and the site does not render it. The library
  validators do not surface these rules yet; a consumer that needs one enforced checks it itself.
- **The cross-check sees only marked rules.** A rule stated without a marker phrase passes unnoticed, and so does
  a second rule in a description that already has an entry.
- **Shared-schema rules are declared again by each spec that reaches them.** An inherited `x-uncheckedRules`
  keyword would remove the copies, but it needs every generator to strip it first. That is future work.
- **What the drift check cannot see.** HCP's conditionals (`if`/`then`/`else`, `not`, `contains`); the operations
  HCP describes only in prose; whether two different patterns accept the same strings, beyond the listed pairs;
  constraints inside a union whose two sides differ in shape; a newer HCP commit, until `carries.reference` moves;
  and whether a member means what HCP's does.
- **Generated libraries are unchanged.** The PR changes `spec.md` front matter, the build scripts, CI and docs, and
  no payload schema. None of the four generators reads the field, so no regeneration is needed.

### Pending HCP confirmation

The rules declared here are HCP's own, cited by section. The working assumptions behind the `hcp/*` family are
listed in the `hcp/*` suite PR and in each spec's `## Pending HCP confirmation` section. This PR adds none.

### Merge order and stacking

This PR is stacked on the `hcp/*` suite PR (`feat(hcp)`) and needs it merged first; retarget this PR to `main`
after that. It is independent of the demos PR (`feat(examples)`), and the two can merge in either order.

### Test evidence

All run fresh on this tip, which merges the suite's review fixes (the request proof on every token-carrying
request, the export bound) and then its schema-scan fixes (`hcp/import` taking any HCP-valid export, the required
purpose description, the framework-bound notes), each with a merge commit, not a rebase. The `hcp/import` entries
for the export's rules and delegations now resolve to its local `ImportedStandingRule` and `ImportedDelegation`, and
still state the same HCP rules. The tip then merges the maintainer's corrections on this branch (among them the
`hcp/entries/query` entry for the rule that a request names exactly one of `ref` and `entryId`) and the suite again,
which brings `main` ccb265eeb (the 0.31.9 release and the `vtc/rooms/community` specs) and the `clippy::unit_arg`
allow. This round, answering Alberto L's follow-up review (thank you, Alberto), adds the drift check's second mode,
its allowlist and the CI job, then merges the suite again with its review-round changes (among them `format: uri`
on the audit event's purpose and the optional `accessToken`). After that merge the shared audit purpose's
non-empty bound, which the suite gave it with `PurposeCode`'s shape, is documented too: HCP's pattern already
refuses an empty value, so it narrows nothing.

- `npm run validate`: pass. 115 rules declared by 16 specs, and the pointer check and cross-check are clean.
- The TypeScript and Dart API compatibility checks pass against the published 0.31.9 (TypeScript: additions
  only, nothing removed or changed; Dart: no breaking change).
- `npm run build`, `npm run check`: pass.
- `npm run test:checks`: 104/104.
- `npm run check-hcp-drift`, both modes, at the pinned HCP commit: members 39 differences, all allowlisted;
  constraints 283 differences, all allowlisted; 0 stale entries. Also run against a fresh blobless clone, as the
  CI job does.
- Negative check (run before the merge; the merge changes no `uncheckedRules` entry): removing the `hcp/rules/list` entry makes the build fail, naming
  `/$defs/Response/properties/rules/items`. The cross-check therefore reaches the marker in the shared
  `StandingRule` description.
- After merging the suite's terminology pass (29b5d8e60), 53f2ed8a3 names HCP's General Context and VC Evidence
  Profiles as HCP does in the `rule` texts (no rule added, removed or moved) and the Authorizing Principal in one
  constraint-allowlist reason. Re-run on 53f2ed8a3: `npm run check` passes, `npm run test:checks` 104/104, and both
  drift modes give the same counts as above.

### Not changed

`SPEC.md` is untouched. There are no version bumps and no `CHANGELOG.md` entries.

title: feat(build): declare the rules a payload schema does not check (uncheckedRules) and check the declarations (#1381)
body:
feat(build): declare the rules a payload schema does not check (uncheckedRules) and check the declarations (#1381)

* feat(hcp): carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 query, grant revoke and revocation notice as Trust Tasks

Add the hcp/* protocol family (SPEC §9.4) with three draft 0.1 specs
targeting framework 0.6.0, each carrying one Human Context Protocol
2.0-draft-3 operation:

- hcp/entries/query: Query (HCP 5.2.1). The HCP access token travels
  opaquely in `accessToken`; the result's `timestamp` is renamed
  `respondedAt`; `categories` gets a framework bound of 256.
- hcp/grants/revoke: Revoke grant (HCP 6.2, 9.2), destructive and acting
  for the Authorizing Principal, with an empty response for HCP's 204.
- hcp/grants/revoked: the revocation notice (HCP 6.2.3, 9.9). The SET
  claims map to the envelope, and an empty response carries RFC 8935's
  202. The notice is signed with a provider VID key that the provider's
  JWKS must also publish.

HCP's invalid-token condition maps to the family code hcp:invalidToken.
Shared shapes (common, context entry, disclosure, directive) live in
specs/hcp/_shared/0.1. They were written from the CC BY 4.0 HCP text,
with attribution, not copied from HCP's schema files. HCP's kebab-case
enum values are allowlisted as external.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(hcp): name hcp/* owners in CODEOWNERS and cite the family as a carries example

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for hcp/*

Generated by trust-tasks-codegen (plus cargo fmt), build-ts-bindings, build-go-bindings and build-dart-bindings. Adds the hcp Cargo feature.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): match the hcp/_shared and query schemas to HCP 2.0-draft-3

Checked member by member against HCP 2.0-draft-3 (schemas/2.0-draft-3 and the
specification text, b790561):

- Directive: directiveId, action, effect, text, setBy and createdAt are
  required (HCP 6.4).
- Disclosure: version, content, assertion, classification, standing and
  useUntil are required, and id, subject, record and schema are refused
  (HCP 7.4); provenance on request carries no identifiers (HCP 7.4.1).
- Entry: type is an array, schema is the HCP entry URI, content names its
  profile, record carries version and provenance (HCP 4.2).
- Minimization report requires method (HCP 7.5); the query response example
  uses a registered method and carries version and standing.
- Query request: categories has no minItems and purposeDescription no
  minLength, as in HCP 5.2.1.

The rules HCP states with if/then/else or contains (General Context value,
VC Evidence content, confidence only for model-inferred assertions, one
content evidence item, ContextEntry in type, credential shape, proposal only on
contradicts) are written into the descriptions instead: the Rust generator
(typify) supports neither keyword.

Allowlists the HCP enum values the casing lint flags, and HCP's evidence
verification.at member for the wire-conventions lint. Adds invalid-example
fixtures for each corrected rule a validator can check.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): correct the hcp/* spec prose against HCP 2.0-draft-3

- Drop claims HCP does not make: that query text is as sensitive as content
  or is not logged (HCP 8.2 has no member for it), and that a Management
  Client token cannot query (HCP 5.1, 5.2.1, 7.4).
- Directives are present in every result to a Context Client (HCP 6.4), and
  only a client that claims to follow them must.
- Give the full nine-error table of HCP 5.5, including idempotency-conflict,
  version-conflict and credential-invalid, and scope-denied's "the entry does
  not exist"; quote invalid-token's own condition and say that reading a
  revoked grant's evidence as invalid is this specification's reading (6.2.2).
- Revoke: a delegate revokes within the delegation's scope (HCP 17.5); a
  Context Client token on the same HTTP DELETE relinquishes (HCP 9.4.6); notice
  goes only to a client holding disclosed entries with an endpoint (6.2.2).
- Revoked: the client stops using its copies and passes none on, with the
  legal-obligation exemption (HCP 6.2.2, 6.2.5); HCP does not require
  deletion. "5 attempts" (HCP 9.9), asymmetric signing, and the iat-versus-
  retry tension and delegation-end case flagged as open questions.
- Citations: relevance ordering is 7.3, the method is declared in discovery
  (19.3), cryptosuites per 14.5.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for hcp/*

Generated by trust-tasks-codegen (plus cargo fmt), build-ts-bindings, build-go-bindings and build-dart-bindings from the corrected hcp/_shared and hcp/entries/query schemas.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): take the approved working assumptions, each marked pending HCP confirmation

Each hcp/* spec gains a 'Pending HCP confirmation' section that lists, by the
number of the question put to the HCP editors, the reading it takes where HCP
2.0-draft-3 is silent, and every sentence that relies on one links to it.

- A request under a revoked grant gets hcp:invalidToken (question 1).
- hcp/grants/revoke: revoking an already-revoked grant succeeds idempotently
  with the empty response; an unknown grantId, or one the caller cannot see,
  gets permissionDenied with the same text (question 2).
- hcp/grants/revoked: every delivery attempt reuses the id but carries a fresh
  issuedAt and proof, a declared departure from HCP 9.9; a client that already
  accepted the notice answers idConflict (SPEC 7.2 item 11), which the
  provider records as the acknowledgement (question 3).
- hcp/grants/revoked: an optional reason (revoked | delegation-ended) announces
  a grant ended with its delegation, with revokedAt the instant it ended
  (HCP 17.6, question 4); delegation-ended is allowlisted as an HCP value.
- A Management Client may query and receive whole entries (question 5); a
  re-delivered query causes no second context.read event (question 6).
- Providers do not claim the carriage in conformsTo and advertise it through
  trust-task-discovery (question 7).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for hcp/grants/revoked reason

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): send each hcp/grants/revoked delivery attempt as a fresh document with a stable noticeId

Replace the retry rule for hcp/grants/revoked 0.1 (question 3, still pending
HCP confirmation). Each delivery attempt is now a fresh Trust Task document
with a new id, issuedAt and proof, so the framework's duplicate-execution and
idConflict rules (SPEC 7.2 item 11, 8.4) apply normally and HCP's 300 s
freshness check applies to each attempt's issuedAt.

- Add the required payload member noticeId (a urn:uuid), carrying the SET's
  jti (HCP 9.9): minted per notice and the same on every attempt.
- The client deduplicates on noticeId and answers a repeat with the normal
  empty acknowledgement without acting twice; the provider treats that
  acknowledgement as delivery success (HCP 6.2.3).
- Drop the reading of idConflict as an acknowledgement.
- Field mapping: jti becomes noticeId; HCP's same token on every attempt
  becomes a fresh document per attempt with a stable noticeId.
- Examples carry noticeId, with a new later-attempt example; invalid fixtures
  for a missing and a malformed noticeId.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for hcp/grants/revoked noticeId

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP 2.0-draft-3 context plane as Trust Tasks

Adds hcp/entries/{get,create,revise,withdraw}, hcp/grants/{read-own,relinquish}
and hcp/shares/report at 0.1 (draft, framework 0.6.0), each carrying the HCP
Core context operation of the same name (HCP 5.2.2 to 5.2.8), with valid
examples and invalid fixtures. Adds the shared grant and entry-write schemas,
written from the HCP text with attribution, and bounds two request-reachable
arrays in the shared entry schema.

Maps version-conflict and credential-invalid to hcp:versionConflict and
hcp:credentialInvalid, and HCP's idempotency key to the document id. Points
HCP leaves open are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions C1 to C7).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): add the shared HCP governance objects (standing rule, delegation, audit event, export, grant)

New hcp/_shared/0.1 schemas written from HCP 2.0-draft-3 (6.1.5, 6.3, 8.2, 5.4.1, 17.2). grant.schema.json is the phase-2 draft, needed by hcp/grants/list. Directive arrays gain a maxItems framework bound, now that hcp/import makes them request-side. HCP's kebab-case values and its verbatim timestamp/at members are allowlisted, attributed to HCP.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP standing-rule and directive operations (list, set, remove)

hcp/rules/{list,set,remove} and hcp/directives/{list,set,remove} 0.1 carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 6.3, 6.4, 9.4.14 and 9.4.15. Open points are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions 7, 13, 14, 26).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP entry governance operations (hard delete, confirm or reject, change categories, restrict purposes)

hcp/entries/{hard-delete,confirm,set-categories,restrict-purposes} 0.1 carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 5.4.2, 3.8, 4.7.3, 4.2.1, 4.2.6, 9.4.5, 9.4.9 and 9.4.10, with hcp:versionConflict for expectedVersion. Open points are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions 7, 16, 20).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP audit log, disclosure summary and delegation operations

hcp/audit/read, hcp/disclosures/summary, hcp/delegations/{list,end} 0.1 carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 8.3, 8.6, 9.4.7, 9.4.12, 9.4.13, 9.5 and 17. Open points are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions 4, 7, 13, 14, 15, 21, 22, 25).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP export, import and list grants operations

hcp/export, hcp/import and hcp/grants/list 0.1 carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 5.4.1, 5.4.3, 6.1.5, 9.4.6, 9.4.8 and 9.4.11. Export and import are bounded at the registry's 16 MiB document ceiling, with hcp:exportTooLarge. Open points are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions 7, 14, 17, 23, 24).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): add hcp/grants/request 0.1, a Trust-Task grant request held with a next step while the person decides

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): answer a Context Client's hcp/grants/list with its own grant only, as HCP 9.4.6 does over HTTP

A Context Client presenting its own token is listed only the grant under
which that token was issued, with authorizingPrincipal.delegation withheld
(HCP 17.4), instead of being refused with permissionDenied. Marked pending
HCP confirmation.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): mark the delegate confirmation and purpose-removal readings pending HCP confirmation

hcp/entries/confirm reads HCP 17.4 as letting a delegate confirm or reject
an entry within the delegation's scope, where HCP 3.8 names the Context
Subject; hcp/entries/restrict-purposes returns the entry without
classification.permittedPurposes once the narrowing is removed. Both were
stated without a mark; each now carries one and a Pending HCP
confirmation entry, beside the hcp/grants/list Context Client reading.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): cite the renumbered list of questions for the HCP editors

The questions put to the HCP editors are now one list, 1 to 36, grouped by
specification. Every pending HCP confirmation reference in the hcp/* specs
and schemas cites the new numbers, and each Pending HCP confirmation
section lists them in order. Phase 2's lettered questions take numbers, and
the rules and directives list descriptions no longer cite the duplicate 23.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for the hcp/* suite

Generated by trust-tasks-codegen (plus cargo fmt), build-ts-bindings,
build-go-bindings and build-dart-bindings, once, for the context plane,
the governance plane, hcp/grants/request and the fixes on top of them. The
new specs fall under the existing hcp Cargo feature.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): mark the carriage of governance operations outside the HTTP Binding pending HCP confirmation

HCP 2.0-draft-3 carries governance operations only over its HTTP Binding
(1.6, 5.4, 9.1, 10.1). The 18 governance specs now say so in Conformance
and Authorization and under "What HCP requires that a document cannot
express", take the reading that another carriage may carry them for a
Management Client acting for the Authorizing Principal (6.1.9), and mark
it pending HCP confirmation (question 37). Each Question 1 bullet points
to question 37, since the binding identifier it asks for is the same
question.

Review finding B1.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): give every Management Client read one front-matter profile

Every Management Client read now declares actsAsSubject false, since a
read produces no attributable effect in the person's name (SPEC 7.3
item 14); a request proof REQUIRED where the response discloses a
secret (export, audit/read, delegations/list, disclosures/summary) and
RECOMMENDED where it discloses metadata (grants/list, rules/list,
directives/list); and grants/read-own takes the transient retention
class of grants/list, since the provider records nothing for either
read. The rationales and the Authorization prose follow, the export
request example gains its now-required proof, and CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md
states the profile once.

Review finding I4.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): keep the access token out of retained documents and bind it to the issuer VID

Every hcp/* spec whose document carries accessToken gains one shared
"The access token" paragraph under Security & Privacy: the token MUST
travel only to the provider, a recipient MUST NOT log it or retain it
beyond the exchange, and a duplicate-execution or evidentiary record
keeps the document with the token removed, or a digest of it. Where the
request carries a proof, the provider MUST refuse with permissionDenied
a token issued to a client other than the one the issuer VID
identifies, a strengthening HCP does not itself require, marked pending
HCP confirmation (question 22) with a Question 22 bullet in each spec.
grants/request states the same for the token its response carries.

The Authorization sections replace the issuer-binding SHOULD with that
rule, the signed-request retention sentences keep the request with the
token removed, each durable retention rationale says the token is not
retained, and entries/query's lower-case "must travel only to the
provider" becomes BCP 14.

Review finding I5.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): name the Context Client as the party of grants/read-own and grants/relinquish

Both tasks refuse a Management Client's token, so the party that sends
them is a Context Client, not any HCP Client. The summary, the parties
front matter, the abstract and the Parties table say so, and the table
notes that HCP 5.2.6 and 5.2.7 say HCP Client.

Review finding N7.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): require operators or requires on a standing rule

HCP 6.3 and 9.4.14 require a standing rule to carry operators, requires, or both, and HCP's standing-rule.json states it as an anyOf of two required clauses. Add that anyOf to the hcp/rules/set request and to the shared StandingRule, remove the text that called the rule unchecked, and add invalid fixtures with neither member for the rules/set request, a rules/list listed rule and an export's rules.

Review finding I3.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): allow an empty permittedPurposes list in restrict-purposes

HCP 4.2.6 defines an empty classification.permittedPurposes: an entry may be disclosed for a purpose only where each list present includes it, so [] permits no purpose. HCP's common.json sets no minItems. Drop the minItems of 1, correct the prose and the member description, remove the invalid fixture for the empty list and add a spec example that sends one.

Review finding I7.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): align the entry response bounds, citations and wording of the entry governance tasks

Raise the response bound of hcp/entries/confirm, set-categories and restrict-purposes from 256 KiB to 512 KiB, the bound of create, revise and get, so an entry those tasks carry can also be confirmed, recategorised or restricted. Raise hcp/entries/query's response bound from 2 MiB to 12 MiB, so that 20 disclosures (HCP 7.2) each within get's bound always fit, with 2 MiB for directives, the minimization report, envelope and proof; it stays within the 16 MiB ceiling, and needs no rule for returning fewer entries.

Cite HCP 9.4.2, which says a Management Client names an entry by its id, instead of 9.4.5, and say "Context Subject" where HCP 5.4 does for whom the Management Client showed expectedVersion.

Review findings I11 (entries part), N1, N2.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): name a Management Client as a party of hcp/entries/query

Question 5 lets a Management Client query, but the parties listed only a Context Client. Use the wording of hcp/entries/get and withdraw in the front matter and the Parties table.

Review finding M1.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): cite get's refusal of a missing version as a reading of HCP's existence hiding

HCP 5.2.2 does not itself say that a version that does not exist is refused as not authorized. State the refusal as this specification's reading of the existence hiding of HCP 5.2.2 and 5.5, explain why version-conflict (a write naming a non-current version) does not arise, and say it where the request describes version.

Review finding M2.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): map hard-delete's idempotency key to the document id

HCP 9.6 asks a provider to accept an Idempotency-Key on DELETE /v2/entries/{entryId}, the path a hard deletion takes with hardDelete=true (HCP 9.4.5). Treat the document id as that key, as hcp/entries/withdraw does: add the field-mapping row, map idempotency-conflict to idConflict, and state the 24-hour retention of HCP 9.6.

Review finding M3.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): require withdraw to keep its duplicate-execution record for 24 hours

HCP 9.6 requires an idempotency key and its response to be kept for at least 24 hours. State it for hcp/entries/withdraw as create and revise do.

Review finding M4.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): make the hcp/grants/revoked events-wrapper fixture fail for one reason only

The fixture lacked noticeId, grantId and revokedAt as well as carrying the SET events wrapper. It now carries all three, so only the wrapper makes it invalid.

Review finding M14.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): bound hcp/grants/revoked delivery at 24 hours and keep noticeId records for 25

The client was told to keep a processed noticeId for the provider's whole retry period, which it cannot know. A provider now makes no delivery attempt more than 24 hours after the first (a carriage bound; HCP sets only the minimum), and a client keeps each processed noticeId for at least 25 hours.

Review finding N8.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): align hcp/grants/revoke with list on a delegate's scope, and define revoking an expired grant

A delegate now revokes exactly the grants hcp/grants/list lists to it (question 20), rather than an undefined "within the delegation's scope". Revoking an expired grant succeeds with the empty response and changes nothing (question 15, extended). The spec links hcp/grants/relinquish where it says relinquishment is not this task, and lists relinquish and list in related.

Review findings M5, M6.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): declare response size bounds for hcp/grants/list and read-own, and make list paginate to fit

grants/list declares a 4 MiB response bound for a page of up to 1000 grants, and a provider MUST return fewer grants and nextCursor where the rest would not fit. read-own declares 5 MiB: the 4 MiB hcp/directives/list bound for its directives plus room for the grant. Both are framework bounds. The cursor and nextCursor maxLength of 2048 already match the family constant.

Review findings I11 (grants part), I14 (grants/list part).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): return HCP's grant object whole in the hcp/grants/request response

The response modelled the grant with its own names (grantedAt, grantExpiresAt absent rather than null), a 1024-character purpose description and an optional one, where HCP's grant object and the shared Grant have issuedAt, a nullable expiresAt, a required description bounded at 4096. The response is now {accessToken, tokenExpiresAt, grant}: the OAuth token response's members beside HCP's grant object (HCP 6.1.5, 13.3), as hcp/grants/read-own returns it, with authorizingPrincipal.delegation withheld (HCP 17.4).   say the field is source-only for now: build-registry.mjs does not emit
  it and the site does not render it.

Review findings I13, M21, M22, M23, N10.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): declare the operators-or-requires standing-rule rule where the shared def no longer checks it

Applies user decision 4 on the restacked branch. The anyOf of the two
`required` clauses now lives only at the hcp/rules/set request root; the
shared StandingRule in hcp/_shared/0.1 no longer checks that a standing
rule carries `operators`, `requires`, or both. Declare it again where a
standing rule is reached through the shared def: hcp/rules/list
(/$defs/Response/properties/rules/items), hcp/rules/set
(/$defs/Response/properties/rule), hcp/export
(/$defs/Response/properties/export/properties/rules/items) and hcp/import
(/properties/export/properties/rules/items, now through ImportedExport).

Also declare, on hcp/import, that ext["vnd.trusttasks.hcp-carriage"]
validates against HcpCarriageImportExtension, which the opaque framework
Ext does not check (/$defs/Response/properties/ext).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): require a request proof on every hcp/* request that carries an access token

The token binding applied only where a request carried a proof, so on the six
reads whose request proof was RECOMMENDED (entries/query, entries/get,
grants/read-own, grants/list, rules/list, directives/list) a token lifted from a
stored or forwarded document could be replayed in an unsigned request. The
request proof is now REQUIRED on all six, so it is REQUIRED on all 26 specs whose
request carries accessToken, and the binding always applies.

This is a carriage rule, stricter than HCP's bearer model, and is recorded in
each of the 26 specs as pending HCP confirmation (question 53). The family's
front-matter profile in CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md is widened to match, and the four
request examples that had no proof now carry one.

Also lower hcp/export's response bound to 14 MiB, so that an export always fits
an hcp/import request (16 MiB) with the token, categoryMap, envelope and proof
that request adds; the rationale states the 2 MiB of headroom.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for the request proof and export bound

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): accept any HCP-valid export in hcp/import and document where hcp/* is stricter than HCP

hcp/import said an export written to HCP's schema alone is accepted, but its
standing rules, directives, delegations and audit events reused the shared
shapes, with their framework size bounds and extra non-empty requirements, so
an HCP-valid export (a long directive text, an empty setBy or
basis.description) could still be refused. ImportedExport now takes them as
ImportedStandingRule, ImportedDirective, ImportedDelegation and a relaxed
ImportedAuditEvent, which keep only HCP's own constraints; where a lint needs a
declared bound it is the request's own 16 MiB document bound. The category
pattern is kept (question 54). The spec says so, with a new example of such an
export and invalid examples for what HCP itself still refuses.

hcp/grants/request: a requested purpose's description is REQUIRED (HCP
6.1.5.2), and the requesting party's name is bounded at 1024, as in the stored
grant.

Every hcp/* schema with size bounds now says they are framework bounds, not HCP
requirements, as is a non-empty requirement HCP does not make; every spec's
field mapping says its payload is closed at the top level where HCP's shapes are
open. Questions 54 (HCP's URI patterns disagree) and 55 (HCP's grant and
delegation schemas disagree) are cross-referenced in the Pending sections of
the specs they touch.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): sign the request and hold examples with authentication

The 32 request examples and the one next-step (hold) example in the 28
hcp/* specifications carried "proofPurpose": "assertionMethod". SPEC §4.7.3
says a producer SHOULD sign a Trust Task document with authentication, and
SHOULD NOT sign with assertionMethod unless the governing specification
defines the document's proof as an attestation (§7.3 item 8). No hcp/*
specification defines a request or a hold that way, and the proof libraries
sign with authentication by default.

The example proofValues are placeholders: every signer is a
did:web:*.example identifier and most values are not base58btc, so no check
verifies them and none is changed. The Rust conformance tests embed the
request examples and are regenerated. The TypeScript, Go and Dart modules
do not carry the examples and regenerate unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Alberto L <alberto_leon@seas.harvard.edu>

* fix(hcp): name the export size refusal hcp/export:tooLarge

SPEC §8.5 rule 2 keeps a family namespace for a code whose meaning is
defined once for the whole family, in a shared convention its
specifications reference, "and never to give a specification-specific code
a broader name than it has earned". hcp:exportTooLarge is declared and
emitted by hcp/export alone, is defined against that task's own
maxDocumentBytes bound, and is, as the specification says, not an HCP
error. Unlike hcp:invalidToken, hcp:versionConflict and
hcp:credentialInvalid, it maps no HCP Core error (HCP 5.5). It takes the
task's own slug as its namespace (§8.5 rule 1): hcp/export:tooLarge, the
form four vtc/* specifications already use for the same condition.

Renamed in hcp/export's front matter, error text, example and question 33,
and in the shared Export definition's description. The registry build's
namespace check accepts it. Regenerated: the Rust constant is now
hcp::export::v0_1::error_codes::TOO_LARGE, and the description text moves
in the TypeScript, Go and Dart modules.

Signed-off-by: Alberto L <alberto_leon@seas.harvard.edu>

* fix(hcp): say that create and revise carry no top-level member HCP does not define

The request payload roots of hcp/entries/create and hcp/entries/revise are
closed, so a top-level member that HCP does not define is refused, while
HCP's own create and revise request schemas admit one (HCP A.2) and, for
create, the body is an entry whose undefined members a provider preserves
(HCP 4.2, 9.4.3). SPEC §9.4 item 6 has a carriage say what it cannot
express, and neither field mapping did. Each now says so, and names the
nested members that stay open.

Text only: no schema changes, and the four libraries regenerate unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Alberto L <alberto_leon@seas.harvard.edu>

* fix(ts): carry the request's ceremony member onto responses and error responses

respondWith and rejectWithRecipient, and so rejectWith, refuse and the
transport's reject, copied parentThreadId onto the document they build but
not ceremony. A reply built with them left the enactment unless the caller
set the member itself. SPEC §4.11.3 says a producer SHOULD carry the same
ceremony.enactment onto every document of the step it names, "including
any error response", and trust-tasks-rs's respond_with and
reject_with_recipient already clone the member. The TypeScript builders now
do the same: the answer gets its own copy, and the member stays absent when
the request has none.

Go and Dart are not changed here. RespondWith and RejectWithRecipient in
trust-tasks-go, and respondWith and rejectWithRecipient in
trust-tasks-dart, also carry parentThreadId only. docs/runtime-parity.md
records the difference as a todo.

Signed-off-by: Alberto L <alberto_leon@seas.harvard.edu>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for the schema-scan fixes

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): declare the disclosed-evidence credential rule on hcp/entries/query

hcp/entries/query's uncheckedRules listed the rule that a
verifiable-credential evidence item carries `credential` (HCP 4.2.2) for the
Entry branch of a result item only. The Disclosure branch reaches the same
shared EvidenceItem through DisclosedEvidenceItem's allOf, where the schema
leaves the rule unchecked in the same way, and HCP's own disclosure schema
enforces it. hcp/entries/get, create and revise list both branches; query
now does too, in the form get uses.

The build's cross-check did not report the gap because it counts a marked
shared schema as covered once it is reached on any path, and the Entry
branch reaches EvidenceItem first.

Signed-off-by: Alberto L <alberto_leon@seas.harvard.edu>

* fix(rs): allow clippy::unit_arg on the generated spec tree

HCP's reserved subject.relationship is typed "type": "null", as HCP's own
entry schema writes it, so typify emits a () field and builder code that
clippy::unit_arg flags under --all-features. Allow the lint beside the other
typify-output allows in specs/mod.rs.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): carry format uri on the audit event's purpose, and name the consumer's URI check on the slug-or-URI unions

HCP writes an audit event's purpose as anyOf [purposeCode, null], and its
purposeCode carries format: uri. AuditEvent.purpose now has the same shape as
our own PurposeCode (format uri, minLength 1, maxLength, pattern) while still
admitting null, since format constrains only a string. After 0.1 is released a
format change is breaking, so it is made now.

Category, Directive.action and Delegation.relationship admit a slug or an
absolute URI in one pattern, and format: uri would refuse every slug; their
descriptions now say that checking a custom value is a well-formed absolute
URI, as HCP's prose requires, is the consumer's check.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): define the grants/request hold hint

trust-task-next-step says a producer validates a hint against the schema of
the specification its typeUri names, and the hold's { "retryAfter": 5 } had
no schema to validate against. grants/request now defines it as
$defs.NextStepHint, reachable via $anchor "next-step-hint" in the same
payload schema the hold's typeUri names: a closed object whose REQUIRED
retryAfter is a whole number of seconds from 1 to 3600, which the
description distinguishes from trust-task-error's RFC 3339 retryAfter. The
hold's prose names the definition and says a hint that fails is ignored.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): make accessToken optional for an enrolled Management Client

HCP 3.2.3 has a Management Client act under credentials the Authorizing
Principal obtained by authenticating, and no hcp/* task issues a Management
Client token; a wallet paired with the provider proves itself by the request
proof the carriage already requires. accessToken becomes OPTIONAL on the
eighteen governance requests and on hcp/entries/create. With no token, the
provider authenticates the issuer VID by the REQUIRED request proof as a
Management Client the Authorizing Principal enrolled, and refuses any other
issuer with permissionDenied; with one, the token rules, including question
22's binding, apply unchanged. The proof requirement is unchanged.

Recorded as a working assumption pending HCP confirmation (question 56) in
each affected spec. The "Missing accessToken" invalid fixtures of those specs
are removed, since such a payload is now valid. Context Client operations
keep the token REQUIRED.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for the audit purpose format, the optional accessToken and the hold hint

accessToken is now optional on the governance requests and on
hcp/entries/create (an Option in Rust, a pointer in Go, nullable in Dart and
optional in TypeScript); AuditEvent.purpose carries format uri, which typify
turns into a plain String; and grants/request gains $defs.NextStepHint. The
conformance tests drop the removed "Missing accessToken" fixtures.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(build): compare bounds, patterns, formats and closed objects with HCP's schemas

check-hcp-drift's first mode compares members, required-ness, types and
enums, and by design not bounds, patterns, formats or closed payloads, so
a meaning-changing difference there (a "must not be empty" rule HCP does
not have, a slug-or-URI union merged into one pattern, a dropped format,
a closed request root) went unseen.

A second mode, `constraints` (scripts/lib/hcp-drift-constraints.mjs),
walks the same mapped objects and compares every bound keyword,
`pattern`, `format`, `additionalProperties`/`unevaluatedProperties:
false` and scalar unions. It is written independently of the first mode,
with its own $ref resolution, walker and comparison; the two share only
the map. Its allowlist, scripts/lib/hcp-drift-constraints-allowlist.json,
keeps the first one's discipline (reason, ref, stale entries fail), adds
an optional `detail` glob so a class such as "a cap ours adds where HCP
sets none" can be allowed without allowing a cap HCP sets, and lists
pattern pairs that accept the same strings.

Both modes run by default; `--mode members|constraints` runs one, and
`--pinned-commit` prints the HCP commit the carried specs pin. The
existing flags are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* chore(build): give each constraint difference from HCP's schemas its reason

Every difference the constraints mode finds, each with its reason and the
spec's field-mapping section or editors' question:

- each non-empty bound (minLength/minItems of 1) where HCP's schema
  accepts the empty value: what the member names and why an empty value
  names nothing, under the framework non-empty bound the field mappings'
  "Where this payload is stricter than HCP's shapes" paragraph states;
  the ten HCP's own pattern, enum or `contains` already makes redundant
  say so;
- the four slug-or-URI unions merged into one pattern (category,
  directive action twice, delegation relationship), and hcp/import's
  copies of them, with the `format: uri` the merge drops;
- `format: uri` left off hcp/import's audit-event `purpose`;
- the closed request and result roots, entries/create and entries/revise
  with the provider-preserved members they refuse;
- the size caps ours adds where HCP sets none, and hcp/import's nominal
  16 MiB bounds, as classes;
- the two pattern pairs that are the same language written differently.

The shared AuditEvent's `purpose` is left out on purpose: HCP gives it
`format: uri` and the schema is being fixed instead, so the check reports
it until that fix lands.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* ci: run the HCP drift check, both modes, against the pinned HCP commit
