title: feat(hcp): add the hcp/* specifications, carrying the Human Context Protocol (HCP 2.0-draft-3) as Trust Tasks
body:
### What and why

This is the first implementation of the Human Context Protocol over Trust Tasks. It adds the `hcp/*` spec family,
28 specifications at 0.1 (framework 0.6.0), which carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 (`loyalagents/hcp-spec` @ `b790561`)
operations as Trust Task documents. A Context Client, a Management Client and an HCP Provider can then run HCP over
any Trust Task binding (TSP, DIDComm, HTTPS) instead of only HCP's own HTTP and MCP bindings, with each document
signed by its issuer's VID.

Each spec carries one HCP operation (`carries:` in its front matter) and maps its members one for one onto HCP's
(a field-mapping table in each spec). It changes nothing in HCP's semantics, so a provider applies every HCP rule
unchanged. Where the HCP text leaves a point open, the spec takes a working assumption and marks it *pending HCP
confirmation*. These are listed below. The full list of questions put to the HCP editors is published with the
family, in `specs/hcp/_shared/0.1/QUESTIONS.md`, and every spec links to it.

### What's included

- **Context plane (8):** `hcp/entries/{query,get,create,revise,withdraw}`, `hcp/grants/{read-own,relinquish}`,
  `hcp/shares/report`.
- **Governance plane (18):** `hcp/grants/{list,revoke}`, `hcp/audit/read`, `hcp/disclosures/summary`,
  `hcp/export`, `hcp/import`, `hcp/entries/{hard-delete,confirm,set-categories,restrict-purposes}`,
  `hcp/rules/{list,set,remove}`, `hcp/directives/{list,set,remove}`, `hcp/delegations/{list,end}`.
- **Grant channel and notice (2):** `hcp/grants/request` (a Trust Task grant request. The provider holds it with a
  `trust-task-next-step` while the person decides. HCP defines no wire format for this, so the spec has no
  `carries`) and `hcp/grants/revoked` (the provider's revocation notice).
- **Shared schemas** in `specs/hcp/_shared/0.1/`: common types, context entry, entry write, disclosure, grant,
  standing rule, directive, delegation, audit event and export, each matched to HCP's JSON Schemas.
- **Regenerated libraries:** Rust (the `hcp` Cargo feature of `trust-tasks-rs`), TypeScript, Go and Dart, all
  generated, with no generator source changes and no hand-written library lines. Regenerated over main's
  generators after #1385, #1378 and #1379 merged (see below).
- **An HCP drift check:** `npm run check-hcp-drift -- --hcp <hcp-spec checkout>`. It compares each spec's schemas
  with HCP's own, member by member, through a mapping file. An allowlist names each intended difference and why
  it is there. At this tip: 39 differences, all 39 allowlisted, 0 stale entries. The stacked uncheckedRules PR adds
  a second mode (bounds, patterns, formats, closed objects) and runs both modes in CI.
- **The questions for the HCP editors:** `specs/hcp/_shared/0.1/QUESTIONS.md`, with the three that matter most
  (37, 46 and 56) first, a status summary, and each question's working assumption and the specs that take it.
- **A `task-consent/request` example** of a request typed with the `#request` fragment, beside the bare form, so
  that implementations are tested on both (the framework already requires accepting both).
- **Family conventions:** `specs/hcp/_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md` defines the three family error codes
  (`hcp:invalidToken`, `hcp:versionConflict`, `hcp:credentialInvalid`) once, as SPEC §8.5 rule 2 requires, and
  every spec declares each with that meaning, unchanged.
- **Docs:** CODEOWNERS for `specs/hcp/`; the drift check in DEVELOPMENT.md and CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md, with the
  family's front-matter profile for Management Client reads; one payload-presence row in `docs/runtime-parity.md`
  stating, per runtime, whether generated types keep an optional member absent, empty and `null` apart and write a
  required nullable member's `null`; and in `docs/packages/rust.md`, typify's folding and the `hcp` members whose
  schemas carry presence themselves.

### Decisions taken

- **The carriage's own members live in an extension namespace.** `ext["vnd.trusttasks.hcp-carriage"]` holds them,
  for example `rulesNotApplied` on the `hcp/import` response, so every payload member reads as an HCP member.
- **Token binding, MUST, on a required request proof.** Every `hcp/*` request that has an `accessToken` member (26
  specs) REQUIRES a request proof, and the provider refuses with `permissionDenied` a token issued to a client other than
  the one the `issuer` VID identifies. Both are carriage rules, not HCP's, and requiring the proof is stricter than
  HCP's bearer model (question 53). Without it, a token lifted from a stored or forwarded query could be replayed
  in an unsigned request, so the six reads that only RECOMMENDED a request proof (`entries/query`, `entries/get`,
  `grants/read-own`, `grants/list`, `rules/list`, `directives/list`) now require one. A
  retained copy of a document drops `accessToken` and keeps `accessTokenDigest` instead: a SHA-256 multihash in
  multibase base64url, the framework's DigestMultibase form (SPEC 4.9.3).
- **An enrolled Management Client may send no token.** `accessToken` is OPTIONAL in the 18 governance requests and
  in `hcp/entries/create`. A request without one is the Management Client's, authenticated by its required request
  proof under a key the Authorizing Principal enrolled, and acts for that person; a create with no token is the
  Management Client's write for the person, under no grant. The other seven requests that carry a token
  (`entries/{query,get,revise,withdraw}`, `shares/report`, `grants/{read-own,relinquish}`) keep it REQUIRED. Whether
  this counts as HCP's Management Client credentials is question 56.
- **The token lives as long as the grant.** In `hcp/grants/request`, `tokenExpiresAt` SHOULD equal the grant's
  `expiresAt`, since 0.1 has no refresh, within HCP 13.4's 24 hours and HCP 16.2's one hour for `health_context`.
  The example's token now ends with its four-hour grant, and the token's description no longer names a one-hour
  default.
- **The token stays out of a model's context (HCP 10.5).** `hcp/entries/query`'s "The access token" says that in an
  agent runtime the token is held by the component that presents it, and never enters a model's context or is
  returned as tool content, including a token received in a response. Every other token-carrying spec points there,
  and `hcp/grants/request`, which returns the token, says the same.
- **A provider with no discovery document is anchored on its VID.** The client's anchor is the provider VID it
  obtained when the person connected it (by pairing, or by `trust-task-discovery` from a VID it already trusts), and
  it sends a token only to that VID. The binding to HCP's discovery document applies only where one exists (HCP 19.1,
  question 1). Every spec's reference to the rule matches, and `hcp/grants/revoked` takes the notice key from the
  VID's DID document, using the JWKS only where a discovery document exists.
- **A new identity is a new client.** A grant identifies its client (HCP 3.11 invariant 3): a new VID, or a key
  without provable continuity, needs a new grant, and a grant never moves to another client identity.
- **The export fits an import.** `hcp/export`'s response is bounded at 14 MiB, 2 MiB under `hcp/import`'s 16 MiB
  request bound, so that an export always fits an import request with the `accessToken`, `categoryMap`, envelope
  and proof that request adds (about 1.03 MiB at their schema bounds).
- **Import leniency.** `hcp/import` accepts any export valid under HCP's export schema, within its 16 MiB request
  bound. Its `options` is optional, its audit events may carry only HCP's members, and its standing rules,
  directives, delegations and audit events (`ImportedStandingRule`, `ImportedDirective`, `ImportedDelegation`,
  `ImportedAuditEvent`) keep only HCP's own constraints: none of the shared shapes' framework size caps or extra
  non-empty requirements (a long directive `text`, an empty `setBy` or `basis.description` are accepted). Where a
  lint needs a declared bound, it is the 16 MiB document bound itself. The one constraint kept beyond HCP's export
  schema is the category pattern (question 54).
- **Framework bounds are labelled as such.** Every `hcp/*` schema with size bounds says in its description that
  they are Trust Tasks framework bounds, not HCP requirements, as is a non-empty requirement HCP does not make.
  Every spec's field mapping says its payload is closed at the top level, where HCP's shapes are open
  (for `hcp/entries/create` and `revise`, in the maintainer's wording: a top-level member HCP does not define
  cannot be written through the task).
- **The export size refusal is `hcp/export:tooLarge`** (`retryable: false`), the code namespaced to the task,
  not `hcp:` (question 33).
- **Every example is signed with an `authentication` proof.** Alberto L moved the request and hold examples; the 14
  response examples in 13 specs, and the third `hcp/import` request example, now follow, as every library signs. The
  sentences that said any third party can verify a response now say it is a statement signed by the provider, which
  anyone holding the provider's public key can check came from it, and that the proof is made for `authentication`,
  not as an attestation (SPEC §4.7.3).
- **An audit event's `purpose` carries `format: uri`,** as HCP's does, with the same shape as `PurposeCode`. The
  three slug-or-URI unions (`Category`, `Directive.action`, `Delegation.relationship`) cannot carry it, since it
  would refuse every slug, so each says that checking a custom value is a well-formed absolute URI, as HCP A.3
  requires, is the consumer's check.
- **The TypeScript reply builders carry the request's `ceremony` member** onto the success and error responses, as
  the Rust and Go builders already did (`docs/runtime-parity.md`).
- **A requested purpose carries its description.** In `hcp/grants/request` a purpose's `description` is REQUIRED,
  as HCP's purpose is (HCP 6.1.5.2), and the requesting party's `name` is bounded at 1024, as in the stored grant.
- **The hold's hint has a schema.** `hcp/grants/request` defines `$defs.NextStepHint` (`$anchor: "next-step-hint"`):
  a closed object whose `retryAfter` is REQUIRED, a whole number of seconds from 1 to 3600, unlike
  trust-task-error's RFC 3339 `retryAfter`. It lives in grants/request's own schema because `trust-task-next-step`
  says a hint is validated against the schema of the spec its `typeUri` names. A client ignores a hint that fails,
  as if it were absent.
- **A decline is `permissionDenied`, and an ended hold stays ended.** `hcp/grants/request` says why a decline is
  `permissionDenied`: the task issues a grant and does not exist to produce a decision (SPEC §4.13.3 rule 2, last
  sentence, and §8.6), which the neutral denial depends on (question 25). A hold has a lifetime set by policy. Once
  it passes undecided the policy denies, the next resubmission gets the same fixed `permissionDenied`, and the
  thread is never reopened; a new ask is a new thread. The provider keeps an ended thread's record for at least as
  long as it would accept a resubmission on that thread (question 39). It never answers `cancelled`, which would
  let a client tell an abandoned hold from an unknown person.
- **The approval exchange names the held thread.** A nested approval exchange, such as `task-consent/request`,
  SHOULD carry `parentThreadId` equal to the held `threadId` (SPEC §4.9.2, §4.13.3 rule 3), so that the approver
  can check it against the thread it was shown.
- **A next step is not the response.** A client MUST NOT treat a `trust-task-next-step` as the response to
  `hcp/grants/request`; it resubmits or gives up.
- **Size bounds are not delivery guarantees.** `hcp/entries/query`, `hcp/export` and `hcp/import` say that the
  bounds and every `maxDocumentBytes` limit what a party writes and accepts; a transport or mediator may cap a
  message lower (1 MiB, for example), so a producer MUST NOT assume delivery.
- **HCP 15, 16.2 and 18.1 are cited where they bind,** in each spec's "What HCP requires that a document cannot
  express": the Memory Manager on create, revise and import, the health-entry credential rules on create, revise
  and import, the unconfirmed model-inferred health entry that query omits and get refuses, and the review that
  confirm should offer.
- **Revocation notice retries.** Each `hcp/grants/revoked` delivery attempt is a fresh document with a stable
  `noticeId`, so the client deduplicates on `noticeId`, not on the document id. Delivery is bounded at 24 hours,
  and `noticeId` records are kept for 25 hours.
- **The standing-rule rule is checked only at `hcp/rules/set`'s payload root.** That is the rule that a standing
  rule carries `operators`, `requires`, or both. Leaving it out of the shared definition keeps `StandingRule`
  fully typed in every library. The description says it is not checked by the schema there.

### Assumptions pending HCP confirmation

Every spec has a `## Pending HCP confirmation` section that cites, by number, the questions that bear on it, and
links the published list, `specs/hcp/_shared/0.1/QUESTIONS.md`. Questions 35, 36, 43 to 52 and 57 appear in no spec
(marked *in no spec* below); 41 is unused. In summary:

- **Family-wide:** the carriage's conformance identifier, and a provider with no discovery document (1); a carriage
  other than the HTTP Binding carrying governance operations (37); DPoP-bound tokens (43, in no spec); the error a token
  presented by the wrong client gets (49, in no spec); a request proof on every request that carries a token (53); a Management
  Client authenticated by a proof under an enrolled key, with no token (56);
  presence signals the carriage adds (42); HCP's URI patterns disagree (54); HCP's grant and delegation schemas
  disagree (55).
- **Shared behaviour:** the error for a revoked grant (2); pagination and `nextCursor: null` (3); repeated reads
  and the `context.read` audit event (4).
- **Entries:** a Management Client calling Query (5); `ref` or `entryId` (6); `permittedPurposes` on a create (7);
  the members of a revise (8); revising a rejected version (9); withdrawing (10); the hard-delete result (11); a
  delegate confirming an entry (12); changing categories (13); removing a purpose narrowing (14); health entries resting on supporting credentials, still open (57, in no spec).
- **Grants:** revoking a grant that is already revoked, expired or unknown (15); `iat` freshness against retries
  (16); the notice when a grant ends with its delegation (17); read-own and directives (18); list grants with a
  Context Client's token (19); a delegate's list (20).
- **Grant requests:** a Trust Task as the grant channel (21); the client's VID as its client identifier (22);
  naming the person (23); persistent grants (24); a token in a Trust Task response as grant evidence, and a
  decline answered with `permissionDenied` (25); collecting a held request's outcome, and a hold that ends
  undecided (39); registering a client at first approval (52, in no spec).
- **Onward sharing:** a re-delivered report (26); a model API run by another organization (46, in no spec); a person in a
  group conversation (50, in no spec).
- **Rules and directives:** removing an unknown rule or directive (27); a delegate's lists (28); custom directive
  actions (51, in no spec).
- **Audit and the disclosure summary:** filter names (29); the result member and date bounds (30); a delegate's
  summary (38).
- **Delegations:** `status=ended` (31); who may end a sub-delegation (32).
- **Export and import:** export size, the export bounded at 14 MiB so that it fits a 16 MiB import request (33); import outcomes (34);
  a delegate's export and import scope (40).
- **Deployment, not tied to one spec (in no spec):** a local bridge over a non-HTTP carriage (44); the Client Operator of an
  agent plugin (45); MCP over Streamable HTTP under First-Party (47); the 20.2 test hook (48).
- **Not carried:** dismissing a conflict and declining a proposal (35) are not carried, and neither is HCP
  discovery (36). A provider advertises the `hcp/*` Type URIs with `trust-task-discovery`.

### Known limitations

- **Presence in the generated libraries** (`docs/runtime-parity.md`, the payload-presence row). TypeScript keeps
  an optional member absent, empty and `null` apart. Rust writes and reads an optional `[]`, `{}` and `null` as
  absent; Go and Dart keep `[]` but write and read an optional `null` as absent. Where that difference means
  something, `hcp` carries the meaning in the schema instead (required nullable members,
  `options.includeVersions`/`includeAudit`, `minItems: 1` on query categories). One gap remains for Go and Dart: both
  drop a required nullable member whose value is null, writing a schema-invalid document, and the `hcp` members
  this affects are listed in that row (`Grant.expiresAt`, `DelegationTerm.endsAt`, the disclosure summary's
  `usableUntil`, restrict-purposes `permittedPurposes`, five `AuditEvent` members, get and query `directives`). The
  generator fixes ship as separate PRs; until they land, a Go or Dart producer must not send those members null
  through the generated types.
- **Go:** the `hcp` packages under `trust-tasks-go/specs/hcp` are generated types with no package-level tests
  (`go vet` is clean). Optional slices are pointers, as elsewhere in the module.
- **Dart:** the generated `hcp` libraries are exported per module, not from the barrel, which exports the runtime
  only. They are covered by the package's existing generator and analyzer runs.
- A few rules are stated in prose and not checked by the schema (for example, that a temporary grant has an
  `expiresAt` and a persistent one has none, and that a request names exactly one of `ref` and `entryId`). Each description says so. The stacked uncheckedRules PR declares them in
  front matter and checks the declarations.
- **Rust: a string with both `format` and `pattern` has no typed check.** The Rust generator emits a plain `String`
  for a format it does not map to a native type, dropping the length and pattern check it gives a pattern-only
  string. That now applies to `PurposeCode` and to `AuditEvent.purpose`; full validation (`--features validate`)
  still checks both. The generator fix changes Rust types across the registry, so it goes in its own PR.

### Merge order and stacking

1. **This PR** (`feat/hcp-suite`), on `main`.
2. **The uncheckedRules PR** (`feat(build)`), stacked on this one.
3. **The demos PR** (`feat(examples)`), also stacked on this one. It is independent of the uncheckedRules PR.

Merge this one first, then retarget the other two to `main`. They can then merge in either order.

### The `--all-features` clippy leg

It had failed on this PR for two reasons. One was the runner running out of memory (exit 143), which #1391
(adaptive swap) fixed. The other was a real lint, `clippy::unit_arg`, in the hcp entries modules: HCP reserves an
entry's `subject.relationship` as `"type": "null"`, and typify rendered that member `()`. Since #1385 merged, the
Rust presence pass renders it `Option<()>`, so the lint no longer fires and the temporary allow in
`trust-tasks-rs/src/specs/mod.rs` has been removed. `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-rs --features hcp,validate
--all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

### Test evidence

This tip, 186773c97, takes the follow-up round from Alberto L's review (the decisions above on authentication
proofs, the audit purpose's format, the optional token, the provider anchor, the end of a hold, the approval
exchange, HCP 10.5, the token lifetime, the hint schema, size bounds, client identity and the HCP citations, and
the published questions). Thank you, Alberto, for a second careful pass. The schema changes, and the examples the
Rust conformance tests embed, are regenerated in all four libraries in two separate commits. All run fresh on this
tip:

- `npm run check`, `npm run build` and `npm run test:checks`: pass (77/77 tests).
- `npm run build-bundles` and `npm run check-bundles`: pass (1453 bundles verified).
- `npm run check-hcp-drift`: 39 differences, 39 allowlisted, 0 stale entries.
- `npm run check-bindings`: pass.
- Rust: `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `cargo build --workspace --all-targets` passes; `cargo clippy --workspace
  --all-targets -- -D warnings` (default features) clean; `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate,hcp`
  373 passed, 0 failed, 16 ignored.
- Rust, `--all-features`: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` on this tip is
  pending confirmation on a second machine with the CI toolchain; on the previous tip it was clean there. That leg peaks at about 26 GB, which is why CI's hosted runner kills it with exit 143
  before it finishes, a known issue separate from this PR.
- TypeScript: `tsc --noEmit` clean and `npm test` 291/291.
- Go: `go build`, `go vet` and `go test` pass on the module and on `specs/hcp`, and `gofmt -l` reports nothing.
- Dart: `dart analyze --fatal-infos` clean and `dart test` 317/317.
- After that tip, 039d2ace3 widens `hcp:credentialInvalid` in create and revise to HCP 16.2's health case and adds question 57 (open, no assumption taken), and 50de0bb21 regenerates (two Rust doc comments; TypeScript, Go and Dart unchanged). Every check above except the `--all-features` leg re-ran on 50de0bb21 with the same results.
- 08bbef082 defines the three `hcp:` family codes once (`_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md`) and makes the family's terms consistent (descriptions and prose only; no member, value, title or validation change); 7f34f76dd regenerates all four libraries. On 7f34f76dd: `npm run check` passes, `npm run test:checks` 77/77, `check-hcp-drift` 39 differences, 39 allowlisted, 0 stale; `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate,hcp` 373 passed; `go build`/`go vet` on `specs/hcp`, `dart analyze --fatal-infos lib/specs/hcp` and `tsc --noEmit` clean. 9700339e9 then names HCP's General Context and VC Evidence Profiles as HCP does in the shared entry schema, regenerated in the same commit; `npm run validate` and the drift check pass on it.

### Follow-ups

- HCP's unmerged branch `codex/hcp-c8-completion-replay` adds a `completion-result` arm to the create, revise,
  import and withdraw results; no spec change now, but recheck it before this PR merges.
- A note in the TSP and DIDComm bindings that a mediator may cap a message below a task's `maxDocumentBytes`. Those
  are released transport specs outside this family, so it goes in its own `docs(bindings)` change.
- The Rust generator fix for strings with both `format` and `pattern` (see Known limitations).

### Not changed

`SPEC.md` is untouched. There are no version bumps and no `CHANGELOG.md` entries; the Release PR assigns those.

title: feat(hcp): add the hcp/* specifications, carrying the Human Context Protocol (HCP 2.0-draft-3) as Trust Tasks (#1380)
body:
feat(hcp): add the hcp/* specifications, carrying the Human Context Protocol (HCP 2.0-draft-3) as Trust Tasks (#1380)

* feat(hcp): carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 query, grant revoke and revocation notice as Trust Tasks

Add the hcp/* protocol family (SPEC §9.4) with three draft 0.1 specs
targeting framework 0.6.0, each carrying one Human Context Protocol
2.0-draft-3 operation:

- hcp/entries/query: Query (HCP 5.2.1). The HCP access token travels
  opaquely in `accessToken`; the result's `timestamp` is renamed
  `respondedAt`; `categories` gets a framework bound of 256.
- hcp/grants/revoke: Revoke grant (HCP 6.2, 9.2), destructive and acting
  for the Authorizing Principal, with an empty response for HCP's 204.
- hcp/grants/revoked: the revocation notice (HCP 6.2.3, 9.9). The SET
  claims map to the envelope, and an empty response carries RFC 8935's
  202. The notice is signed with a provider VID key that the provider's
  JWKS must also publish.

HCP's invalid-token condition maps to the family code hcp:invalidToken.
Shared shapes (common, context entry, disclosure, directive) live in
specs/hcp/_shared/0.1. They were written from the CC BY 4.0 HCP text,
with attribution, not copied from HCP's schema files. HCP's kebab-case
enum values are allowlisted as external.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(hcp): name hcp/* owners in CODEOWNERS and cite the family as a carries example

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for hcp/*

Generated by trust-tasks-codegen (plus cargo fmt), build-ts-bindings, build-go-bindings and build-dart-bindings. Adds the hcp Cargo feature.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): match the hcp/_shared and query schemas to HCP 2.0-draft-3

Checked member by member against HCP 2.0-draft-3 (schemas/2.0-draft-3 and the
specification text, b790561):

- Directive: directiveId, action, effect, text, setBy and createdAt are
  required (HCP 6.4).
- Disclosure: version, content, assertion, classification, standing and
  useUntil are required, and id, subject, record and schema are refused
  (HCP 7.4); provenance on request carries no identifiers (HCP 7.4.1).
- Entry: type is an array, schema is the HCP entry URI, content names its
  profile, record carries version and provenance (HCP 4.2).
- Minimization report requires method (HCP 7.5); the query response example
  uses a registered method and carries version and standing.
- Query request: categories has no minItems and purposeDescription no
  minLength, as in HCP 5.2.1.

The rules HCP states with if/then/else or contains (General Context value,
VC Evidence content, confidence only for model-inferred assertions, one
content evidence item, ContextEntry in type, credential shape, proposal only on
contradicts) are written into the descriptions instead: the Rust generator
(typify) supports neither keyword.

Allowlists the HCP enum values the casing lint flags, and HCP's evidence
verification.at member for the wire-conventions lint. Adds invalid-example
fixtures for each corrected rule a validator can check.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): correct the hcp/* spec prose against HCP 2.0-draft-3

- Drop claims HCP does not make: that query text is as sensitive as content
  or is not logged (HCP 8.2 has no member for it), and that a Management
  Client token cannot query (HCP 5.1, 5.2.1, 7.4).
- Directives are present in every result to a Context Client (HCP 6.4), and
  only a client that claims to follow them must.
- Give the full nine-error table of HCP 5.5, including idempotency-conflict,
  version-conflict and credential-invalid, and scope-denied's "the entry does
  not exist"; quote invalid-token's own condition and say that reading a
  revoked grant's evidence as invalid is this specification's reading (6.2.2).
- Revoke: a delegate revokes within the delegation's scope (HCP 17.5); a
  Context Client token on the same HTTP DELETE relinquishes (HCP 9.4.6); notice
  goes only to a client holding disclosed entries with an endpoint (6.2.2).
- Revoked: the client stops using its copies and passes none on, with the
  legal-obligation exemption (HCP 6.2.2, 6.2.5); HCP does not require
  deletion. "5 attempts" (HCP 9.9), asymmetric signing, and the iat-versus-
  retry tension and delegation-end case flagged as open questions.
- Citations: relevance ordering is 7.3, the method is declared in discovery
  (19.3), cryptosuites per 14.5.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for hcp/*

Generated by trust-tasks-codegen (plus cargo fmt), build-ts-bindings, build-go-bindings and build-dart-bindings from the corrected hcp/_shared and hcp/entries/query schemas.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): take the approved working assumptions, each marked pending HCP confirmation

Each hcp/* spec gains a 'Pending HCP confirmation' section that lists, by the
number of the question put to the HCP editors, the reading it takes where HCP
2.0-draft-3 is silent, and every sentence that relies on one links to it.

- A request under a revoked grant gets hcp:invalidToken (question 1).
- hcp/grants/revoke: revoking an already-revoked grant succeeds idempotently
  with the empty response; an unknown grantId, or one the caller cannot see,
  gets permissionDenied with the same text (question 2).
- hcp/grants/revoked: every delivery attempt reuses the id but carries a fresh
  issuedAt and proof, a declared departure from HCP 9.9; a client that already
  accepted the notice answers idConflict (SPEC 7.2 item 11), which the
  provider records as the acknowledgement (question 3).
- hcp/grants/revoked: an optional reason (revoked | delegation-ended) announces
  a grant ended with its delegation, with revokedAt the instant it ended
  (HCP 17.6, question 4); delegation-ended is allowlisted as an HCP value.
- A Management Client may query and receive whole entries (question 5); a
  re-delivered query causes no second context.read event (question 6).
- Providers do not claim the carriage in conformsTo and advertise it through
  trust-task-discovery (question 7).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for hcp/grants/revoked reason

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): send each hcp/grants/revoked delivery attempt as a fresh document with a stable noticeId

Replace the retry rule for hcp/grants/revoked 0.1 (question 3, still pending
HCP confirmation). Each delivery attempt is now a fresh Trust Task document
with a new id, issuedAt and proof, so the framework's duplicate-execution and
idConflict rules (SPEC 7.2 item 11, 8.4) apply normally and HCP's 300 s
freshness check applies to each attempt's issuedAt.

- Add the required payload member noticeId (a urn:uuid), carrying the SET's
  jti (HCP 9.9): minted per notice and the same on every attempt.
- The client deduplicates on noticeId and answers a repeat with the normal
  empty acknowledgement without acting twice; the provider treats that
  acknowledgement as delivery success (HCP 6.2.3).
- Drop the reading of idConflict as an acknowledgement.
- Field mapping: jti becomes noticeId; HCP's same token on every attempt
  becomes a fresh document per attempt with a stable noticeId.
- Examples carry noticeId, with a new later-attempt example; invalid fixtures
  for a missing and a malformed noticeId.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for hcp/grants/revoked noticeId

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP 2.0-draft-3 context plane as Trust Tasks

Adds hcp/entries/{get,create,revise,withdraw}, hcp/grants/{read-own,relinquish}
and hcp/shares/report at 0.1 (draft, framework 0.6.0), each carrying the HCP
Core context operation of the same name (HCP 5.2.2 to 5.2.8), with valid
examples and invalid fixtures. Adds the shared grant and entry-write schemas,
written from the HCP text with attribution, and bounds two request-reachable
arrays in the shared entry schema.

Maps version-conflict and credential-invalid to hcp:versionConflict and
hcp:credentialInvalid, and HCP's idempotency key to the document id. Points
HCP leaves open are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions C1 to C7).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): add the shared HCP governance objects (standing rule, delegation, audit event, export, grant)

New hcp/_shared/0.1 schemas written from HCP 2.0-draft-3 (6.1.5, 6.3, 8.2, 5.4.1, 17.2). grant.schema.json is the phase-2 draft, needed by hcp/grants/list. Directive arrays gain a maxItems framework bound, now that hcp/import makes them request-side. HCP's kebab-case values and its verbatim timestamp/at members are allowlisted, attributed to HCP.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP standing-rule and directive operations (list, set, remove)

hcp/rules/{list,set,remove} and hcp/directives/{list,set,remove} 0.1 carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 6.3, 6.4, 9.4.14 and 9.4.15. Open points are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions 7, 13, 14, 26).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP entry governance operations (hard delete, confirm or reject, change categories, restrict purposes)

hcp/entries/{hard-delete,confirm,set-categories,restrict-purposes} 0.1 carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 5.4.2, 3.8, 4.7.3, 4.2.1, 4.2.6, 9.4.5, 9.4.9 and 9.4.10, with hcp:versionConflict for expectedVersion. Open points are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions 7, 16, 20).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP audit log, disclosure summary and delegation operations

hcp/audit/read, hcp/disclosures/summary, hcp/delegations/{list,end} 0.1 carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 8.3, 8.6, 9.4.7, 9.4.12, 9.4.13, 9.5 and 17. Open points are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions 4, 7, 13, 14, 15, 21, 22, 25).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): carry the HCP export, import and list grants operations

hcp/export, hcp/import and hcp/grants/list 0.1 carry HCP 2.0-draft-3 5.4.1, 5.4.3, 6.1.5, 9.4.6, 9.4.8 and 9.4.11. Export and import are bounded at the registry's 16 MiB document ceiling, with hcp:exportTooLarge. Open points are marked pending HCP confirmation (questions 7, 14, 17, 23, 24).

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): add hcp/grants/request 0.1, a Trust-Task grant request held with a next step while the person decides

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): answer a Context Client's hcp/grants/list with its own grant only, as HCP 9.4.6 does over HTTP

A Context Client presenting its own token is listed only the grant under
which that token was issued, with authorizingPrincipal.delegation withheld
(HCP 17.4), instead of being refused with permissionDenied. Marked pending
HCP confirmation.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): mark the delegate confirmation and purpose-removal readings pending HCP confirmation

hcp/entries/confirm reads HCP 17.4 as letting a delegate confirm or reject
an entry within the delegation's scope, where HCP 3.8 names the Context
Subject; hcp/entries/restrict-purposes returns the entry without
classification.permittedPurposes once the narrowing is removed. Both were
stated without a mark; each now carries one and a Pending HCP
confirmation entry, beside the hcp/grants/list Context Client reading.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): cite the renumbered list of questions for the HCP editors

The questions put to the HCP editors are now one list, 1 to 36, grouped by
specification. Every pending HCP confirmation reference in the hcp/* specs
and schemas cites the new numbers, and each Pending HCP confirmation
section lists them in order. Phase 2's lettered questions take numbers, and
the rules and directives list descriptions no longer cite the duplicate 23.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for the hcp/* suite

Generated by trust-tasks-codegen (plus cargo fmt), build-ts-bindings,
build-go-bindings and build-dart-bindings, once, for the context plane,
the governance plane, hcp/grants/request and the fixes on top of them. The
new specs fall under the existing hcp Cargo feature.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): mark the carriage of governance operations outside the HTTP Binding pending HCP confirmation

HCP 2.0-draft-3 carries governance operations only over its HTTP Binding
(1.6, 5.4, 9.1, 10.1). The 18 governance specs now say so in Conformance
and Authorization and under "What HCP requires that a document cannot
express", take the reading that another carriage may carry them for a
Management Client acting for the Authorizing Principal (6.1.9), and mark
it pending HCP confirmation (question 37). Each Question 1 bullet points
to question 37, since the binding identifier it asks for is the same
question.

Review finding B1.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): give every Management Client read one front-matter profile

Every Management Client read now declares actsAsSubject false, since a
read produces no attributable effect in the person's name (SPEC 7.3
item 14); a request proof REQUIRED where the response discloses a
secret (export, audit/read, delegations/list, disclosures/summary) and
RECOMMENDED where it discloses metadata (grants/list, rules/list,
directives/list); and grants/read-own takes the transient retention
class of grants/list, since the provider records nothing for either
read. The rationales and the Authorization prose follow, the export
request example gains its now-required proof, and CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md
states the profile once.

Review finding I4.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): keep the access token out of retained documents and bind it to the issuer VID

Every hcp/* spec whose document carries accessToken gains one shared
"The access token" paragraph under Security & Privacy: the token MUST
travel only to the provider, a recipient MUST NOT log it or retain it
beyond the exchange, and a duplicate-execution or evidentiary record
keeps the document with the token removed, or a digest of it. Where the
request carries a proof, the provider MUST refuse with permissionDenied
a token issued to a client other than the one the issuer VID
identifies, a strengthening HCP does not itself require, marked pending
HCP confirmation (question 22) with a Question 22 bullet in each spec.
grants/request states the same for the token its response carries.

The Authorization sections replace the issuer-binding SHOULD with that
rule, the signed-request retention sentences keep the request with the
token removed, each durable retention rationale says the token is not
retained, and entries/query's lower-case "must travel only to the
provider" becomes BCP 14.

Review finding I5.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): name the Context Client as the party of grants/read-own and grants/relinquish

Both tasks refuse a Management Client's token, so the party that sends
them is a Context Client, not any HCP Client. The summary, the parties
front matter, the abstract and the Parties table say so, and the table
notes that HCP 5.2.6 and 5.2.7 say HCP Client.

Review finding N7.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): require operators or requires on a standing rule

HCP 6.3 and 9.4.14 require a standing rule to carry operators, requires, or both, and HCP's standing-rule.json states it as an anyOf of two required clauses. Add that anyOf to the hcp/rules/set request and to the shared StandingRule, remove the text that called the rule unchecked, and add invalid fixtures with neither member for the rules/set request, a rules/list listed rule and an export's rules.

Review finding I3.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): allow an empty permittedPurposes list in restrict-purposes

HCP 4.2.6 defines an empty classification.permittedPurposes: an entry may be disclosed for a purpose only where each list present includes it, so [] permits no purpose. HCP's common.json sets no minItems. Drop the minItems of 1, correct the prose and the member description, remove the invalid fixture for the empty list and add a spec example that sends one.

Review finding I7.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): align the entry response bounds, citations and wording of the entry governance tasks

Raise the response bound of hcp/entries/confirm, set-categories and restrict-purposes from 256 KiB to 512 KiB, the bound of create, revise and get, so an entry those tasks carry can also be confirmed, recategorised or restricted. Raise hcp/entries/query's response bound from 2 MiB to 12 MiB, so that 20 disclosures (HCP 7.2) each within get's bound always fit, with 2 MiB for directives, the minimization report, envelope and proof; it stays within the 16 MiB ceiling, and needs no rule for returning fewer entries.

Cite HCP 9.4.2, which says a Management Client names an entry by its id, instead of 9.4.5, and say "Context Subject" where HCP 5.4 does for whom the Management Client showed expectedVersion.

Review findings I11 (entries part), N1, N2.

an HCP-valid export (a long directive text, an empty setBy or
basis.description) could still be refused. ImportedExport now takes them as
ImportedStandingRule, ImportedDirective, ImportedDelegation and a relaxed
ImportedAuditEvent, which keep only HCP's own constraints; where a lint needs a
declared bound it is the request's own 16 MiB document bound. The category
pattern is kept (question 54). The spec says so, with a new example of such an
export and invalid examples for what HCP itself still refuses.

hcp/grants/request: a requested purpose's description is REQUIRED (HCP
6.1.5.2), and the requesting party's name is bounded at 1024, as in the stored
grant.

Every hcp/* schema with size bounds now says they are framework bounds, not HCP
requirements, as is a non-empty requirement HCP does not make; every spec's
field mapping says its payload is closed at the top level where HCP's shapes are
open. Questions 54 (HCP's URI patterns disagree) and 55 (HCP's grant and
delegation schemas disagree) are cross-referenced in the Pending sections of
the specs they touch.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): sign the request and hold examples with authentication

The 32 request examples and the one next-step (hold) example in the 28
hcp/* specifications carried "proofPurpose": "assertionMethod". SPEC §4.7.3
says a producer SHOULD sign a Trust Task document with authentication, and
SHOULD NOT sign with assertionMethod unless the governing specification
defines the document's proof as an attestation (§7.3 item 8). No hcp/*
specification defines a request or a hold that way, and the proof libraries
sign with authentication by default.

The example proofValues are placeholders: every signer is a
did:web:*.example identifier and most values are not base58btc, so no check
verifies them and none is changed. The Rust conformance tests embed the
request examples and are regenerated. The TypeScript, Go and Dart modules
do not carry the examples and regenerate unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Alberto L <alberto_leon@seas.harvard.edu>

* fix(hcp): name the export size refusal hcp/export:tooLarge

SPEC §8.5 rule 2 keeps a family namespace for a code whose meaning is
defined once for the whole family, in a shared convention its
specifications reference, "and never to give a specification-specific code
a broader name than it has earned". hcp:exportTooLarge is declared and
emitted by hcp/export alone, is defined against that task's own
maxDocumentBytes bound, and is, as the specification says, not an HCP
error. Unlike hcp:invalidToken, hcp:versionConflict and
hcp:credentialInvalid, it maps no HCP Core error (HCP 5.5). It takes the
task's own slug as its namespace (§8.5 rule 1): hcp/export:tooLarge, the
form four vtc/* specifications already use for the same condition.

Renamed in hcp/export's front matter, error text, example and question 33,
and in the shared Export definition's description. The registry build's
namespace check accepts it. Regenerated: the Rust constant is now
hcp::export::v0_1::error_codes::TOO_LARGE, and the description text moves
in the TypeScript, Go and Dart modules.

Signed-off-by: Alberto L <alberto_leon@seas.harvard.edu>

* fix(hcp): say that create and revise carry no top-level member HCP does not define

The request payload roots of hcp/entries/create and hcp/entries/revise are
closed, so a top-level member that HCP does not define is refused, while
HCP's own create and revise request schemas admit one (HCP A.2) and, for
create, the body is an entry whose undefined members a provider preserves
(HCP 4.2, 9.4.3). SPEC §9.4 item 6 has a carriage say what it cannot
express, and neither field mapping did. Each now says so, and names the
nested members that stay open.

Text only: no schema changes, and the four libraries regenerate unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Alberto L <alberto_leon@seas.harvard.edu>

* fix(ts): carry the request's ceremony member onto responses and error responses

respondWith and rejectWithRecipient, and so rejectWith, refuse and the
transport's reject, copied parentThreadId onto the document they build but
not ceremony. A reply built with them left the enactment unless the caller
set the member itself. SPEC §4.11.3 says a producer SHOULD carry the same
ceremony.enactment onto every document of the step it names, "including
any error response", and trust-tasks-rs's respond_with and
reject_with_recipient already clone the member. The TypeScript builders now
do the same: the answer gets its own copy, and the member stays absent when
the request has none.

Go and Dart are not changed here. RespondWith and RejectWithRecipient in
trust-tasks-go, and respondWith and rejectWithRecipient in
trust-tasks-dart, also carry parentThreadId only. docs/runtime-parity.md
records the difference as a todo.

Signed-off-by: Alberto L <alberto_leon@seas.harvard.edu>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for the schema-scan fixes

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(rs): allow clippy::unit_arg on the generated spec tree

HCP's reserved subject.relationship is typed "type": "null", as HCP's own
entry schema writes it, so typify emits a () field and builder code that
clippy::unit_arg flags under --all-features. Allow the lint beside the other
typify-output allows in specs/mod.rs.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): carry format uri on the audit event's purpose, and name the consumer's URI check on the slug-or-URI unions

HCP writes an audit event's purpose as anyOf [purposeCode, null], and its
purposeCode carries format: uri. AuditEvent.purpose now has the same shape as
our own PurposeCode (format uri, minLength 1, maxLength, pattern) while still
admitting null, since format constrains only a string. After 0.1 is released a
format change is breaking, so it is made now.

Category, Directive.action and Delegation.relationship admit a slug or an
absolute URI in one pattern, and format: uri would refuse every slug; their
descriptions now say that checking a custom value is a well-formed absolute
URI, as HCP's prose requires, is the consumer's check.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): define the grants/request hold hint

trust-task-next-step says a producer validates a hint against the schema of
the specification its typeUri names, and the hold's { "retryAfter": 5 } had
no schema to validate against. grants/request now defines it as
$defs.NextStepHint, reachable via $anchor "next-step-hint" in the same
payload schema the hold's typeUri names: a closed object whose REQUIRED
retryAfter is a whole number of seconds from 1 to 3600, which the
description distinguishes from trust-task-error's RFC 3339 retryAfter. The
hold's prose names the definition and says a hint that fails is ignored.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): make accessToken optional for an enrolled Management Client

HCP 3.2.3 has a Management Client act under credentials the Authorizing
Principal obtained by authenticating, and no hcp/* task issues a Management
Client token; a wallet paired with the provider proves itself by the request
proof the carriage already requires. accessToken becomes OPTIONAL on the
eighteen governance requests and on hcp/entries/create. With no token, the
provider authenticates the issuer VID by the REQUIRED request proof as a
Management Client the Authorizing Principal enrolled, and refuses any other
issuer with permissionDenied; with one, the token rules, including question
22's binding, apply unchanged. The proof requirement is unchanged.

Recorded as a working assumption pending HCP confirmation (question 56) in
each affected spec. The "Missing accessToken" invalid fixtures of those specs
are removed, since such a payload is now valid. Context Client operations
keep the token REQUIRED.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart libraries for the audit purpose format, the optional accessToken and the hold hint

accessToken is now optional on the governance requests and on
hcp/entries/create (an Option in Rust, a pointer in Go, nullable in Dart and
optional in TypeScript); AuditEvent.purpose carries format uri, which typify
turns into a plain String; and grants/request gains $defs.NextStepHint. The
conformance tests drop the removed "Missing accessToken" fixtures.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): sign the response examples with authentication

SPEC §4.7.3 says a producer SHOULD sign a Trust Task document with
authentication, and SHOULD NOT sign with assertionMethod unless the
governing specification defines the proof as an attestation (§7.3 item 8).
No hcp/* specification does, and the proof libraries, the VTA and Keyring
sign hcp/* responses with authentication. The 13 response example proofs in
12 specifications move to authentication, as do the one request example
added to hcp/import after the request examples moved (its third request).

The six sentences that called the response "a signed assertion any third
party can verify" (audit/read, entries/confirm, entries/query,
entries/restrict-purposes, entries/set-categories, export) now say it is a
statement signed by the provider, which anyone holding the provider's public
key can check came from it, made for authentication and not as an
attestation. The onward-passing rules after them are unchanged.

The repository has no tool that signs spec examples, and the proofValues are
placeholders over did:web:*.example signers that no check verifies, so only
proofPurpose changes. The Rust conformance tests embed the examples and
change at regeneration.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): anchor a provider with no discovery document on its VID

hcp/entries/query required every provider to bind its VID to its HCP
discovery document, and every client to check that binding before sending a
token. A provider that serves the family only over a Trust Task binding may
publish no discovery document: HCP requires one of an implementation that
claims HCP conformance (HCP 19.1), its schema lists at least one of HCP's own
bindings, and the provider may not claim the carriage (question 1). Such a
provider could not meet the rule, and no client could reach it.

entries/query's Parties section now states one rule in two parts. The
client's trust anchor is the provider VID it obtained when the person
connected it (the pairing or QR code, or trust-task-discovery asked of a VID
it already trusts), and it sends a token only to that VID. Where the provider
publishes a discovery document, the existing binding rule applies as well.
The 25 specifications that restate the rule by reference say the same.

hcp/grants/revoked: the notice key is a key the provider VID's DID document
authorizes for the proof's purpose, and must also be in the provider's JWKS
only where the provider publishes a discovery document.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): keep the access token out of a model's context (HCP 10.5)

HCP 10.5 says, for its MCP binding, that the grant is held by the component
that presents credentials and never by the model, that the access token
must not enter the model's context or be returned as tool content (3.11,
invariant 14), and that where the client claims to follow directives the
host applies them. The family moves the token into the document and never
said so.

entries/query's "The access token" section now states the rule for any
agent runtime carrying hcp/*: the token, whether presented or received in a
response, is held by the component that builds and sends the document and
must not enter a model's context or be returned as tool content or in a
tool's result; directives are applied by the host. The 25 other
specifications whose requests carry accessToken cite it from their own
access-token sections.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): say size bounds are not delivery guarantees, a new identity is a new client, and cite HCP 15, 16.2 and 18.1

Size bounds: entries/query's paragraph on the family's framework bounds now
says that they, and every declared maxDocumentBytes, bound what a party
writes and accepts and are not delivery guarantees; a transport or mediator
may cap a message lower (for example at 1 MiB), so a party must not assume
a document within the bound is delivered. hcp/export (14 MiB) and
hcp/import (16 MiB) say the same where they discuss their bound. The TSP
and DIDComm bindings are not changed here: neither has any text on message
size, and they are shared by every family, so a note there belongs in its
own bindings change.

A new identity is a new client: entries/query's Authorization says a grant
identifies its client (HCP 3.11, invariant 3), so a client that moves to a
new VID, or a key it cannot prove continuity with, needs a new grant; a
grant is never moved to another client identity.

HCP 15, 16.2 and 18.1, where they bind: entries/create names the Memory
Manager Profile (detection on every write) and the Health Context Profile's
credential rule for issuer-attested health entries; entries/revise names
detection and re-evaluation on a revision (HCP 15.2, 15.3) and the health
credential rule; hcp/import names detection on each entry it writes and the
health credential rule on import; entries/query and entries/get name the
24-hour use limit for health_context and the rule that an unconfirmed
model-inferred health entry is not disclosed; entries/confirm names the
review of unconfirmed health inferences. Prose only; no schema changes.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(hcp): deny an expired hold in grants/request, never reopen its thread, and link the approval exchange to it

The end of a hold (rule 6): a hold has a lifetime set by provider policy,
and when it passes the policy denies (SPEC §4.13.3 rule 5). The next
resubmission on that thread gets the same permissionDenied, with the same
fixed message, as a decline and an unknown person, so a client cannot tell
an expired hold from either; the provider does not abandon a hold, which
would end it cancelled. A thread that has ended (declined, timed out, or
approved and past its hour) is never reopened, a new ask needs a new
request on a new thread, and the provider remembers an ended thread for at
least as long as it would accept a resubmission on it. The Errors table and
the question 39 entry say the same.

Why a decline is permissionDenied: Errors now says this task does not
exist to produce a decision, so a deny after a declined referral is
permissionDenied (SPEC §4.13.3 rule 2, its last sentence; §8.6), and that
the neutral denial depends on it.

The approval exchange: where the provider asks the person through a Trust
Task exchange of its own, such as task-consent/request, its documents
SHOULD carry parentThreadId equal to the held request's threadId (SPEC
§4.9.2, §4.13.3 rule 3), so the approver can check it against the thread
it was shown. And a client MUST NOT treat a trust-task-next-step as the
response; it resubmits per rule 2 or gives up.

Also in grants/request:
- Parties: the trust anchor is the provider VID the person connected the
  client to; the discovery binding applies where the provider publishes an
  HCP discovery document (as entries/query now says for the family).
- The token is held by the component that sends the client's hcp/*
  documents and never enters a model's context or tool results (HCP 10.5).
- tokenExpiresAt SHOULD equal grant.expiresAt while 0.1 has no refresh
  token, within HCP 13.4's 24-hour maximum and HCP 16.2's 1 hour for
  health_context; the response example now ends the token with the grant.
  The accessToken and tokenExpiresAt schema descriptions say the same
  (description only; the libraries need regenerating).
- The response example is signed for authentication, and the "third-party
  verifiable assertion" sentence now says it is a signed statement by the
  provider, which anyone holding its public key can check came from it, not
  an attestation. The example proofValues are placeholders (did:web
  *.example signers), so only the purpose changes. The Rust conformance
  test embeds the response example and needs regenerating.
- The Pending section links to the list of questions put to the editors.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(hcp): publish the questions put to the HCP editors

The list of questions the hcp/* specs cite by number in their "Pending HCP
confirmation" sections, with the assumption each spec takes, now lives
beside the family's shared schemas as specs/hcp/_shared/0.1/QUESTIONS.md,
as other families keep their shared prose (CONVENTIONS.md, CLAIM-TYPES.md).
It is published with the specs and linked from them.

Questions 37, 46 and 56 open the list. Question 56's assumption adds that
a create with no token is the Management Client's write for the person,
under no grant, and its specs line records that the change has landed.
Questions 25, 36 and 39 point to the spec rules they summarise: the
decline as permissionDenied (SPEC §4.13.3 rule 2), the provider VID as the
trust anchor where there is no HCP discovery document, and an expired hold
denied and never reopened.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(task-consent): show a request typed with the #request fragment

A request's type may be the bare Type URI or carry the #request fragment
(SPEC §4.4.1), and an approver accepts either. Every example used the bare
form, and an implementation that compared the type to it refused the
other. A second request example, with only the REQUIRED members, is typed
with the fragment, so the spec-examples lint and the generated Rust
conformance test exercise both forms. Example only; the Rust conformance
test needs regenerating.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(hcp): link each spec's pending questions to the published list

Every hcp/* spec's "Pending HCP confirmation" section says its question
numbers are those of the list of questions put to the editors; that list
is now a link to specs/hcp/_shared/0.1/QUESTIONS.md.

Signed-off-by…

title: feat(go): add trusttasks.Nullable
body:
Stacked on #1374 (`build/go-floor-1.24`), which raises the Go floor to 1.24 that `omitzero` needs.

Adds `trusttasks.Nullable[T]`, a three-state optional for a member whose schema admits null:
- absent: the zero value;
- null: `trusttasks.Null[T]()`;
- a value: `trusttasks.Value(v)`.

It is read with `IsSet`, `IsNull` and `Get`, and is meant for members tagged `omitzero` (Go 1.24+).
The prebuilt and generated packages adopt it in a later release (PR C).

**Why:** a pointer has two states and these members have three. On `acl/update` 0.3, an absent
`label` leaves the label unchanged, `"label": null` clears it, and a string replaces it. Today a Go
client cannot send "clear".

**Behaviour:**
- **Absent:** an absent `Nullable` is left out by `omitzero`. One that reaches `MarshalJSON` anyway
  (a field without `omitzero`; `omitempty` never omits a struct) is an error, not `null`, because
  `null` would turn "leave it unchanged" into "clear it".
- **For a plain slice or map `T`, only `Null()` writes `null`:** `Value(nil)` writes `[]` or `{}`. This
  matters on `acl/*` `allowedKeys`, where `null` (like absent) means every key in scope and `[]`
  means none: `Value(filtered)` with nothing left in `filtered` must grant no key, not every key.
  The rule differs from `encoding/json`'s nil-slice rule on purpose, and it is settled now because a
  Go tag cannot be retracted. A `T` that encodes itself is left alone and writes a nil value as `T`
  does. That covers `json.RawMessage` and `[]byte` (both write `null`), and any type with
  `MarshalJSON` or `MarshalText` on the value or the pointer. So `Value(json.RawMessage(nil))` still
  writes `null`, and no `[]` or `{}` appears that `T` did not ask for.
- **Member names:** `CheckMemberNames` enters a `Nullable` (an unexported method gives the walk its
  `T`). A member that differs from a declared one only by case, such as
  `{"step":{"x":"a","X":"b"}}`, is refused inside a `Nullable` exactly as it is behind a pointer.
  Before this fix the walk stopped at `Nullable`, because it is a `json.Unmarshaler`, and Go read
  `x = "b"` where every other runtime reads `"a"`.
- **Comparable:** `Nullable[T]` compares with `==` whenever `T` does.
- **Where to use it:** only as a struct field tagged `omitzero`. The type doc warns that each of
  these fails silently, and tests pin each one:
  - behind a pointer, `null` decodes as a nil pointer;
  - nested, a null value and null write the same bytes;
  - as a map value, an absent entry fails the whole encode.

**Breaking:** none. It is a new API, and nothing uses it yet. It is released as core 0.14.0 only
because A's `go!` lands in the same release.

**Tests:** `trusttasks/nullable_test.go` covers the three states, round trips, comparability,
tagging, nil and non-nil slices and maps, the unsupported uses, and nil values of self-encoding
types (`json.RawMessage`, `[]byte`, and named types with `MarshalJSON` on the value or the pointer,
or with `MarshalText`). `trusttasks/membercase_test.go`
covers a `Nullable` over a struct, a slice of structs, a map of structs, a nested `Nullable` and a
`*Nullable`, each refusing a case-variant member as a pointer field does, and null skipped.

title: feat(go): add trusttasks.Nullable (#1375)
body:
feat(go): add trusttasks.Nullable (#1375)

* build(go,go-specs,go-proof,go-didcomm,go-capabilityclient)!: require Go 1.24

Raise the `go` directive from 1.22 to 1.24 in the core, specs, proof,
didcomm and capabilityclient modules and in the two Go examples
(consumer-app-go, getting-started-go). tsp stays at 1.27, the floor it
inherits from affinidi-tsp-go. The go.yml matrices that prove the floor
move from ["1.22", "stable"] to ["1.24", "stable"], and the comments, the
dependabot note, go.md and the go.mod the generator and smoke tests write
for their throwaway modules say 1.24.

1.24 is the first release whose encoding/json honours `omitzero`, which an
optional member that admits null needs in order to be a comparable struct
that is still left out when absent.

A consumer whose toolchain is older than 1.24 and that runs with
GOTOOLCHAIN=local (a distribution's Go, a pinned CI image) can no longer
build these modules; with the default GOTOOLCHAIN=auto the go command
fetches 1.24 itself. Go supports only its two newest releases, and 1.22
and 1.23 are long out of support.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* feat(go): add trusttasks.Nullable

Nullable[T] is an optional member whose schema admits null, with three
states: absent (the zero value), null (Null[T]()) and a value (Value(v)),
read with IsSet, IsNull and Get. acl/update 0.3 is the case that needs
all three: an absent label leaves it unchanged, "label": null clears it.

It is a struct with unexported fields, so Nullable[T] compares with ==
whenever T does. IsZero reports absent, so a member tagged `omitzero`
(Go 1.24 and later) is left out; null writes null and a value writes the
value. An absent Nullable that reaches MarshalJSON (a member without
`omitzero`; `omitempty` never omits a struct) is an error rather than a
null, which would turn "leave it unchanged" into "clear it".
UnmarshalJSON reads null as null and anything else as a T.

Nothing uses it yet; the generators move to it separately.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(go): check member names inside a trusttasks.Nullable

CheckMemberNames stopped at any type that decodes itself, and Nullable is
a json.Unmarshaler, so a case-variant member inside one went unchecked:
{"step":{"x":"a","X":"b"}} was refused behind a *step and accepted, read
as x = "b", inside a Nullable[step]. Nullable decodes a non-null member
with a plain encoding/json decode of T, which matches names without
regard to case, so the check has to follow it there.

Nullable now tells the walk its T through an unexported method, and the
walk enters it before the Unmarshaler short-circuit, skipping null. The
tests cover a struct, a slice of structs and a map of structs, each
refused as the same member behind a pointer is.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(go): write a nil slice or map in a trusttasks.Nullable as empty, never null

Value(nil) with a slice or map T wrote null, as encoding/json writes a nil
slice. With Null() there to say null, that mapping is only a trap: on
acl/* allowedKeys null (like absent) means every key and [] means none,
so Value(filtered) with nothing left in filtered granted every key. Only
Null() writes null now; Value(nil) writes [] or {}.

The type doc says so, warns against a Nullable behind a pointer, nested
or as a map value (each fails silently, and a test pins each), and its
example uses a local type rather than the acl/update payload, whose
Nullable member only exists once the prebuilt packages adopt it.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(go): leave a self-encoding T's nil value to T in a trusttasks.Nullable

The nil-to-empty rule chose by kind alone, so it overrode T's own
encoding: Value(json.RawMessage(nil)) wrote [] where RawMessage writes
null, Value([]byte(nil)) wrote [] where an empty []byte writes "", and a
named slice with its own MarshalJSON lost it. Each can make a document
schema-invalid or change what it says.

The rule now applies only to a plain slice or map: not []byte, and with
no MarshalJSON or MarshalText on T or *T. Anything else writes a nil
value as encoding/json writes T. The type doc says so, and a test covers
RawMessage, []byte, and named types encoding through MarshalJSON (on the
value and on the pointer) and MarshalText.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
Co-authored-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: build(go,go-specs,go-proof,go-didcomm,go-capabilityclient)!: require Go 1.24
body:
Raises the `go` directive of every released Go module to 1.24: the core, `specs`, `proof`,
`didcomm` and `capabilityclient`, plus the two Go examples. `tsp` is unreleased and already on
1.27.

**Why:** 1.24 is the first release whose `encoding/json` honours `omitzero`. `trusttasks.Nullable`
(the next PR) relies on it, so that an optional member which admits null can be a comparable struct
that is still left out when absent. Go supports only its two newest releases, and 1.22 and 1.23 are
long out of support.

**What changed:**
- the `go` directive in each `go.mod`;
- every `go.yml` matrix that proves the floor, from `["1.22", "stable"]` to `["1.24", "stable"]`,
  and the comments beside them;
- the dependabot note, `docs/packages/go.md`, and the `go.mod` that `gen_test.go` and
  `smoke/smoke_test.go` write for their throwaway modules.

**Breaking:** a consumer whose toolchain is older than 1.24 and that builds with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`
(a distribution's Go, or a pinned CI image) can no longer build these modules. With the default
`GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`, the go command fetches 1.24 itself. Each of the five modules takes a minor
bump: core 0.14.0, `specs` 0.2.0, and `proof`, `didcomm` and `capabilityclient` one minor each.

**Release order:** this PR and the `trusttasks.Nullable` PR stacked on it go into the same Release PR; the full order is in the nullable-bindings PR.

title: build(go,go-specs,go-proof,go-didcomm,go-capabilityclient)!: require Go 1.24 (#1374)
body:
build(go,go-specs,go-proof,go-didcomm,go-capabilityclient)!: require Go 1.24 (#1374)

Raise the `go` directive from 1.22 to 1.24 in the core, specs, proof,
didcomm and capabilityclient modules and in the two Go examples
(consumer-app-go, getting-started-go). tsp stays at 1.27, the floor it
inherits from affinidi-tsp-go. The go.yml matrices that prove the floor
move from ["1.22", "stable"] to ["1.24", "stable"], and the comments, the
dependabot note, go.md and the go.mod the generator and smoke tests write
for their throwaway modules say 1.24.

1.24 is the first release whose encoding/json honours `omitzero`, which an
optional member that admits null needs in order to be a comparable struct
that is still left out when absent.

A consumer whose toolchain is older than 1.24 and that runs with
GOTOOLCHAIN=local (a distribution's Go, a pinned CI image) can no longer
build these modules; with the default GOTOOLCHAIN=auto the go command
fetches 1.24 itself. Go supports only its two newest releases, and 1.22
and 1.23 are long out of support.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
Co-authored-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
