trust-tasks-tsp reports binding URI https://trusttasks.org/binding/tsp/0.3
(the envelope type stays the tsp/0.1 one) and refuses a message in a TSP
MAJOR other than 1 as the new TspError::UnsupportedTspVersion, read from the
version marker before any key is used, instead of TspError::Upstream. New
advertised_sender() reads the cleartext sender and refuses a draft before the
caller resolves the sender; new TSP_VERSION ("1.0"). The rustdoc no longer
describes the draft's HPKE-Auth seal. Adding a variant to TspError and
changing which variant a draft message produces is a break of this crate's

title: feat(bindings): tsp 0.3 — require TSP 1.0
body:
## What

A new transport binding version, `bindings/tsp/0.3`, that requires TSP 1.0. It is `tsp/0.2` plus:

- **§2.2 TSP version.** A producer sends a TSP 1.0 message (`YTSP-BAA`). A consumer refuses a message whose TSP MAJOR is not 1 (the Rev 2 `YTSP-AAB` and Rev 3 `YTSP-AAC` drafts among them) before using any key or resolving the sender, does not answer it (nothing in it is authenticated), and should report it to the operator as a version mismatch. A consumer never refuses on the TSP MINOR: an unknown 1.x MINOR is not a version refusal.
- **§4** gains the matching error-mapping row, and the `errored` row of §4.1 counts it among the conditions that produce no reply.
- **§7** attributes sender authentication to the TSP signature plus the ESSR sender check (TSP 1.0 receiver procedure, step 7), because TSP 1.0's HPKE-Base mode does not authenticate the sender itself. 0.2's wording ("HPKE authenticated encryption binds the sender's static key") described the draft.
- **TSP references** point at TSP 1.0 ([tswg-tsp-specification@ccda6b3](https://github.com/trustoverip/tswg-tsp-specification/tree/ccda6b33159d860f05c328eb436dabe83548b705/spec)). Section numbers were checked against the 1.0 text and are given with the section names.
- **§9.1 Changes from 0.2**, with 0.2's own change list kept as §9.2.

Unchanged: the envelope type (`binding/tsp/0.1/envelope`), the envelope object including `deliveryId`, and every Trust Tasks rule. `tsp/0.3` is registered in `website/assets/bindings.js` with `implementations: []`. `tsp/0.2` is left as published. Like earlier binding versions, it counts as superseded because a later MINOR exists on disk (the same way `checkBindingErrorSpecPin` and the stale-references check treat it).

## Why

`tsp/0.2` cites the TSP Implementers Draft (Rev 2) and names no TSP version normatively. With #1387 (TypeScript) and #1388 (Go and Dart), all four libraries speak TSP 1.0 and refuse the drafts, so the binding describes a TSP version that nothing here implements. TSP has no version negotiation, so a Rev 2 implementation and a 1.0 implementation cannot exchange a single message.

That changes which messages conform. It is a wire change, not an editorial one, so it gets a new version rather than a note in 0.2. It is a MINOR because the binding is at `draft` status (SPEC §5.2 allows a breaking change to a draft artifact as a MINOR, the same reasoning `didcomm-v1/0.2` used). §9 of 0.3 says so explicitly.

## Not in this PR (follow-up)

The libraries' binding URIs do **not** move here. Every TSP package still reports `https://trusttasks.org/binding/tsp/0.1`: Rust `BINDING_URI`, TS `BINDING_URI`, Go `BindingURI` and Dart `bindingUri`, plus their READMEs and doc comments. The `implementations` list in `bindings.js` stays under `tsp/0.1`. A separate cross-library PR will move all four to `tsp/0.3` and move the `implementations` entry with them. It will keep the envelope type at `tsp/0.1/envelope` and add a runtime-parity row.

## Checks

Run locally on this branch (Node 24):

- `npm run validate`: passes. Stale references: 0. Binding framework target and error-spec pin checks: clean.
- `npm run check-bindings`: passes (all four libraries agree).
- `npm run build`: passes. `checkBindingRegistry` sees the new entry, and the site copies `website/bindings/tsp/0.3`.

No library regeneration: nothing under `specs/` changed. Bindings are prose plus the `bindings.js` registry, and no generator reads them.

title: fix(go-tsp,dart-tsp): speak TSP 1.0 on affinidi-tsp-go v0.2.0 and affinidi_tsp 0.2
body:
## Why

The Rust TSP binding (`affinidi-tsp` 0.5), the TypeScript binding (#1387, `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js` 0.4), the VTA and Keyring all speak **TSP 1.0** (`YTSP-BAA`). The Go and Dart bindings were still on **TSP Rev 3** (`YTSP-AAC`). TSP has no version negotiation, so Go and Dart could not exchange a single message with any of them.

Both Rev 3 pins were stopgaps "until published":

- Go required `affinidi-tsp-go` at an untagged Rev 3 pseudo-version (`d32ca7cd`, "Bump to a real tag when one is published"). Tag **v0.2.0** (2026-11-23) is TSP 1.0 (its CHANGELOG: "Packs `YTSP-BAA` … `Peek` and `Open` refuse every MAJOR but 1").
- Dart overrode `affinidi_tsp` to a git commit (`5b1cb003`) "until it is published to pub.dev". **0.2.0–0.2.3** are on pub.dev, and 0.2.0 is "TSP 1.0 (YTSP-BAA); refuse Rev 3 and earlier drafts, require the ESSR sender".

I checked that the pins had no other reason. #485 and #486 give only "not tagged / not on pub.dev". The pin lines never changed after they were introduced, and neither upstream changelog shows a workaround or API need. The old Dart commit predates two upstream hardening fixes that the published releases carry: "harden TSP message processing" and "fail closed before resolving unauthenticated senders".

This also **unblocks the releases**. The Dart override was what made `trust_tasks_tsp` unpublishable, because a release deletes the override and `dart pub get` then fails on a git-only dependency. Go's release was waiting on a tagged `affinidi-tsp-go`.

## What changes

**Go (`trust-tasks-go/tsp`)**
- Requires `github.com/affinidi/affinidi-tsp-go v0.2.0`, plus `x/crypto` 0.59.0 and `x/sys` 0.50.0 after `go mod tidy`. The `go` directive stays `1.27`, because v0.2.0 still declares 1.27. The `go.mod` comment is rewritten.
- New `TSPVersion = "1.0"` and `FailUnsupportedTSPVersion` (string `unsupportedTspVersion`, the same name as TS).
  - A message whose TSP MAJOR is not 1 is refused from its version marker (`Peek`), before `Open`, whatever sender identity is passed, nil included. `Open` validates the sender before it reads the version, so without the `Peek` a draft would only be classified after sender resolution.
  - MINOR never gates a message (TSP §9.1). A 1.x message with an unknown MINOR that fails to open is `FailNotForThisReceiver`, as in #1387.

**Dart (`trust_tasks_tsp`)**
- `affinidi_tsp: ^0.2.0` from pub.dev, and the git override is gone. `pubspec_overrides.yaml` now holds only the in-tree `trust_tasks`, with the same text as the other siblings.
- The SDK floor rises **3.8 → 3.10**, the floor `affinidi_tsp` 0.2 sets. The `trust-tasks-dart-tsp` floor leg in `dart.yml` moves from 3.8 to 3.10.
- New `tspVersion = '1.0'` and `TspFailure.unsupportedTspVersion`. The version is checked first in `unpackTrustTask` and in `TspConsumer.receive`, before the allowlist and sender resolution: a draft message names no sender that `advertisedSender` can read. MINOR behaves as in Go.

**What breaks**
- **On the wire, for both packages:** a Go or Dart peer still on Rev 3, or any Rev 2 peer, can no longer exchange messages with these packages in either direction. Upgrade both ends.
- **API:** only additions. One new constant and one new failure value in each package. Adding a Dart enum value would break an exhaustive `switch` on `TspFailure`, but neither package has ever been released (no `trust-tasks-go/tsp/*` tag, and `trust_tasks_tsp` is not on pub.dev), so no consumer can observe it.
- **No `!`:** neither package is in a bump script. `go-tsp` and `dart-tsp` are not in commit-lint's `!` package list either, so a `!` would also fail the title check.

**Docs:** both package READMEs, the `trust-tasks-go` module table, `docs/packages/go.md` and `dart.md`, `RELEASING.md`, the `go.yml`, `dart.yml` and `publish.yml` comments, the `website/assets/libraries.js` notes (Go's reader-visible "waits on a tagged affinidi-tsp-go" was no longer true), and a `docs/runtime-parity.md` row for the TSP version.

## Depends on #1387 (one-line rebase)

#1387 adds the "TSP version the TSP binding seals and opens" row to `docs/runtime-parity.md`. It is still open. This PR adds the same row in the same place, with #1387's Rust and TS cells verbatim (from its head `7bd74d477`) and the Go and Dart cells moved to 1.0. Whichever PR merges second has a one-line conflict on that row: keep this PR's Go, Dart and notes cells. The fixtures here are #1387's, copied byte for byte.

## Tests

Each language has a new interop test (`trust-tasks-go/tsp/interop_test.go`, `trust-tasks-dart-tsp/test/interop_test.dart`) over three fixed messages. All three use the same parties: alice signs with the Ed25519 seed `0x01`×32 (X25519 `0x65`×32), and bob's X25519 key is `0x66`×32. The Dart test asserts that the derived public keys equal the ones #1387 records.
- **TSP 1.0, packed by the Rust `affinidi-tsp` 0.5.0.** This is #1387's `AFFINIDI_TSP_1_0_HEX`. It opens through `UnpackTrustTask` / `unpackTrustTask` and through the consumer, the pipeline runs, and the reply is sealed back in 1.0.
- **Rev 3, packed by `affinidi-tsp-go` `d32ca7cd`** (new). This is the library this module used before, standing for an un-upgraded Go or Dart peer here. A throwaway program packed it and opened it with that library first. It is refused `unsupportedTspVersion` (with the right sender, with a nil sender in Go, and through the consumer, without the handler running), and `AdvertisedSender` returns nothing for it.
- **Rev 2, packed by `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js` 0.2.0.** This is #1387's `VTI_TSP_JS_0_2_REV2_HEX`. It is refused the same way.
- **An unknown MINOR:** a 1.0 message with byte 8 set to 5 (TSP 1.5) still frames and names its sender, and is refused `notForThisReceiver`, not as a version mismatch.
- A test checks that our own messages seal in TSP 1.0.

Checks run:
- Go: `go build`, `go vet`, `go test -race -count=1 ./...` and gofmt on go1.27.1 (the `go 1.27` floor) and go1.27.4 (what CI's `1.27` and `stable` legs resolve to).
- Dart:
  - `dart analyze --fatal-infos`, `dart test` (42 tests), and `dart format` at language version 3.10, on 3.10.9 (the floor) and on 3.14.1 (stable).
  - The `downgrade` leg as `dart.yml` runs it: it drops the `trust_tasks` override and runs `dart pub downgrade` (resolving `affinidi_tsp` 0.2.0, `ssi` 3.9.6 and `trust_tasks` 0.12.0), then `dart analyze --fatal-infos lib example`. Clean.
  - All 42 tests also pass with `affinidi_tsp` pinned to 0.2.0.
- Root (Node 24.20.0): `validate`, `check-bindings`, `check-version-edits`, `check-release-lists`, `check-dart-packages`, `check-doc-facts` and `check-sibling-core-ranges` pass. Not run locally: the full `npm run check` and the website build (CI runs them).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **TSP binding text.** `bindings/tsp/0.2` cites the TSP Implementers Draft (Rev 2) and names no TSP version normatively, although every implementation now speaks 1.0. A separate change is proposed: a new `bindings/tsp/0.3` pinning TSP 1.0 (MAJOR-only refusal, never on MINOR), rather than an in-place note, because the change is not additive at the TSP layer. A related point: all four TSP libraries report `binding/tsp/0.1` as their binding URI, although the latest binding is 0.2. The proposal moves them together to the new version.
- **Release wiring.**
  - Dart: the four release entries (`tag-dart`, `DART_PACKAGES`, the `publish-dart.yml` pattern and case, and the `release-bump-dart.sh` case), the manual first publish, and the website matrix cell.
  - Go: a `publish-go` leg, a `GO_MODULES` entry, `version.go`, and the bump-script and commit-lint scopes.
  - Nothing upstream blocks either any more.

* fix(go-tsp,dart-tsp): speak TSP 1.0 on affinidi-tsp-go v0.2.0 and affinidi_tsp 0.2

The Go and Dart TSP bindings move from TSP Rev 3 (YTSP-AAC) to TSP 1.0
(YTSP-BAA), the version the Rust binding, the TypeScript binding (#1387), the
VTA and Keyring speak. TSP has no version negotiation, so a Rev 3 peer and a
1.0 peer cannot exchange messages in either direction.

a message whose MAJOR is not 1 is refused from its version marker, before Open
and whatever sender identity is passed; an unknown 1.x MINOR is not a version
refusal (TSP section 9.1).

title: fix(ts-tsp)!: speak TSP 1.0 on @openvtc/vti-tsp-js 0.4
body:
## What

Moves `@openvtc/trust-tasks-tsp` (`trust-tasks-ts-tsp`) from `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js` `^0.2.0` to `^0.4.0`, so it seals and opens **TSP 1.0** (`YTSP-BAA`, HPKE-Base) messages instead of the Rev 2 draft (`YTSP-AAB`, HPKE-Auth).

- `PackKeys` / `UnpackKeys` (re-exported from vti-tsp-js) drop `senderEncryptionKey`: HPKE-Base does not use the sender's X25519 key. The consumer stops passing it. `SenderPublicKeys.encryptionKey` stays, since a reply is sealed to it.
- A message from a peer still on a draft (Rev 2 or Rev 3) is refused from its version marker, before sender resolution, as `TspEnvelopeError` with a new failure kind, `unsupportedTspVersion`. The message names the version found. Before, an unreadable frame surfaced as a generic `notForThisReceiver`. Bytes that are not TSP at all stay `notForThisReceiver`, and so does a TSP 1.x message with a MINOR vti-tsp-js does not know that fails to open: MINOR never gates a message (TSP §9.1).
- New export `TSP_VERSION` (`"1.0"`).
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: the note on why `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js` minor updates are held back no longer says the package does not compile on 0.4.
- The package README, `docs/packages/typescript.md` and `docs/runtime-parity.md` (a new row for the TSP version each binding speaks) are updated.

### Why `!`

vti-tsp-js 0.4 speaks TSP 1.0 only. Its README says it refuses any MAJOR but 1, including both drafts (Rev 2 and Rev 3), because TSP has no version negotiation. So this is a wire break for every peer of this package, and a compile break for a caller passing `senderEncryptionKey` in a `PackKeys`/`UnpackKeys` literal. Per DEVELOPMENT.md ("judge a library bump by what a consumer observes"), that is a break of this package's API. It is scoped to `ts-tsp` only, so no other package moves. No version or CHANGELOG edits: the Release PR does those.

## Why

Keyring and the VTA (`affinidi-tsp`, vta-service v0.79+) speak TSP 1.0, and the Rust `trust-tasks-tsp` crate (`affinidi-tsp` 0.5) does too. The TypeScript binding read only the old format, so an agent built on it could not reach today's VTA. This was found in Alberto L's review of the HCP work. It was already like this on `main` and is not part of the HCP PRs.

## Tests

- **TSP 1.0 interop:** `test/fixtures.ts` holds a Direct message packed by the **Rust `affinidi-tsp` 0.5.0** (the version `trust-tasks-tsp` resolves in `Cargo.lock`). It carries the binding's `{type, document}` envelope and was sealed with the test parties' fixed keys. A throwaway Rust program produced it through `affinidi_tsp::message::direct::pack(…, MessageType::Direct, …)`, the call `trust-tasks-tsp`'s `pack_trust_task` makes, and unpacked it with the same crate before printing it. The tests check that it declares 1.0, then open it with `unpackTrustTask` and run it through `TspConsumer` (handled, and the reply seals back and opens).
- **Old peers:** a Rev 2 message packed by `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js` 0.2.0 (this package's previous dependency) is refused by `unpackTrustTask` and by `TspConsumer.receive` as `unsupportedTspVersion`, naming `Rev 2 (YTSP-AAB)`. The consumer refuses it without calling `resolveSender`.
- What this package seals declares TSP 1.0 (`peekRevision`).
- A 1.0 message with its MINOR changed to 5 (so it no longer verifies) is `notForThisReceiver`, not `unsupportedTspVersion`, through both `unpackTrustTask` and `TspConsumer`.
- Run locally on Node 24: `trust-tasks-ts-tsp` `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck:test` and `npm test` (26/26 pass). At the root, the full `npm run check` passes.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Dart:** `trust_tasks_tsp` overrides `affinidi_tsp` to git commit `5b1cb003`, which is **Rev 3** (`YTSP-AAC`) and refuses 1.0 messages. `affinidi_tsp` is now on pub.dev at 0.2.x, described as TSP 1.0. Moving to it (widening `affinidi_tsp: ^0.1.0` in `pubspec.yaml`) would also let the git override go, which is what blocks publishing `trust_tasks_tsp` (RELEASING.md).
- **Go:** `trust-tasks-go/tsp` requires `affinidi-tsp-go` at pseudo-version `v0.0.0-20260916130837-d32ca7cdde20`, which is **Rev 3** and refuses 1.0. `affinidi-tsp-go` has since tagged `v0.2.0` with TSP 1.0. Moving to it would also unblock that module's first release.
- **Rust:** none. `affinidi-tsp` 0.5 already speaks 1.0 and refuses the drafts.
- **Binding text:** `bindings/tsp/0.2/spec.md` still cites the TSP Implementers Draft (Rev 2). Changing the TSP version the binding names is a wire change on the outer layer, so it needs its own decision: a new `bindings/tsp/0.3`, or an explicit note. No CI check or DEVELOPMENT.md rule ties it to this library change (the binding-prose rules cover the framework target and the error-spec pin), so it goes in a separate PR.
- Re-lock the TS HCP demo once it lands.

title: ci(rs): adaptive swap for the test, test-validate and clippy jobs
body:
## Problem

The Rust jobs that compile trust-tasks-rs with every spec family are being killed, not failed: `cargo clippy (--all-features)` on #1380, #1381, #1382 and #1385, and on #1385 also `cargo test (stable, full workspace)` and `cargo test (trust-tasks-rs, --features validate)`, end with exit 143 ("The runner has received a shutdown signal") and no compile error. main itself is right at the edge.

## Measurements

Peak RSS of the largest single process (`/usr/bin/time -v`), measured on an 8-core, 30 GiB Linux machine with the same commands and environment as `rust.yml` (`CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, `-D warnings`, 4 jobs, warm dependencies):

| branch | clippy --all-features | test (workspace, all-specs) | test-validate |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (ccb265eeb) | 22.9 GiB | 22.9 GiB | 22.9 GiB |
| HCP suite, #1380 (186773c97) | 23.8 GiB | not run | not run |
| #1385 (013eeac83) | 25.2 GiB | 25.2 GiB | 25.2 GiB |

- The peak is one rustc process, the compile of trust-tasks-rs with every family, which all three jobs share. It is in the compiler front end (type checking and borrow checking of the serde derive output), not in LLVM.
- `-j 1` saves nothing: clippy on the HCP suite peaks at 23.76 GiB with `-j 4` and with `-j 1`.

## The runner

`ubuntu-24.04` hosted runners have 16 GiB of RAM. `add-swap mode: fixed` adds a 10 GiB swapfile but leaves systemd-oomd running, and in practice the job is killed at about 23 GiB: main (22.9) passes, the HCP suite (23.8) and #1385 (25.2) do not.

## The change

`test`, `test-validate` and `clippy` switch to `add-swap mode: adaptive`, as `doc`, `package` and `semver` already use. Adaptive stops systemd-oomd and adds up to 16 GiB of swap (leaving 8 GiB of disk free), about 32 GiB in total, which gives 7 to 9 GiB of headroom over what we measured. The comments beside the step and the action's description are updated to match. `mode: fixed` now has no users; I left it in the action rather than widen this PR.

Cost: when the peak pages out, those jobs get slower. They already have 90-minute timeouts.

This should merge before #1380, #1381, #1382 and #1385, so their Rust jobs can pass. The jobs on this PR run on main's code, so they are a check that adaptive swap doesn't break anything, not of the larger peaks.

@stormer78, could you review this when you have a moment? It changes CI for every Rust PR, so I'd rather it had a maintainer's eyes. The longer-term plan (CI matrix by feature group, then the milestone 5 removal of the prebuilt modules), and a note on the published crate's size, are in #1392.

title: fix(devices): read the device/register 0.2 `binding` envelope
body:
Fixes #636.

## Problem
`device/register/0.2` responds with `{ "binding": DeviceBinding }`, which is what the VTA sends (`vta-service/src/operations/device.rs`). `parse_binding` only looked under `device` or at the top level, so the first launch after setup logged `WARNING: device registration failed: VTA contract mismatch: device registration returned no binding` even though the registration had succeeded. That launch also never learned its own `deviceId`, which `live_siblings` falls back to for VTAs whose rows lack `consumerDid`.

## Fix
Read `binding` first. The `device` envelope and the bare record are kept as fallbacks for older VTAs.

## Tests
- Spec `binding` envelope parses
- Legacy `device` envelope and bare record still parse
- A response with no binding still returns `None`, so it is still reported as a contract mismatch

`cargo test -p openvtc-core --lib devices`: 30 passed. `cargo clippy -p openvtc-core --all-targets`: clean.

## Checklist (vti-stack-development-guide)
- R3.6: response shape checked against the current spec bundle and VTA source
- R6.4: a reply that really has no binding still surfaces as a contract mismatch

title: fix(rooms): pnm reads a room's file at rooms/records/get/0.3, as its other reads do
body:
Leftover from the vtc-mcp / vtc-client version audit (#2831, #2834): `vta-cli-common`'s room file download asked only `rooms/records/get/0.2`.

## Change
- **`pnm rooms file get`** (`vta-cli-common/src/commands/rooms/files.rs`): asks `rooms/records/get/0.3` through the member's VTA (`rooms/keys/act/0.11`), falling back to 0.2 only on `unsupportedType`, from the host or from a VTA without act/0.11. The answer is read as `get::v0_3::Response` or `get::v0_2::Response`, whichever version answered, through one macro: no parallel struct.
- **Member-name read** (`records.rs`): it already asked 0.3; it now falls back to 0.2 too.
- **`pnm rooms get`**: already 0.3 with a 0.2 fallback; unchanged.
- **Shared decision:** the fallback rule is now `newest_answer` in `commands/rooms/mod.rs`: reply → answer, `unsupportedType` → older version, any other refusal → that refusal. It's the same rule as vtc-client's `room_task_newest`. That helper lives in vtc-client and talks to the host directly, while these reads go through the VTA's `act`, so they share the rule rather than the code.
- **Docs:** `docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md` says which version these reads use and why.

## Why not get/0.4
No published `rooms/keys/act` version (0.8–0.12, the newest on trusttasks.org) lists `rooms/records/get/0.4` in its table, so a VTA cannot relay it for the CLI; serving it would need a spec change (an act 0.13) first. Its one addition is an optional `purpose`, which these reads do not name. The VTA's own `rooms/keys/read/0.3` already passes a named purpose to the host as get/0.4.

## Tests
- `only_an_unserved_version_falls_back`: reply → answer; `unsupportedType` → older version; `permissionDenied` / `notFound` / a task-specific code → that refusal, never retried.
- `a_record_reads_as_the_version_that_answered`: a 0.3 answer reads as 0.3 (file members intact) and is refused as 0.2.
- `cargo nextest -p vta-cli-common -p pnm-cli -p cnm-cli` 521/521, `cargo test -p vta-cli-common --doc`, clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, fmt, `check-docs.py`.

title: fix(step-up): answer a relying party's step-up as the identity that signed in
body:
Follow-up to #456. With the control plane now accepted as the step-up's executor, a holder signed in to the did-hosting console as a **per-site persona** was refused at the next check:

> step-up approve-request refused: it is addressed to did:webvh:…:glenn-vta, not this wallet

## Why
The persona is the session's subject: `auth/authenticate` was signed as it, through the VTA. The control plane addresses the approve-request to the subject and accepts a decision only from it (`approve_response`: `approver != pending.subject` → `approverUnauthorized`). The wallet always answered with its own `did:key`, so a persona session could never be stepped up.

## Change
- **Background:** `handleApproveSessionStepUp` decides the identity the way sign-in does: `stepUpIdentity` → `decideSiteIdentity`. It never raises the picker, and the page can't name the entry. It passes the vault `entryId` (plus `restBaseUrl`) to the offscreen.
- **Offscreen:** `doApproveSessionStepUp` signs as that persona through the VTA (`personaTaskSigner`). With no persona, the holder key answers, unchanged.
- **VTA purpose:** `vault/sign-trust-task` signs `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7` for `assertionMethod` (vta-sdk `purpose_for_document_type`, `ATTESTATION_SLUGS`; covered by vta-service `vault_sign_trust_task_purpose.rs`).
- **Core:** `buildStepUpApproval` / `performRpStepUp` / `verifyRpStepUpRequest` take a `ChannelSigner` (a local key or a `TaskSigner`) instead of a bare `SigningIdentity`. The signature now goes through `asTaskSigner(...).sign(doc, { proofPurpose: "assertionMethod" })`.
- **Docs:** `CLAUDE.md` records the rule and what would break it.

## Verified
- **Against a live control plane** (webvh.storm.ws, persona `glenn-vta`): the control plane logged `step-up approved: session elevated to aal2`. The session renewal that follows failed for an unrelated control-plane reason, fixed separately in affinidi-webvh-service.
- **Tests:** core `tests/rp-login.step-up.mjs` adds two: a persona session is answered by the persona, signed for `assertionMethod`; the holder key can't answer a persona's step-up. Core 1350 pass and extension 1612 pass.
- **Build:** `npm run build` succeeds, and the CI bundle guards pass locally.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): the persona signs through the existing VTA session (`getVtaSession`)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): nothing written
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): internal background→offscreen message only (`entryId`, `restBaseUrl`, optional, background-set)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): a vault lookup failure refuses the step-up
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutations
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(vtc): the portal's room stops re-reading itself in a loop
body:
Reported in First Room: the chat window kept refreshing, with messages appearing and disappearing.

## Cause
`room-live.ts` acknowledged `read(v)` where `v = highestVersion(view.records)`, the highest record the page *shows*. Reactions, `memberProfile` names, edits and withdrawals are folded into the messages they concern by the wallet's reading rules, so they are never among the shown records. When the room's newest record is one of them (here a reaction), `v` is below the room's version, and the host fires again immediately for a room already past the watermark (`vti-rooms` watch: `a_room_already_past_the_watermark_fires_at_once`). The page then re-reads, acknowledges the same stale `v`, and the loop never ends.

## Fix
Track the `changed` event's `latestVersion` and acknowledge `max(latestVersion, read, held)`. Re-arming after `closed` and after `lapsed` starts from the same value. The `vtc-service/CLAUDE.md` portal-rooms entry now states the rule.

## Test
`a room whose newest record is folded away (a reaction) is acknowledged at the room's version, so the watch does not fire forever`: fails without the fix (acknowledges 4, never 9), passes with it. Admin UI 1667/1667, lint, `check-docs.py`.

title: fix(vtc): the portal's room stops re-reading itself in a loop (#2835)
body:
fix(vtc): the portal's room stops re-reading itself in a loop (#2835)

In a live room the page re-read the conversation over and over. After each
change the page told the wallet's watch the highest version it had read — the
highest record it shows. But the page's records are not every record:
reactions, member names, edits and withdrawals are folded into the messages
they concern. Once the room's newest record was one of those (a reaction, say),
the version acknowledged sat below the room's, the host fired again at once for
a room already past it, and the page read, acknowledged the same stale version,
and was fired again — forever.

The watch's `changed` event carries the room's `latestVersion`. The page now
acknowledges the highest of that, what it read and what it holds, and starts a
renewed watch from it too.

title: feat(rooms): a member may let a portal send messages and reactions in a room without asking while it is open
body:
Requested by the user: a portal chat should not need a confirm window for every message while the member is in the room.

## What
A message's or reaction's confirm offers an **unticked** box: "Send messages and reactions in <room> without asking while this room is open in <portal>". Ticking it creates a **session grant** (`src/room-session-grant.ts`), the second bounded exception to "every page write is confirmed", after #455's reaction grant.

## Lifetime: what "while this room is open" means
- **Bound to one page document:** `tab.id` plus the browser's `documentId` (`pageSessionOf`), read from the `sender` of both the `rooms.*` call and the `ROOM_WATCH_PAGE_PORT`. A reload or navigation is a new document and asks again.
- **Open = holding a watch:** the grant lives only while that document holds a watch port on that room (`roomOpened`, counted per document and room). The portal's room page keeps one open while it shows the room and `stop()`s it on leaving. The last port closing ends the grant: leaving the room, closing the tab, reloading, navigating away, or the extension's background worker being stopped.
- **Also ends on:** `tabs.onRemoved`; the share ending (`reviewSessionGrants` on any share-storage change); 30 minutes with no write under it; 8 hours from the confirm however used; the wallet locking (`RUNTIME_LOCK_WALLET`); Stop in the console.
- **Offered only while the room is open** in the asking document, so nothing ever lacks an end.

## Scope
- **Covered:** `putMessage` (replies too), `react` and `unreact` for the same origin, community, VTA, room and member.
- **Never covered:** notes, files, any other write.
- **Gates still apply:** gates 1–3, `recordMembersNotListed` and value validation.
- **Rate limit:** more than 10 writes in a rolling minute, or a message over 4,000 characters, is confirmed as usual and the grant stays. `MAX_BODY` is 1 MiB and already refuses outright, so a chat-sized bound is used instead.

## Visibility
- **Storage:** held in the background's memory only, never stored.
- **Action icon:** while any grant is live, the tooltip names the rooms and the badge reads **LIVE** (green). It ranks below a waiting approval and above the room-offers count.
- **Console:** the Communities tab shows "Sends without asking while open · Stop" beside the share, via `RUNTIME_ROOM_SESSION_GRANTS` (extension pages only).
- **Page:** it can't ask for, see or extend a grant; the page contract is unchanged. `sessionGrant` crosses the consent window only with an approval, from a prompt that offered it.

## Deviations
- **Grant ends with the background worker:** a grant ends if Chrome stops the extension's background worker. The page's 20 s ping keeps it alive in a visible tab; in a tab hidden for more than 5 minutes the worker can stop, which drops the port, so the member is asked again. Storing the grant to survive that would detach it from the open-room signal, so the grant ends by design.
- **Reload ends it** (the default in the brief): a reload is a new `documentId`.

## Rules
`CLAUDE.md`: gate 4, the "no remember" sentence and the reaction-grant section now name this exception precisely. "What breaks it" adds: widening the grant to notes, files or other writes; letting it outlive the document (storing it, keying it by tab alone); lifting its idle limit, cap or rate limit; removing the badge or tooltip; renewing it without a confirm.

## Tests
`tests/room-page-session-grant.test.mts`, 11 tests:
- The box is offered only while the room is open.
- Only the box grants; a denial grants nothing, including at the consent window.
- Covered writes skip the window; notes are still confirmed.
- Another room, member, origin, VTA, tab or reloaded document asks again.
- Each of these ends it: the port closing, two ports closing (the last one ends it), tab close, lock, Stop, share revoked, 30 min idle, 8 h cap.
- The rate limit and long message fall back to the confirm while keeping the grant.
- The badge is notified on start and end.

Lint, build and `check-task-versions` pass; all workspace tests pass (extension 1623, core 1348).

title: fix(step-up): signing in to a relying party enrolls it for its own step-ups
body:
A holder signed in to a did-hosting control plane is refused on the first privileged change (e.g. saving an ACL entry):

> step-up approve-request refused: signed by did:webvh:…:webvh.storm.ws, not an executor this wallet is enrolled with

The only way through was pasting the control plane's DID into **Options → Enrolled executor DIDs**, and nothing pointed there.

## Why the requirement protected nothing here
Before the offscreen verifies anything, an RP session step-up has already passed these checks:
- **Sign-in pin:** the background refuses unless the step-up's `rpDid` is the RP DID the page's origin was pinned to by a sign-in the human approved (`pageStepUpBindingRefusal`).
- **Signer:** `verifyRpStepUpRequest` requires the approve-request to be signed by that `rpDid`.
- **Scope:** the approve-response is addressed to that RP and bound to its own session's single-use challenge, so it can only elevate that RP's own session.

The human already confirmed this RP at the login prompt. Requiring it a second time in settings added a refusal the human couldn't act on.

## Change
- **`page-task-policy.ts`:** new `rpStepUpExecutorDids(enrolled, pinnedRpDid, rpDid)`. It returns the enrolled set, plus the pinned RP only when it equals `rpDid`.
- **`background.ts`:** after the binding check passes, passes the pin it read as `signedInRpDid` on `OffscreenApproveSessionStepUpRequest`. It is set by the background, never by the page.
- **`offscreen.ts`:** `doApproveSessionStepUp` feeds `rpStepUpExecutorDids(...)` to `performRpStepUp`.
- **Unchanged:** executor-initiated pushes (task consent, disclosure step-up) arrive from no origin and still use the enrolled set alone.
- **`options.tsx`:** the help text says signed-in sites are enrolled automatically.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** records the rule and what would break it.

## Tests
- **New:** extension `tests/page-rp-binding.test.mts` adds 3 tests: pinned RP added when it matches, not added for another RP, unchanged with no pin.
- **Suite:** full extension suite, 1603 pass.
- **Build:** `tsc -b` and `npm run build` succeed, and the CI bundle guards (admin, key-material, persona, mediator URIs) pass locally.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no network code touched
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): no state written
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): internal background→offscreen message only (`signedInRpDid`, optional)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): no pin means no widening
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutations
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: feat(vtc-client): room tasks ask the newest version the host serves
body:
Follow-up to #2831's audit: `vtc-client` still asked superseded versions of several room tasks.

## Audit: every Type URI vtc-client names, against what the hosts serve

| URI in vtc-client | Newest pinned | Served by vtc-service / room-host | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rooms/records/put/0.3` (`put_record`, `put_sealed_record_with_blobs`, `put_cleartext_record_v3`) | 0.5 | 0.3, 0.4, 0.5 | Ask 0.5 → 0.4 → 0.3 on `unsupportedType`; new `put_cleartext_record` (0.5); `put_cleartext_record_v3` deprecated |
| `rooms/records/get/0.3` (fallback 0.2) | 0.4 | 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 | Ask 0.4 → 0.3 → 0.2 |
| `rooms/records/list/0.6` (fallback 0.5) | 0.8 | 0.5 – 0.8 | Ask 0.8 → 0.6 → 0.5 |
| `rooms/create/0.2` | 0.3 | 0.2, 0.3 | Ask 0.3 → 0.2 |
| `rooms/watch/0.1` (`watch`, `cancel_watch`) | 0.2 | 0.1, 0.2 | Ask 0.2 (without `live`, the same one-shot watch) → 0.1 |
| `rooms/info/0.5` → 0.4 → 0.3 | 0.5 | 0.3 – 0.5 | Already current; added 0.4/0.5 to the read-retry list (was missing) |
| `acl/{show,grant,update,revoke}/0.2`, `acl/list/0.3` | 0.3 / 0.4 | VTC serves 0.2 / 0.3 (the newer ones are the VTA's) | Kept |
| `acl/change-role/0.1` (test fixture only) | 0.3 | VTC serves 0.2 | Fixture → 0.2 |
| `trust-task-error/0.1`, `0.3`; `trust-task-discovery/0.4` | framework specs, never pinned | — | Kept (reading what older peers send) |
| Every other URI (groups, boards, elections, badges, members, vetting, policy, git-ns, auth) | Same as used | Served | None |

## How
- One helper, `room_task_newest`: ask each version in turn, the next only on `unsupportedType`; any other refusal is the answer. Used only where the request carries nothing the newer versions added, so an older answer means the same.
- **No silent downgrade:** `put_cleartext_record` checks the record against 0.5, and falls back only to a version whose schema accepts it as given. An open record with `kind` / `inReplyTo` goes to 0.5 or gets the host's refusal back.
- **No public type changes:** `put_sealed_record_with_blobs` and `watch` still return their published types. The answer is read against the version that gave it, then as the published type (every put answers the same members; a one-shot 0.2 watch answers 0.1's).

## Tests
- 5 new tests against a fake host: newest asked first and stops there; fallback order; one-shot watch 0.2 → 0.1; a 0.5-only record is not downgraded; a non-`unsupportedType` refusal is not retried.
- `nextest -p vtc-client -p cnm-cli -p vta-cli-common -p vtc-mcp -p room-host`: 606/606.
- `nextest -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3823 passed.
- `cargo test -p vtc-client --doc`, clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, fmt, `check-docs.py`: clean.
- Docs: the room verb table in `docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md`.

## Not in this PR
`vta-cli-common`'s file download asks `rooms/records/get/0.2` through the member's VTA (`act_and_send`), not through `vtc-client`, so it is left as is.

feat(vtc-client): room tasks ask the newest version the host serves (#2834)

`vtc-client` asked `rooms/records/put/0.3`, `get/0.3`, `list/0.6`,
`rooms/create/0.2` and `rooms/watch/0.1`, each superseded. It now asks
`put/0.5`, `get/0.4`, `list/0.8`, `create/0.3` and `watch/0.2`, and asks again at
the version before only when the host answers `unsupportedType` (one helper,
`room_task_newest`), so a host that predates a version still answers. Every
request still carries only what all those versions accept, so the
older answers mean the same.

`put_cleartext_record` is new: an open room's record checked against
`put/0.5`, so it may carry `kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt` and `editedAt`
(and 0.4's `file`). It falls back only to a version whose schema accepts the
record as given; a record that needs 0.5 gets an older host's refusal back
rather than being sent without its reply or kind. `put_cleartext_record_v3`
is deprecated in its favour. `put_sealed_record_with_blobs` asks the newest
put too; its answer is read against the version that gave it and returned as
the same published type, since every version answers the same members.

Read retries on `429` now also cover `get/0.4`, `list/0.8` and `info/0.4`
and `0.5` (the last two were missing). The admin-action test fixture names
`acl/change-role/0.2`, the version the VTC serves.

body:
Every page write is confirmed in the wallet's own window, so a portal chat asked for a confirm on every emoji (after #454). The user chose a bounded, revocable reaction grant (option A of the review).

## What changes
- **The prompt:** a reaction's confirm is compact (emoji, the message as the wallet read it, who signs) and offers an **unticked** box: "Let <portal> add and remove your reactions in <room> for 30 minutes without asking."
- **Where the grant lives:** `reactionsUntil` on the share itself, so it is keyed exactly as the share is (origin, community, VTA, room, member). It ends with the share: Stop sharing, the page's `forget`, a fresh `choose`, or the share lapsing. It is capped at 30 minutes and at the share's expiry, and never extended by use.
- **While it is live:** `react`/`unreact` from that origin for that room run without a window. Gates 1–3, the value checks and `recordMembersNotListed` still run. Messages, notes and files are always confirmed.
- **Who can grant it:** only that box on an approval. `deliverConsentResult` passes it only with `approved`, and `requestRoomConsent` only from a prompt that offered it. The page can neither request nor see a grant; the page contract is unchanged.
- **Console:** the Communities tab lists a live grant with the minutes left and a Stop, beside Stop sharing.
- **CLAUDE.md:** "no remember" now names this one bounded exception. Widening it (beyond reactions, one room or 30 minutes, or renewing it without the box) is added to "What breaks it".

## Design deviation from the brief
The brief keyed the grant as its own record `(origin, hostDid, vtaDid, roomId, kind=reaction)`. I put it on the share record instead: same key, same storage and revocation by construction, with no second record to keep in step.

## Tests
`tests/room-page-reaction-grant.test.mts` (9):
- the offer, unticked
- only the box grants it, and a denial with the box ticked grants nothing (gates and consent window)
- no window under a live grant

- one room only
- a message or note under a grant is still confirmed
- it ends when stopped, revoked or re-shared
- the key (origin, member) is checked, and it is capped by the share
- a tampered value is no grant

The existing reply/react tests were updated for the offer. Locally: `npm run lint`, `npm test` (extension 1609, core 1348, others) and `npm run build` all pass.

title: fix(vtc): the portal's live room keeps reading while its watch says it is armed
body:
From the review of the wallet's room watch (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#454 + #2828).

The watch path holds up: a dropped port posts `closed`, the page polls and re-watches, a re-arm with the held version fires at once for a room already past it, and lapses are re-armed. The one gap is R6.2-adjacent: `room-live.ts` shows "Live" on `armed`/`fired` and drops it only on lapse, close or failure, so a delivery that breaks **silently** while the watch stays armed (a wedged offscreen mediator session, a host that lost its watch) left the page "Live" and deaf for up to the one-day lease. Hidden tabs make it likelier: Chrome throttles a tab hidden for more than 5 minutes to about one timer a minute, which leaves gaps past the service worker's 30 s idle limit.

## Change
- While the watch is armed, read the room every 5 minutes (`BACKSTOP_READ_MS`) when the tab is visible, and tell the watch what was read.
- Read at once on `visibilitychange` to visible.
- The 20 s fallback poll is unchanged.
- The `vtc-service/CLAUDE.md` portal-rooms entry now says not to remove the backstop.

## Test
`a watch that says it is armed is still backed by a slow read, and the room is read when the tab is seen again`: fails without the change, passes with it. Admin UI 1666/1666, lint, `check-docs.py`.

body:
fix(vtc): the portal's live room keeps reading while its watch says it is armed (#2830)

"Live" in a portal room is derived from the wallet's watch events and drops
on any other event (R6.2). But a watch can stop delivering without saying so
— a wedged mediator session in the wallet, a host that lost the watch — and
then the page showed "Live" and missed updates for up to the watch's one-day
lease. A hidden tab's timers are also throttled to about once a minute, which
lets the wallet's service worker be put to sleep between pings.

While the watch reports itself armed, the page now also reads the room every
five minutes, and at once when the tab is seen again, and tells the watch
what it read. A broken delivery costs minutes, never the lease.

title: feat(vtc): reply, react and live updates in the member portal's room chat
body:
Builds on the restyle (#2826) and the wallet's new room methods (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#454). Every new method is feature-detected; an older wallet keeps today's chat (no reply or react controls, refresh button).

## What a member gets
- **Reply**: hover or focus a message, or tap it on a phone, for Reply and React. The composer shows "Replying to <name>: <excerpt>" with ✕ and sends `putMessage({ …, replyTo: { key, version } })`.
- **React**: a picker (👍 ❤️ 😂 😮 😢 🙏 🎉 👀). Reaction chips are buttons; the member's own is marked and selecting it takes it back (`unreact`). Counts, authors and "yours" come from the wallet's reading, never counted here. The wallet confirms every reply and reaction.
- **Rooms that don't take them** (`recordMembersNotListed`): nothing was written. The page says the room doesn't take replies and reactions yet (an administrator can turn on *Replies and reactions*, #2824), stops offering both, and offers the typed words as a plain message. A reply's target is never dropped silently.
- **Live updates** (`room-live.ts`): `watch` from the highest version held. On `changed` the page reads the conversation again and calls `read(version)`. On `refused`/`unavailable`/`failed` it reads every 20 s while the tab is visible. On `closed` it watches again with backoff (1 s doubling to 60 s). A small **Live** mark replaces the refresh button while armed; it is derived from the latest event and drops on any other (R6.2). "Refresh now" moves into *About this room*.

## Tests
`Rooms.test.tsx`:
- A reply is sent with `replyTo`, and the chip clears.
- `recordMembersNotListed` brings up the notice and "Send as a plain message", which sends without `replyTo`.
- React and un-react go through the wallet with the right arguments, and a refused reaction hides the controls.
- An older wallet shows no controls and keeps the refresh button.
- Watch: subscribe from v4, then armed shows Live, then changed refetches and calls `read(5)`, then refused drops Live; unmount stops the watch.
- `unavailable` falls back to the 20 s timer.

`conversation.test.ts`: reaction value bounds, `reactedWith`, `highestVersion`, `rewatchDelay`.

Local: admin-ui lint clean, vitest 1661/1661, `check-docs.py` passed. No Rust touched.

Checked visually with a throwaway headless-Chrome harness (fake wallet, not committed) at desktop and phone width, light and dark: the actions bar sits beside the bubble on desktop and beneath it on a phone, scrolled into view when opened. Not yet tried against a live wallet.

title: spec(vtc/directory/query): 0.2 answers the member's directory entry
body:
A caller that meets a community member by their DID, such as the author of a record in a data room, can read their projection with `vtc/directory/query`. Every other directory read is addressed by **entry** instead: the member's picture (`images/get`), their entry with shared groups (`entries/show`), and the card a member surface opens. Without the entry identifier, such a caller can name the member but cannot show their picture or open their card. The VTC member portal names a room's authors this way and wants their pictures and a link to their card.

## Changes
- **`vtc/directory/query/0.2`**: 0.1 plus a required `entryId` (directory-card `EntryId`) on every answer, never on a `notFound` and never in a refusal's `details`. Targets framework 0.6.0, with full request and response examples (0.1 had none; its examples-allowlist entries are removed, since the baseline only shrinks).
- **Answer rule:** now stated normatively. An answer is given only where the projection shows the caller the member's DID anyway, to the member themselves, or to an administrator holding `vtc.directory.admin` or `vtc.members.manage`. In every other case the answer is the same `notFound` as for no such member.
- **Security & Privacy:** the entry identifier is not derived from, and does not reveal, any DID. It is answered only to a caller already shown the member, so it links the DID they named to an entry they could open by browsing. It survives a DID rotation, as every other directory read already allows.
- **`entries/show/0.1`:** its "succeeds `query/0.1`" reference is updated by `fix-stale-references`.

The request is unchanged and the response gains a required member, so this is a MINOR increment under §5.2's draft allowance. 0.1 remains published.

## Checks run locally
- `npm run validate` (1431 specs), `npm run build`, `build-bundles` + `check-bundles` (1425)
- Codegen + `cargo fmt`; TS / Go / Dart regenerated; `check-bindings`: all four agree
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features vtc --test conformance`: 758 passed
- `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features --all-targets` with `-D warnings`: clean

title: feat(vtc): administrators set a community room's record members — replies and reactions
body:
**Depends on trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1373 (unmerged).** `vti-specs-vtc` is pinned from a local build of that PR (`trust-tasks.lock` `registry` is a local path). Once #1373 merges and publishes: `trust-tasks -C vti-specs-vtc update` (no `--registry`, so the lock reads `registry = "https://trusttasks.org"`), commit, then mark this ready.

## Why
A community-owned room's profile was written with its label and description only. So a room meant as a conversation started with replies and reactions off, and turning them on took a member holding `curate`. Keyring's maintainers asked for a "Replies and reactions" option in the room form, on by default.

## What
**VTC**: serves `vtc/rooms/community/create/0.6`, `update/0.5`, `get/0.6` beside the earlier versions.
- **create/0.6**: `recordMembers` is written into the profile with the label and description (item 12), echoed in the answer and audited with the create. Absent is none, as in 0.5.
- **update/0.5**: `recordMembers` (the whole set) or `removeRecordMembers: true`. The set compares as a set (item 4), and a record-members-only change re-writes the profile (item 10). Neither given, the read-back's set is carried over as before.
- **get/0.6**: `recordMembers` is what the profile listed at the community's last write, never a pending request's set (item 6).
- **Storage**: `rooms::community_profile` keeps a requested set in a new `#[non_exhaustive]` `RecordMembersRecord` (`room-record-members:<room>`) until a write carries it, then records it as written. `ProfileRecord` is unchanged, so no published struct gains a field. A set requested while a write is in flight is not lost; the room stays pending.
- **Unknown values**: never refused (update item 15).

**Wiring**: conformance table, spine-proof list, admin-UI manifest, `vta_sdk::openapi` wrappers + `routes::openapi_spec`, the OpenAPI snapshot and the console's wire types.

**Console**: a "Replies and reactions" box beside Watch signals.
- Ticked for a new room, sending `kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt`.
- A room's page shows On/Off.
- Edit details sends `recordMembers` / `removeRecordMembers` only when the box changed, keeping any other member a curator listed (e.g. `editedAt`).
- The box notes that members on an older app can't read the room's name and description once these are listed.

**cnm**: `cnm rooms create|update --replies-and-reactions`, `--record-member <m>` (repeat), `update --no-record-members`. `cnm rooms get` reads at 0.6 and prints them.

**Docs**: `docs/03-vtc/community-rooms.md` (new *Replies and reactions* section, console and cnm), `vtc-service/CLAUDE.md`.

## Tests (local)
- New `vtc_rooms_community_record_members_are_set_at_create_read_and_changed`. It covers:
  - create with and without record members
  - get 0.6 vs 0.5
  - an update replacing a curator's set while keeping the curator's other profile members
  - a reorder that changes nothing
  - a rename carrying the set over
  - a pending write, where get answers the last written set and the next write carries the request's
  - remove, and remove again as no change
  - an unknown value kept
  - both members sent at once → `malformedRequest`
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3815/3815
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 7710/7710 (run before the last two fixes below, which touch `cnm-cli` and one VTC test; `-p cnm-cli` re-run: 152/152)
- clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `check-docs.py`, VTC doctests: clean
- admin-ui `npm run lint` and `vitest`: 1644/1644, including the new console tests

Not changed: `vtc-mcp`'s room workflow still creates at `create/0.5`, which stays pinned and served.

title: feat(rooms): a room page can reply, react and be told the room changed (rooms.react, rooms.unreact, rooms.watch)
body:
The VTC member portal shows a room as a conversation and can send a message, but it can't reply, react, or learn the room moved without a refresh button. This adds what the portal needs from the wallet, behind the same gates as every room call: the community's portal by its DID document, and a room the member shared with it.

## Replies and reactions
- `rooms.putMessage({ hostDid, roomId, body, replyTo?: { key, version? } })` writes `inReplyTo`.
- `rooms.react({ hostDid, roomId, key, version?, value })` writes a record of kind `reaction`: the value as `body`, naming the record. That is exactly the shape `assembleRoomRecords` counts.
- `rooms.unreact({ hostDid, roomId, key, value })` writes an empty version over each of the member's own live reactions with that value on that record (`ownReactions` → `withdrawReactionAsMember`, over the version read), which only their author may. Answers `{ withdrawn }`.
- **Room profile check:** before the member is asked, the background reads the room's profile as the member. Where it doesn't list what the write needs (`inReplyTo`; `kind` + `inReplyTo`), the call is refused with a new wallet code, **`recordMembersNotListed`** (added to `page-error.ts` and `docs/page-bridge-errors.md`). A reply is never sent without its `inReplyTo`. Core refuses the same way as a backstop (`RecordWriteRefused.code`).
- **Confirm window:** each write is confirmed, with no "remember", per the existing rule. The window shows the record being answered or reacted to as the wallet read it (`rooms/keys/read`, `glimpseOf`), never the page's description.

## Change signal
- `rooms.watch({ hostDid, roomId, sinceVersion? }, onEvent) → { read(version?), stop() }`.
- **Port:** one `ROOM_WATCH_PAGE_PORT` per watch, relayed by the content script like `roomFile` frames. The background checks the port's attested origin and the share, then holds the watch in one shared `RoomWatcher`, so two tabs share a room's watch.
- **Arming:** armed through the member's VTA (`rooms/keys/watch/0.1`, offscreen `watch` op), and armed again only after a read the page reports.
- **Signal:** the room's `rooms/keys/changed`, taken only from the offscreen document, is passed to the ports that armed it as `{ kind: "changed", latestVersion }` and nothing else, after re-checking the share. Closing the port cancels the watch at the VTA (the last holder).
- **Keep-alive:** the page pings every 20 s to keep the worker alive while it watches. A worker restart closes the port and the page watches again.
- **Not a broadcast:** this deliberately does not use `RUNTIME_BROADCAST_EVENT`, which reaches every tab of every origin.

Older wallets have none of these methods; a page feature-detects them.

## Tests
- core `tests/rooms.reply-react.mjs` (12)
- extension `tests/room-page-reply-react-watch.test.mts` (22): shapes, the profile check before any prompt, confirm contents, share/origin refusals, watch arm/fire/re-arm/cancel, a shared watch, a share withdrawn mid-watch, no VTA support → `unavailable`, offscreen react/unreact/watch, content-script port-name parity
- full gates: `npm run lint`, `npm test` (123 / 1348 / 1600 / 6 / 9, all pass), `npm run build`

title: fix(vtc): the portal key may look a member up by DID, so a room's authors get their names
body:
Follow-up to #2822. In First Room every author still showed as a DID, even Alberto, whose directory card shows the viewer his DID.

## Cause
The portal looks authors up with `vtc/directory/query/0.1`, signed with the portal key the member delegated `vtc/directory` to. The other directory reads (`directory_tasks.rs`) accept that key as its member. `query/0.1` lives in `community_tasks.rs` and went through `member_signer`, which knows only ACL entries, so it answered `permissionDenied: the signer holds no entry in this community`. The portal reads any refusal as "no name". #2822's page test mocked the call, so it didn't catch this.

## Fix
`handle_directory_query` accepts the delegated key as its member through `member_portal::delegation::accept` (live session, scope-checked, recorded, as the directory tasks do), and authorizes any other signer as before. The projection, and so what may be shown, is the member's own.

## Test
`member_portal_oob::the_portal_key_looks_up_a_member_by_did_as_its_member`: the portal key queries the member's DID and gets the card's `displayName`. Without the fix it fails with exactly the refusal above.

Local: `cargo nextest -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` 3815/3815; clippy `-D warnings`; fmt.

title: feat(vtc): the portal names a room's authors as the member directory shows them
body:
In a room used for chat, an author the wallet's reading gives no name was shown by the last segment of their `did:webvh` (`airport-electric`), which reads as a name but is only a path the DID's owner chose.

## What changes
- **Names**: the room's own name (the wallet's reading, shared with the wallet's console and Keyring) → the name the community's directory shows this member (`vtc/directory/query/0.1`, signed with the portal's delegated key) → the shortened DID, in monospace with a **DID** tag.
- **Member card**: each author's name opens a card on hover, focus or tap: initials, name, nickname, pronouns, role and the full DID.
- **Privacy**: lookups only in `open` / `attributed` rooms, whose host already sees who wrote what. A private room's authors are never looked up, since that would tell the community who writes there. Only the DID is sent, never the room. The directory answers only where the member shows their DID to the viewer; anything else is the DID fallback.
- `DirectoryQuery01{Payload,Response}` added to `vta_sdk::openapi` / `routes::openapi_spec`, the snapshot and the console's wire types regenerated, the task added to the admin-UI manifest.

## Not in this PR
- The card has no avatar or link to the directory entry: `query/0.1` returns no `entryId`, and `images/get` needs one. Adding them needs a spec change first (a `query/0.2` carrying `entryId`).

- `conversation.test.ts`: name order.
- `Rooms.test.tsx`: directory name, DID fallback with its tag, room name first and not looked up, the hover/tap card, and no lookup in a private room.

title: spec(vtc/rooms/community): an administrator sets a community room's record members
body:
A community-owned room's profile is written by the community with its label and description only. So a room meant as a conversation starts with no record members, and turning replies and reactions on took a member holding `curate`, which most of a community room's members do not hold. The community holds `admin` in every room it owns but had no task to set them. Keyring's maintainers asked for this so a new chat room doesn't start with replies and reactions off.

## Changes
- **`vtc/rooms/community/create/0.6`**: optional `recordMembers`, written into the room's profile with its label and description (step 5). Absent is none, as in 0.5. The response carries what was recorded.
- **`vtc/rooms/community/update/0.5`**: optional `recordMembers` (the whole set) or `removeRecordMembers: true`, mutually exclusive (`dependentSchemas`, as `description` / `removeDescription`). Either re-writes the profile. Absent, the profile's record members are carried over as in 0.4. An administrator's surface SHOULD send them only when the administrator changed them, so an unrelated update never overwrites a set a curator wrote in the room.
- **`vtc/rooms/community/get/0.6`**: optional `recordMembers`, as the community last wrote or read back the profile. It says plainly that this is not a read of the room made for the request.
- **`vtc/_shared/0.5`**: `RoomRecordMembers`, with the constraints of `RoomProfile.recordMembers` (additive def).
- Draft specs that linked the previous versions (`list/0.4`, `members/list/0.2`, `unarchive/0.1`, admin events `subscribe/0.6`, `event/0.5`) now point at the new ones, as #1336 did.

An administrator's surface MAY offer the members as one choice ("replies and reactions": `kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt`) and MAY start it on for a room it is creating. `RoomProfile` says record members are "never by default", and that holds: absent on the wire is still none, and a pre-checked box sends an explicit choice. The surface SHOULD warn that a reader predating these members cannot read the profile once it lists them.

All additive on the request (optional on the response), so MINOR increments under §5.2's draft allowance. Previous versions remain published.

## Checks run locally
- `npm run validate` (1430 specs), `npm run build`, `build-bundles` + `check-bundles` (1424 bundles)
- Rust codegen + `cargo fmt`, TS / Go / Dart bindings regenerated; `npm run check-bindings`: all four agree
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features vtc --test conformance`: 756 passed

- create/0.6: optional `recordMembers`, written into the room's profile with
  its label and description; absent is none, as in 0.5. The response carries
  what was recorded.
- update/0.5: optional `recordMembers` (the whole set) or
  `removeRecordMembers: true`, mutually exclusive; either re-writes the
  profile. Absent, the profile's record members are carried over as before.
- get/0.6: optional `recordMembers`, as the community last wrote or read back
  the profile.
- vtc/_shared/0.5: `RoomRecordMembers`, the constraints of
  `RoomProfile.recordMembers`.

An administrator's surface may offer them as one choice (replies and
reactions: kind, inReplyTo, writtenAt) and may start it on for a new room;
the request it sends is still the administrator's explicit choice. Other
draft specs now point at the new versions. All four libraries regenerated.

title: feat(vtc): the member portal sends chat messages in a room, and the conversation scrolls
body:
## Why

Feedback from a community testing data rooms with Keyring:
- A member could add only **notes** to a room from the portal. The form required a title, and a note shows in the chat as a line you click through. Keyring shows a record with text and no title as an ordinary chat message, so the reply the member wanted to send in the room's conversation had nowhere to go.
- The conversation ran oldest-first down the whole page, so reaching the newest message meant scrolling to the bottom of the page.

## What

- **A Note / Message switch** in *Add to this room*. It **starts on Note**, as the community and Keyring's developer asked, and remembers the member's last choice in this browser (`localStorage`; if storage is unavailable it starts on Note).
  - **Message** is one box: Enter sends, and Shift+Enter starts a new line.
  - It writes through the wallet's new `rooms.putMessage` (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#453). That writes the text with **no title**, plus `kind: "message"` where the room's profile lists it. The member confirms in the wallet's window, as for every write.
  - A wallet without `putMessage` gets no switch and is offered notes only, as before.
- **The conversation scrolls in its own window**, sized to the screen and opened at the newest message. It follows new messages while the member is at the bottom, or when the newest message is their own. It never pulls them down while they read something older. Only the layout changes: the order is still the one the wallet gives (`vtc-service/CLAUDE.md`, *Data rooms in the portal*).
- Docs: `data-rooms-files.md` §8.5 lists `putMessage` among the wallet's methods and among the writes that are confirmed; `vtc-service/CLAUDE.md` says how the portal writes messages.

## Depends on

OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#453 for the Message side. This can merge first: until the extension has `putMessage`, the page shows notes only.

## Tests

`Rooms.test.tsx`:
- the switch starts on Note;
- Message sends `{ hostDid, roomId, body }` and never calls `putNote`;
- Enter sends and Shift+Enter does not;
- an empty message is never sent;
- the last choice is remembered;
- a wallet without `putMessage` gets notes only;
- the conversation sits in its scrolling window and opens at the newest message.

`npm run lint` and the full admin-ui suite (133 files, 1642 tests) pass locally, as does `scripts/check-docs.py`.
author: stormer78

Changelog

Sourced from @​openvtc/trust-tasks's changelog.

0.31.2 — 2026-11-17

Added

  • vta/dids: List, get and methods for every identity a VTA holds; method-neutral context deletion (#1332)

A VTA holds identities of several methods, and the only way to ask which was once per method: vta/webvh/dids/list, vta/webs/dids/list. Every client asked only the methods it knew about, so a VTA whose identities were all did:webs reported none, and a new method would add a question to every client.

  • vta/dids/_shared/0.2: CONVENTIONS §20 (every identity: which are summarised, who sees what, the summary, methods), DidSummary and MethodInfo, a did:key profile, and a Summary details heading in each profile. §3.1's level-1 refusal is scoped to the key-role tasks.
  • vta/dids/list/0.1, get/0.1, methods/list/0.1.
  • vta/contexts/update-did/1.2: the DID must be one the VTA holds in that context (notHeld), and its class may be the context's (didClassConflict).
  • vta/contexts/delete/1.2: every DID in the subtree is deleted as its method's delete task deletes it, host work settled first. 1.1 named did:webvh only, so a did:webs record was removed while its key event log stayed published as a live identity.
  • vta/contexts/preview-delete/2.0: dids (every method) replaces webvhDids, which left did:webs out of the confirmation.
  • vta/webvh/dids/list/1.0 and vta/webs/dids/list/0.1 retired in favour of vta/dids/list/0.1.

Bindings regenerated for all four languages.

  • vtc/storage/credentials/recipient: Add vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1 (#1329)

A room-hosting administrator's client asks the community for the key a vtc/storage/credentials/set sealed block is sealed to: the Ed25519 key it opens with, as its did:key, and the verification method in its DID document that publishes it.

A client that cannot resolve and verify the community's DID could not seal at all. A browser console reading a did:webs would need KERI verification, and a hosted did:webvh would need a log from another origin. The VTC console read only the same-origin did.jsonl, which a did:webs community never serves. The answer comes over the same authenticated channel the credential then goes over, and is the same for every DID method. notPublished covers a key the community's document no longer lists, so nothing is sealed past a rotation.

credentials/set 0.3's sealed-block definition and related now point at it (prose only).

A room-hosting administrator's client asks the community for the key a vtc/storage/credentials/set sealed block is sealed to: the Ed25519 key it opens with, as its did:key, and the verification method in its DID document that publishes it.

A client that cannot resolve and verify the community's DID could not seal at all. A browser console reading a did:webs would need KERI verification, and a hosted did:webvh would need a log from another origin. The VTC console read only the same-origin did.jsonl, which a did:webs community never serves. The answer comes over the same authenticated channel the credential then goes over, and is the same for every DID method. notPublished covers a key the community's document no longer lists, so nothing is sealed past a rotation.

[Python] Release 0.63.0

Added

  • JsonTextValidator, validating instances given as JSON text in str or bytes without building Python objects for them.
  • number_format, a custom format check that reads numbers.

Fixed

  • $ref to a bundled meta-schema of a draft other than the schema's own, such as https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema from a Draft 7 schema, failing to resolve.
  • $ref to a json-schema.org URI with no bundled meta-schema, such as http://json-schema.org/draft-03/schema#, never retrieved.
  • Error messages for an empty enum ending after "is not one of" instead of naming the empty enum.

  • Draft 4 schemas with an empty enum, or one with equal members such as [0, 0.0], passing the meta-schema check.
  • HttpOptions(ca_cert=...) reporting invalid PEM as an HTTP client build error instead of a certificate parse error that names the file.
  • Named backreferences such as (?<n>x)\k<n> failing to build in pattern, patternProperties and propertyNames.

Release notes

Sourced from EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action's releases.

Release 2.1.3 - cargo-deny 0.22.0

Changed

  • PR#923 resolved #920 by emitting a new advisory-withdrawn diagnostic when an ignored advisory has been withdrawn in the advisory database and the ignore can be removed, instead of emitting advisory-not-detected.
  • PR#924 resolved #922 by changing advisories.unmaintained to default to workspace scope instead of all.

Release 2.1.2 - cargo-deny 0.21.0

Fixed

  • PR#893 resolved #892 by correctly handling url matching when using IP hosts.
  • PR#895 fixed an issue where --target could not be passed multiple times in the CLI.
  • PR#885 resolved #772 by not emitting diagnostics for unused workspace dependencies when those crates were explicitly excluded from the graph by the user.
  • PR#887 resolved #707 by ignoring renamed packages when checking for workspace duplicates.
  • PR#902 resolved #898 by adding the unmatched-allow-build-script and allowed-crate-without-build-script diagnostics.
  • PR#911 resolved #910 by visiting each crate once when checking build-time dependents, so a dependency cycle no longer overflows the stack.
  • PR#915 resolved #914 by ignoring a trailing slash when exactly matching source urls, so that licenses.private.ignore-sources can match sparse registries.

Added

  • PR#899 resolved #896 by searching for configuration in .config as well.
  • PR#904 resolved #754 and #889 by adding 3 new configuration fields:
    • advisories.ignore-expiry - The default duration after the publishing of an advisory that an advisories.ignore will function for it. Once the current date surpasses that expiry the ignore will not prevent the diagnostic for the advisory being emitted. This also accepts an absolute date.
    • advisories.ignore.expiry is the same as the above, but scoped to a particular ignore. This value overrides the default.
    • advisories.ignore.allow only allows specific crates by PackageSpec to depend on the crate(s) that the advisory applies to, intended to prevent new crates or versions from being added to the graph that increase the number of edges and thus making it harder to update/remove the affected crate.
  • PR#906 changed the diagnostics for advisories and yanked crates to conditionally show the (try cargo update -p <affected crate>) and instead detect if any dependents use 1 or more version requirements that preclude updating to an unaffected/patched/unyanked version.

Deprecated

  • PR#903 deprecated the advisories.git-fetch-with-cli configuration field, which has done nothing since PR#830.

title: fix(setup): don't count OpenVTC's own admin did:key as a persona in the context probe
body:
Fixes #632. Refs #633 (documentation only; the binary build lives in the download pipeline, not here).

## #632: first-time setup stops at "already in use"

`context_probe::probe` runs after setup has rotated the ephemeral setup DID into the long-term admin `did:key`, which the VTA records in the same context. Since #623 (`list_dids_webvh` → `vta/dids/list`), the probe counted **every** DID, so every fresh context read as "1 persona".

- The probe now filters `vta/dids/list` to the persona methods `webvh` and `scid:vh`, the same set the rebuild plan already used. Both now share `context_probe::PERSONA_DID_METHODS`, so they can't drift apart.
- I didn't use `class: "persona"`: the VTA records a class only for `did:webs` (webvh summaries carry `class: None`), so it would hide every real webvh persona and read occupied contexts as empty.

Tests (`mockvta_bootstrap_e2e`, `--include-ignored`):
- New `probe_reads_a_fresh_context_as_empty_after_admin_rotation`: rotates the admin into `ctx1` against `MockVta`, asserts the admin `did:key` *is* listed in the context (the precondition), then asserts the probe returns `Empty`. Against the old probe it fails with `Occupied { persona_dids: ["did:key:z6Mk…"] }`.
- `persona_did_webvh_mint_round_trips` now also asserts a minted `did:webvh` persona makes the probe return `Occupied`.

## #633: Linux runtime libraries

The README's Prerequisites gain a "Linux runtime libraries" section: `libpcsclite.so.1` (from `openpgp-card`) and `libdbus-1.so.3` (from `dbus-secret-service`, linked dynamically, not vendored), with package names for Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora and Arch. Loading PC/SC at runtime, or shipping a no-token download, is a separate change.

Needs a backport to `release/0.9`: the bug ships in 0.9.0.
author: stormer78

title: feat(rooms): a room page can send a chat message (rooms.putMessage)
body:
## Why

A community member portal can write to a room only with `rooms.putNote`, which requires a title. Keyring shows a record that has text and no title as an ordinary chat message. So a member using the portal could not reply in a room's chat: everything they wrote showed up as a note with a title.

## What

- **`@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms` `writeMessageAsMember(room, { body })`** writes the text with no `title`, as the member.
  - Where the room's profile lists them, the record also carries `kind: "message"` and `writtenAt`, so every reader shows it as a message.
  - A room whose profile lists neither still takes the message as an untitled record, which the reading rules show as a message (*Untitled records*, `shownKind`).
  - The record is sealed on `attributed` / `private` rooms and stored in the clear on `open` ones. Writes are create-only, and an empty message is refused before anything is sent.
- **`window.vtaWallet.rooms.putMessage({ hostDid, roomId, body })`** has the same gates as `putNote`:
  - the call's shape is checked;
  - the page must be the community's portal (the `SignInPortal` origin);
  - the room must be shared with that page;
  - the share's member is used, never the member the page names;
  - the member confirms the write in the wallet's window, which says "Send this message to the room as you?" and shows the text.
- `putNote` still requires a title. A note and a message are different records, and a page that offers both says which one it is writing.

The VTI member portal's compose panel will use this behind a Note / Message switch (VTI PR to follow), and will offer only notes to a wallet that has no `putMessage`.

## Tests

- core: the sealed body (`kind`, `body`, `writtenAt`, no title, signed as the member), the untitled fallback, the open-room cleartext, and refusal of an empty message.
- extension: the call-shape check, the confirmation prompt, a declined prompt writing nothing, a room not shared being refused, the share's member being used, and the open-room write going through the offscreen document.
- `npm run lint`, `npm test` (core 1336, extension 1578), `npm run build` and `check-task-versions` all pass locally.

title: fix(app): clear the AppDelegate Swift 6 concurrency warnings
body:
Clears the Swift concurrency warnings from main CI (run 45231454105):

- `AppDelegate.swift:93` (x4): "non-Sendable parameter type '[AnyHashable : Any]' cannot be sent from caller of protocol requirement 'application(_:didReceiveRemoteNotification:)' ... this is an error in the Swift 6 language mode". The `async` import of this requirement has UIKit's caller send `userInfo` into the implementation whatever its isolation (a `nonisolated` first attempt only changed the wording), so the delegate now implements the completion-handler form, which UIKit calls synchronously on the main actor. A main-actor `Task` runs `AgentModel.shared.handlePushWake()` and calls the handler once with the same `.newData` / `.noData` result. The payload was, and is, unused: the push is a contentless wake.
- `AppDelegate.swift:87` (x2): "no 'async' operations occur within 'await' expression". `onApnsRegisterFailed` is synchronous and main-actor, as is the delegate, so it is called directly instead of awaited inside a `Task`. It sets the same status string.

The `appintentsmetadataprocessor ... Metadata extraction skipped` lines are Xcode noise and are left alone. There is no iOS SDK on the authoring machine, so CI's iOS build is the type check.

title: Update the guides for VTI-Fig (verified on release candidates until the final release)
body:
This brings the explore and developer guides up to date for the VTI-Fig release.

**Not to be merged until the final VTI-Fig release is out.** Until then the guides are built and tested against the release candidates, starting with VTI-Fig-RC-0. Each new candidate gets the same run, and this branch and PR are kept up to date with what it finds. Once the final release is tagged, the guides are re-checked against it, the interim "verified on a release candidate" notes are replaced with the release, and the PR is merged.

## What changed
