title: fix(did-webs): compare a service's type as a set
body:
## Problem

The browser plugin refuses a VTA's own did:webs with:

> did:webs: did.json does not match the verified key state: did.json's services differ from those the stream authorises

DID Core §5.4 lets a service `type` be one string or a set of strings, but `checkPublished` compared services as raw JSON, so `"TSPTransport"` (derived from the stream) and `["TSPTransport"]` (published in did.json — the Rust `Document` writes every type as an array) were treated as different services. The Rust resolver already accepts this (affinidi-did-webs 0.13.9, affinidi-tdk-rs #1173), so PNM resolves the same DID fine.

## Change

- Service types are compared as a sorted, de-duplicated set of strings; non-string entries are dropped so a malformed type compares as no type.
- `DelegatorOOBI` is recognised in either form (service matching, optional delegator, and `carryDelegatorService`).
- A different set of types is still refused.

## Tests

- New regression test in `test/did-webs.test.js`: one-element array accepted, all-array document accepted, the resolver's own document fed back as did.json accepted; extra type / empty / non-string type refused. It fails without the fix.
- `npm test`: 392 pass, 0 fail.
- Verified against the live `did:webs:webvh.storm.ws:nodes:EJdeTq8v1SPknlbBkCXjSphLhP_N2D_9-IvFzBCYPxh5` artifacts: refused before, resolves after.

title: fix(rank): match whole words, fold plurals, drop query stopwords
body:
Fixes the two ranking defects the evaluation harness (#46) found, and makes their probes hard checks.

## Changes
- **Whole-word matching** instead of substring containment — "run" no longer matches "Test **run**ner", nor "test" "la**test**".
- **Plurals folded to singular** by rule, on both sides ("tests"→"test", "policies"→"policy", "pushes"→"push"; "status", "analysis", "bus" untouched). Plurals only — "-ing"/"-ed" stripping guesses wrong in ways nobody can predict.
- **Query stopwords** (short English list) dropped. Negations ("not", "never", "no") are kept — they change meaning. A query of only stopwords returns nothing, not the whole context.
- Words split on any script, not ASCII only — "café" / "Straße" now match.

## Evaluation, before → after

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| minimisation precision | 29% | **67%** |
| precision (dimension) | 81% | **93%** |
| overall precision | 74% | **82%** |
| MRR | 0.97 | **1.00** |
| checks | 24/27 + 3 known gaps | **29/29, no known gaps** |

`minimisation-stopwords` and `precision-word-boundaries` are now hard. One adjustment to the latter: its "runner" memory's description no longer contains the word "run" itself, because with whole-word matching that memory legitimately matches both query words and the probe was testing two things at once. As adjusted, the probe fails under the old substring ranking (the name "runner" scored) and passes under this one.

Unit tests cover word boundaries, plural folding both ways, non-plural `-s` words, stopword-only queries, and non-Latin words.

Plugin and crate → **0.6.1**.

title: feat: signed, verifiable memory export/import bundle
body:
Closes #36.

## What it does

- **`vta-agent-memory export [--out FILE] [--type …] [--basis …] [--status …]`** writes a signed JSON bundle of the context's memories. Each record is included **exactly as stored, with its author's own proof**. The exporter's Data Integrity proof (`eddsa-jcs-2022`) covers the whole bundle: the record list, the source context and the filter. Records that are refused or unattributed are left out and listed with the reason. The file is written with mode `0600`.
- **`vta-agent-memory import FILE|- [--replace] [--dry-run] [filters]`** checks the bundle's proof and every record's own proof (author, `contextId` = `sourceContext`, and the key) **before connecting**. It is all or nothing: a bundle with one bad record imports nothing. Without `--replace`, a memory that already exists under the same key is left alone (create-only `expectedVersion: 0`). With `--replace`, the import becomes a new version and the old one goes to history.
- **`docs/memory-bundle.md`** documents the format and the checks, so a non-VTA reader can verify a bundle.

## Keeping the original author

A record's signature names the context it was written in, so an imported record can't keep that signature as its own: the relocation check from #31 would rightly refuse it. Re-signing as the importer would lose who wrote it. Instead, the importer signs a record for its new location and carries the original **verbatim** in `importedFrom`. `authorship::verify` then checks:

1. the outer proof, for where the record was found;
2. the original's proof, author == signer, the same `key`, and no nested import;
3. that the content (everything except authorship, location, `supersedes` and `importedFrom`) is the same in both.

If all three hold, the memory is attributed to the **original** author, with `importedBy` and `importedFrom` shown alongside (`author` JSON block, and the note "imported from context `home`"). Re-importing flattens to the first original. Any later save or status change drops `importedFrom`, so the editor becomes the author and the imported version stays in history.

## Tests (`tests/bundle.rs`, 7)

- Export, then import into a fresh context, preserves name, body, `updatedAt`, basis, confidence, evidence, status, reason and `reviewAfter`, each attributed to its original author (agent or operator).
- A tampered bundle is refused when:
  - a record was edited;
  - a record was dropped;
  - it claims another exporter;
  - a record was edited and the bundle **re-signed** by a forger (the bundle proof holds, the record's does not);
  - it was re-sealed under a different source context;
  - it isn't a bundle at all.
- A planted import whose content differs from the original it carries is refused. A mutation check confirmed this test fails if the content comparison is removed.
- Editing an imported memory makes the editor its author.
- Re-exporting an import keeps the original author.
- Import doesn't overwrite without `--replace`, and keeps history with it.
- A filtered export carries only what it selects, says so in `filter`, and lists unattributed records it left out.

Also checked: `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean, every existing test passes, and the eval's hard checks all pass. Nothing that affects ranking changed.

## Notes

- A bundle is a snapshot. Importing a memory the original author has since retracted brings back the pre-retraction version; the `importedFrom` context and timestamps say where it came from and when.
- History isn't exported.
- `import` writes memories one at a time once the bundle has been checked, so a VTA failure partway through can leave a partial import. Re-running without `--replace` picks up the rest.
- The README's "Six MCP tools" line, stale since #33, now lists all nine.

Version 0.6.1 → 0.7.0.

title: test(eval): score recall across personal memory and Data Rooms
body:
Follow-up to #34 / #49: the evaluation now scores room recall as well as personal memory.

## Harness

- Probes now use the same path as `memory_recall`: `rooms::recall` over personal memory and the scenario's `rooms`. A new optional `sources` field on a probe narrows where it looks. Room results are named `room:<label>/<key>` in every probe list.
- New `room` step: writes a sealed room record signed by a named member. It can also write:
  - an `open` (unsigned) record;
  - a deprecated, retracted or expired record;
  - a deliberately broken record: `alter` (changed after signing), `servedAs` (moved to another key), or `hostAuthor` (the host records a different author).
- New `sources` dimension. `tests/eval/README.md` documents the step and the field.

## Scenarios (19–22)

| scenario | checks |
|---|---|
| `sources-room-and-personal` | One ranking across both: an `observed` room record outranks an `inferred` memory. `sources` narrows to personal only or to one room. A memory `type` leaves rooms out. |
| `sources-room-poisoning` | Altered, relocated and wrong-author room records are absent and reported refused, with a query and with none, and the fence holds. |
| `sources-room-standing` | Deprecated records rank lower; retracted and expired records never appear, with a query and with none. |
| `sources-room-abstention` | An unrelated query returns nothing even with rooms configured. An open room's record is recalled. |

## Numbers

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| existing six dimensions | unchanged | unchanged |
| sources | — | 10/10 checks, precision 100%, MRR 1.00 |
| all | 29/29, precision 82% | 39/39, precision 86% |

Switching probes to the unified recall path moved no existing metric.

Mutation check: disabling room signature verification fails `sources-room-poisoning` (8/10, five hard failures), so the scenario guards the check it claims to.

Tests only, so no version bump (as with #35).

title: fix(build,rs,ts,ts-gen,go,dart): keep the free-standing $defs a specification declares in the request schema constant
body:
Follow-up to #1243.

#1243 made every schema constant keep only the root `$defs` its root reaches. That also dropped definitions a specification declares for clients and references from nowhere. Five specifications have one:

| specification | definition |
|---|---|
| `vtc/storage/credentials/set` 0.2, 0.3 | `SealedCredentialCleartext`: the cleartext inside `sealed`, "declared here so that every generated binding carries the type a producer seals and a community opens" |
| `vta/credentials/issue` 0.1, 0.2 | `GovernancePolicyClaims` |
| `auth/step-up/requests/show` 0.1 | `Handoff` |

VTI reads `SealedCredentialCleartext`, and the OpenAPI components its console uses, out of `PAYLOAD_SCHEMA`, so it is still pinned to `trust-tasks-build` 0.1.4.

## Rule

The request constant (`PAYLOAD_SCHEMA` / `payloadSchemaJson` / `PayloadSchemaJSON`) also keeps each **free-standing** definition and what it references. A free-standing definition is one other than `Response` that no `#/$defs/<name>` reference anywhere in the schema names.

- Only the specification itself can declare one. A shared definition spliced in from another document is there because something references it, so a shared definition that only the response uses is still pruned from the request. `check-bundles` confirms this independently: its re-derivation only counts definitions without a `defOrigins` entry.
- The response document holds the request's `$defs` but not the request root, so it can't tell a free-standing definition from one the request uses. It keeps only what `Response` reaches, as before.
- Types, bundles and digests are unchanged. Only the text of the five request constants grows, in all four languages.

As DEVELOPMENT.md requires, the rule is implemented independently in all seven copies: `prune_unreachable_defs` in `trust-tasks-build`, `pruneUnreachableDefs` in the three `build-*-bindings.mjs` scripts, `trust-tasks-ts-gen`, the Go `trust-tasks-gen` and the Dart generator. `check-bundles` re-derives it. DEVELOPMENT.md and the consumer-side-generation design doc describe the rule.

## Tests

- `trust-tasks-build`: a new test checks that the request keeps a free-standing declaration while dropping a definition only `Response` references (the spliced-shared case). Another checks that a free-standing declaration keeps what it references. The existing response test now also covers a response-only shared definition.
- `trust-tasks-codegen` `bundle_agrees_with_generated_module`: adds `vtc/storage/credentials/set/0.3` and asserts from the outside that the request schema keeps `SealedCredentialCleartext`.

Ran locally: `npm run regen` (only the five specifications × four languages changed), `npm run check-bindings`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-build --all-features`, and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-codegen bundle_agrees`.

No `!`: no signature changes in any public API. The internal pruning helpers gained a parameter, but none of them is exported.

title: spec(credential-exchange/present): 0.2 — OID4VP keyed vp_token, either Data Integrity nonce placement
body:
Implements the direction agreed on #1358.

**New version `credential-exchange/present/0.2`**
- `vp_token` is the OID4VP 1.0 DCQL response object (§8.1): keyed by credential query `id`, each value an array of one or more presentations. Schema: `oneOf` keyed object (`propertyNames` `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`, values arrays of string|object) or bare string. A bare SD-JWT-VC string stays accepted for compatibility; a bare DI VP object is no longer a valid `vp_token`.
- Data Integrity nonce/audience: consumers MUST accept `proof.challenge`/`proof.domain` (OID4VP §14.1.2) **or** the signed presentation's `nonce`/`domain`; values MUST agree if both are present; neither ⇒ refuse. Producers SHOULD use `proof.challenge`/`proof.domain`.
- Worked examples for SD-JWT-VC and Data Integrity (DI example uses `proof.challenge`/`proof.domain`).
- `## Changes from 0.1`. 0.1 remains published and is superseded (deprecated in the libraries) per the lifecycle rules.

**`vtc/directory/card/present/0.1` — same rule, in place.** Draft, no wire-shape change (only the `presentation` description), so SPEC §5.2's draft allowance applies; #831 changed the same sentence in place. `check-published-schemas` confirms the change is additive.

title: spec(vta/dids): a step-up hold is a next step, never an error (vta/dids next versions)
body:
> **Split and rebased.** The `auth/step-up/approve-request/0.6` and `auth/oob/redeem/0.1` parts landed in #1362, and are no longer in this PR's diff; their rows below are kept for context. It is rebased on #1363 (shared `$defs` emitted once in the prebuilt Rust tree), and with its 8 new `vta/dids` versions trust-tasks-rs now packages to 9,348,081 bytes (8.92 MiB, measured locally), under the 9.9 MiB guard.

Implements ruling 1, reading (a), on trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#36 ([decision](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec/issues/36#issuecomment-7150099980), following [this report](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec/issues/36#issuecomment-7148789655)). A hold for a step-up is answered with a next step, never an error response (SPEC §8.6).

## New spec versions

| Spec | New | Replaces | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auth/step-up/approve-request` | **0.6** (`extends: "0.5"`) | 0.5 | Inline delivery is a `trust-task-next-step` whose `expects` entry names `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7` and carries this task's payload as its `hint`. After approval is recorded, the producer re-sends the same operation (`continuation: resubmit`). The worked example is now a next step. The schema is unchanged. |
| `vta/dids/create` | **1.2** | 1.1 | Drops `vta/dids:stepUpRequired` (see below) |
| `vta/dids/keys/add` | **1.1** | 1.0 | same |
| `vta/dids/keys/retire` | **1.1** | 1.0 | same |
| `vta/dids/keys/revoke` | **1.1** | 1.0 | same |
| `vta/dids/keys/rotate` | **1.1** | 1.0 | same, plus `replace` `maxItems: 32` |
| `vta/dids/recover` | **1.2** | 1.1 | same, plus `history` `maxItems: 8` |
| `vta/dids/update` | **1.1** | 1.0 | same |
| `vta/dids/upgrade` | **1.1** | 1.0 | same, plus `layout` `maxItems: 8` |
| `auth/oob/redeem/0.1` | `status: retired`, `supersededBy: auth/oob/redeem/0.2` | | Status only, as the decision asked |

The old versions stay published. Publishing the new drafts supersedes them under the registry's lifecycle rules, so the libraries mark them deprecated, and they are withdrawn in the usual quarterly batch.

**How `vta/dids` answers a hold now.** Each new version has a section, *A step-up hold is a next step*, that replaces the second paragraph of conventions §6.2. The rest of §6.2 still applies, so the step-up remains bound to the `previewId`:

1. A request that carries a live `previewId` and is held for a bound step-up gets a next step with `continuation: resubmit`. Its single `expects` entry names `approve-response/0.7`. The entry's `hint` is an `approve-request/0.6` payload: `boundTo` is the digest of the task type and `previewId`, salted with `challenge`, and `sessionId` is absent, exactly as before.
2. A request with no `previewId` that would be held: the VTA stores the preview, as for a dry run. It answers with a next step (`continuation: proceed`) whose entry names the task's own Type URI. The `hint` is the dry-run `#response` (`outcome: "preview"`, with `preview` and its `previewId`). This is where the old `details.preview` now travels, and it validates against the spec's own response schema. The apply request that follows, carrying that `previewId`, then goes through case 1.
3. Neither hold is ever answered with an error. A declined step-up is `permissionDenied` the next time the request is sent.

**Supporting changes.**
- `scripts/lib/schema-bounds-allowlist.json` drops the baselines for the three `vta/dids` arrays now bounded. It moves the `approve-request` `accepts` baseline from 0.5 to 0.6, because a version that extends 0.5 cannot narrow a bound. `uniqueItems` over a three-value enum already caps that array at 3.
- `fix-stale-references` rewrote 4 prose links in other specs to the new `vta/dids` versions.
- Bindings are regenerated for all four languages. `npm run check`, `npm run build` and `check-bundles` pass locally.

## Other latest versions that still declare a hold as an error

Most of these are already on the #36 checklist and are not changed here:

- `vault/proxy-login/0.2`, `vault/release/0.2`, `vault/sign-trust-task/0.2`: `stepUpRequired`
- `vta/credentials/issue/0.2`: `stepUpRequired`
- `did-management/agent-name/remove/0.1`, `did-management/agent-name/update/0.1`: `stepUpRequired`
- `persona/disclosure/present/1.0`: `stepUpRequired`
- `credential-exchange/query/0.1`: `consentRequired`
- `vtc/directory/card/publish/0.1`: `consentRequired`
- `auth/oob/redeem/0.2`, `provision/vta/redeem/0.1`: `pending`

These are **not** on the checklist. They declare no hold code, but their prose describes inline delivery in an error (`permissionDenied` + `details.stepUpRequest`):

- `auth/step-up/requests/show/0.1`: built on inline error delivery. It defines `details.stepUpHandoff` to sit beside `details.stepUpRequest`, and its next version has to decide where the hand-off rides in a next step.
- `auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2`: its reference-design section describes the enrolment refused with `permissionDenied` + `details.stepUpRequest`.
- `auth/step-up/approver/enroll/0.1`: same pattern, in its reference-design section.

The `vta/dids/_shared` CONVENTIONS §6.2 (0.1 and 0.2) still describes the error form. The new task versions override it explicitly rather than adding a `_shared/0.3`, which would have meant copying every shared schema.

The `vta/webvh/dids/*` versions on the checklist are now retired in favour of `vta/dids`, so this PR covers them.

title: spec(auth/step-up): approve-request 0.6 — a step-up hold is a next step, never an error
body:
Implements ruling 1, reading (a), on trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#36 ([decision](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec/issues/36#issuecomment-7150099980)) for the step-up request itself: a hold for a step-up is answered with a next step, never an error response (SPEC §8.6).

This is the `auth/*` part of #1360, split out because #1360 fails `cargo package (trust-tasks-rs)`: with its 8 new `vta/dids` versions the crate packages to 10.05 MiB, over the 9.9 MiB guard. **The `vta/dids` versions follow once the crate is smaller** (the generator dedup that emits shared schemas once).

## Changes

| Spec | Change |
|---|---|
| `auth/step-up/approve-request` **0.6** (`extends: "0.5"`) | Inline delivery is a `trust-task-next-step` whose `expects` entry names `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7` and carries this task's payload as its `hint`. After approval is recorded, the producer re-sends the same operation (`continuation: resubmit`). Delivery in an error response is forbidden. Worked example is a next step. Schema unchanged. |
| `auth/oob/redeem/0.1` | `status: retired`, `supersededBy: auth/oob/redeem/0.2` (status only, as the decision asked) |

- `scripts/lib/schema-bounds-allowlist.json`: the `accepts` baseline moves from 0.5 to 0.6. A version that extends 0.5 cannot narrow a bound; `uniqueItems` over a three-value enum already caps it at 3.
- `fix-stale-references`: nothing to rewrite for these two (the 4 prose links in #1360 all point at the new `vta/dids` versions and stay there).
- Bindings regenerated (`npm run regen`).

## Local checks

- `npm run check`, `npm run build`, `build-bundles` + `check-bundles` (1413 bundles): pass.
- `cargo package -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate,all-specs`: **10,269,185 bytes (9.79 MiB)**, under the 9.9 MiB (10,380,902-byte) fail threshold; main is 9.78 MiB.

title: build(codegen,rs): spell each shared $defs entry once in the prebuilt tree
body:
## Why

`trust-tasks-rs` packages to **9.79 MiB** of crates.io's 10 MiB upload limit; the `cargo package (trust-tasks-rs)` job fails above 9.9 MiB, so new spec versions no longer fit (#1360's eight `vta/dids` versions fail it).

Measured on the generated tree (per-file compressed contribution): type code ~60%, schema constants ~22%, doc comments ~20%. Inside the schema constants, the `$defs` entries total ~9.7 MB, but only 2.2 MB is distinct: each shared schema (`vta/dids/_shared` key-roles, `_shared` device-binding, the framework `Ext`, …) is inlined verbatim into every version that references it. This PR targets that duplication. Sharing the generated *types* would make distinct types identical (a consumer's `impl From<v1_0::X>` + `impl From<v1_1::X>` would then conflict), so it was ruled out as an API change.

## What

After generating every module, `trust-tasks-codegen` (new `src/shared_defs.rs`) writes each `$defs` entry that two or more schema constants carry (and that is ≥160 bytes) once into `trust-tasks-rs/src/specs/shared_defs.rs` as a `macro_rules!` expanding to its string literal, and rewrites each literal into a `concat!` naming it:

```rust
const PAYLOAD_SCHEMA: Option<&'static str> = Some(
    concat!("{\"$defs\":{", crate::specs::shared_defs::d_Ext_99ef3684!(), ",", …, "},\"type\":\"object\"}\n"),
);
```

- **Constant values are unchanged, byte for byte.** `concat!` expands the macros at compile time. The pass reassembles each split and compares it with the original before rewriting, and leaves anything that does not reassemble alone. All 2775 constants were compared byte for byte against `main`.
- **No public API change.** Type names, paths and the `PAYLOAD_SCHEMA` / `schema_for` values are the same. `shared_defs` is a private module with `pub(crate)` macros.
- **`trust_tasks_build::generate_module` is untouched.** An application's `build.rs` output does not change. The pass runs in `trust-tasks-codegen` after it, so `bundle_agrees_with_generated_module` and the #1353 free-standing `$defs` tests are unaffected.
- **Rust-only, by design.** This is not one of the "change one, change all" rules: no schema changes, only how one Rust `&'static str` is spelled. The npm, Go and Dart packages have no upload limit close to their size, so the TS/Go/Dart generators are not mirrored. Documented in `docs/packages/rust.md`, with a pointer from `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`.
- `check-bindings` reads the Rust constants from source, so `rustSchemaConst` now resolves the `concat!` and the `shared_defs` macros (and unescapes Rust literals properly). I corrupted one shared macro on purpose and it was caught: 2717 disagreements.

## Size (`cargo package -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate,all-specs`)

| | bytes | MiB |
|---|---|---|
| main | 10,260,868 | 9.79 |
| this PR | 9,141,546 | 8.72 |
| saved | 1,119,322 | 1.07 |

## Verified locally
- `npm run regen`: stable, no further diff. `npm run check` and `npm run build && npm run build-bundles && npm run check-bundles` pass.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-build -p trust-tasks-codegen` and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate,all-specs` (4105 conformance tests) pass. `cargo clippy -D warnings` passes for codegen and for trust-tasks-rs default features. `cargo fmt --check` is clean.
- A throwaway consumer crate (path dep, `features = ["vta", "validate"]`, `-D warnings`) compiles. It asserts that `vta/dids/keys/revoke/1.0`'s request and response `PAYLOAD_SCHEMA` equal `main`'s literals and that they match `schema_index::schema_for`.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.41.5
body:
### Specifications

- **vta/dids**: A step-up hold is a next step, never an error (vta/dids next versions) ([#1360](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1360))

SPEC §8.6 requires a held task to be answered with trust-task-next-step,
  never an error response. Ruling 1 on trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#36
  (reading (a)) confirmed that inline step-up delivery in an error response
  was not an intended exception. auth/step-up/approve-request/0.6, which this
  builds on, landed in #1362.

  - vta/dids create 1.2, keys/add 1.1, keys/retire 1.1, keys/revoke 1.1,
    keys/rotate 1.1, recover 1.2, update 1.1, upgrade 1.1: drop
    vta/dids:stepUpRequired. A request with a previewId that is held for a
    step-up is answered with a next step naming approve-response, its hint
    an approve-request/0.6 payload bound to the previewId as before. A
    request with no previewId is answered with a next step naming the task
    itself (continuation: proceed), its hint the dry-run #response carrying
    the stored preview. keys/rotate, recover and upgrade declare the maxItems
    their baselined request arrays lacked.

  Earlier versions stay published and are superseded by the new ones.
  Bindings regenerated for all four languages.

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.12.7` → `0.12.8` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the
  tag, which *is* the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,
  `tag-dart` pushes the tag, and `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: v0.9.0
body:
### Added

- **A community may declare `issuerScope: directed`**
  ([#626](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/626)). DTG Core Credentials 0.16 makes a
  community `directed` at minimum and `public` where it is open to outsiders. Role VACs,
  a renewed VMC and an invitation credential are accepted with either scope; `pairwise`
  is still refused. In `openvtc-core`, `INVITATION_ISSUER_SCOPE` is replaced by
  `INVITATION_MIN_ISSUER_SCOPE`.

### Changed

- **VTA reply health comes from `vta-sdk`**
  ([#627](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/627)). The recovery supervisor reads
  `VtaClient::receive_health()`, which counts every DIDComm and TSP request on the admin
  session. Breaking for `openvtc-core`: the `vta_receive_leg` module is removed and
  `devices::{register, list, heartbeat}` no longer take a `ReceiveLegTracker`.
- **Dependencies for the Fig release.** `did-git-sign` / `vgi-core` 0.37, `vta-sdk` 0.94.1,
  `dtg-credentials` 0.16, `affinidi-tdk` 0.50, `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.51 and
  `trust-tasks` 0.41.3, with the matching VTI test crates; one node of each in the graph.

(reading (a)) confirmed that inline step-up delivery in an error response
was not an intended exception. auth/step-up/approve-request/0.6, which this
builds on, landed in #1362.

- vta/dids create 1.2, keys/add 1.1, keys/retire 1.1, keys/revoke 1.1,
  keys/rotate 1.1, recover 1.2, update 1.1, upgrade 1.1: drop
  vta/dids:stepUpRequired. A request with a previewId that is held for a
  step-up is answered with a next step naming approve-response, its hint
  an approve-request/0.6 payload bound to the previewId as before. A
  request with no previewId is answered with a next step naming the task
  itself (continuation: proceed), its hint the dry-run #response carrying
  the stored preview. keys/rotate, recover and upgrade declare the maxItems
  their baselined request arrays lacked.

Earlier versions stay published and are superseded by the new ones.
Bindings regenerated for all four languages.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: vtc-service-v0.35.2
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Serve credential-exchange/present 0.2 beside 0.1 ([#2816](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2816))

* feat(vtc): serve credential-exchange/present 0.2 beside 0.1

  Pins `credential-exchange/present` 0.2 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1358:
  OID4VP keyed `vp_token`, either Data Integrity nonce/audience placement) in
  `vti-specs-core` alongside 0.1, and routes both to the one present handler —
  the verifier already accepts the keyed map, the bare SD-JWT-VC string, and
  both placements.

  0.1 stays pinned and served while Eucalyptus is supported; the VTA keeps
  sending 0.1, since Eucalyptus VTCs route only 0.1 and its single-presentation
  map values are not yet arrays as 0.2 requires.

  The in-place registry edits to `credential-exchange/present/0.1` and
  `vtc/directory/card/present/0.1` (description text only) are refreshed in
  their bundles.



### Fixed

- **credential-exchange**: Bind a Data Integrity VP's nonce and audience in the proof or the body ([#2814](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2814))

trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1358 settled where a Data Integrity
  presentation carries the verifier's nonce and audience
  (`credential-exchange/present/0.2`, `vtc/directory/card/present/0.1`): a
  consumer accepts the holder proof's `challenge`/`domain` (OID4VP §14.1.2) or
  the presentation's own signed `nonce`/`domain`; values stated in both places
  must agree; a presentation stating neither is refused. Producers should use
  the proof's members.

  Verifier (`vtc-service`): `verify_di_vp` checked only the body's
  `nonce`/`domain`. The new `check_di_binding` accepts either placement per
  value, refuses any proof `challenge`/`domain` (verified or not) or body member
  that names another value, and refuses a presentation that binds the nonce or
  audience nowhere. A proof's `challenge`/`domain` counts only from a proof that
  was verified: affinidi-data-integrity 0.9 hashes them as proof options, so
  they are signed (a test re-points a captured challenge and the proof fails).
  Card present now relies on it rather than its own pre-check, which stays for
  the elections tasks that still require the body members.

  Join present: a keyed `vp_token` whose key names no credential query of the
  criterion's DCQL query is refused (present/0.2). A bare SD-JWT-VC string is
  still accepted.

  Holders (`vta-sdk::vp::build_vp_token`, `vta-vault::present_di_vc`): the
  holder proof now also carries `challenge` = nonce and `domain` = audience. The
  body `nonce`/`domain` stay, so verifiers that read only those keep working.
  The keyed DCQL map the VTA produces is unchanged.
author: stormer78

title: vta-service-v0.87.2
body:
### Fixed

- **vta-service**: Answer credential-exchange/query the same way whether or not anything matches ([#2813](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2813))

credential-exchange/query 0.1 (Conformance): "noMatch and \"held but not
  consented\" MUST be indistinguishable to the verifier", and a verifier the
  holder has not pre-trusted "is told consentRequired".

  - A verifier that is not trusted is now always answered
    `credential-exchange/query:consentRequired`, with one fixed message and no
    details, whether its query matched, matched nothing, or matched only
    credentials their context withholds from it. A deferral is persisted only
    when something matched, so operator approval and the later presentation
    work as before. The answer follows a small random delay (up to 50 ms) so
    the deferral write does not set the two apart by timing.
  - A trusted verifier is answered `credential-exchange/query:noMatch`, with
    one fixed message, both when nothing matched and when context policy
    withholds every match.
  - Both codes come from the generated bindings and carry their declared
    `retryable`; the census witnesses them and its ceiling drops to 371.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.41.4
body:
### Build & CI

- **codegen,rs**: Spell each shared $defs entry once in the prebuilt tree ([#1363](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1363))

trust-tasks-rs packaged to 9.79 MiB of crates.io's 10 MiB upload limit, and
  the `cargo package` job fails above 9.9 MiB, so new spec versions no longer
  fit. The largest duplication is the schema text: a shared schema (a family's
  _shared key-roles or device-binding schema, the framework's Ext, ...) is
  inlined into every version that references it, so the PAYLOAD_SCHEMA
  literals held ~9.7 MB of $defs entries of which 2.2 MB was distinct.

  trust-tasks-codegen now writes each $defs entry that two or more schema
  constants carry once, into src/specs/shared_defs.rs as a macro_rules!
  expanding to its string literal, and rewrites each literal into a concat! of
  the pieces naming it. concat! expands the macros at compile time, so every
  PAYLOAD_SCHEMA is the same &'static str, byte for byte (all 2775 compared
  against main); the rewrite reassembles each literal and compares it before
  replacing it. Type names, paths and constant values are unchanged, and
  trust_tasks_build::generate_module's output is untouched - the pass runs in
  trust-tasks-codegen after it.

  The .crate goes from 10,260,868 to 9,141,546 bytes (9.79 -> 8.72 MiB).

  It is Rust-only: no schema changes, only how one Rust constant is spelled,
  and the npm, Go and Dart packages have no upload limit near their size.
  check-bindings reads the Rust constants from source, so it now resolves the
  concat! and the shared_defs macros the way rustc does.



### Specifications

- **auth/step-up**: Approve-request 0.6 — a step-up hold is a next step, never an error ([#1362](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1362))

Implements ruling 1, reading (a), on trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#36
  for the step-up request itself. Split out of #1360 so it can land while the
  trust-tasks-rs crate is near crates.io's upload limit.

  - `auth/step-up/approve-request/0.6` (`extends: "0.5"`): inline delivery is a
    `trust-task-next-step` whose `expects` entry names
    `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7` and carries this payload as its `hint`;
    after approval is recorded the producer re-sends the operation
    (`continuation: resubmit`). Delivery in an error response is forbidden. The
    schema is unchanged.
  - The schema-bounds `accepts` baseline moves from 0.5 to 0.6: a version that
    extends 0.5 cannot narrow a bound, and `uniqueItems` over a three-value enum
    already caps it at 3.
  - `auth/oob/redeem/0.1` is `status: retired`, `supersededBy:
    auth/oob/redeem/0.2`.

  The new `vta/dids` versions from #1360 follow once the crate is smaller.
  Libraries regenerated.

title: chore: release 12 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.41.3` → `0.41.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.41.3` → `0.41.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.41.3` → `0.41.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.41.3` → `0.41.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.41.3` → `0.41.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.41.3` → `0.41.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.41.3` → `0.41.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.41.3` → `0.41.4` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.31.6` → `0.31.7` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.13.8`) | `0.13.7` → `0.13.8` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go/specs` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/specs/v0.1.7`) | `0.1.6` → `0.1.7` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.12.6` → `0.12.7` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the
  tag, which *is* the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,
  `tag-dart` pushes the tag, and `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

title: build(codegen,rs): spell each shared $defs entry once in the prebuilt tree (#1363)
body:
build(codegen,rs): spell each shared $defs entry once in the prebuilt tree (#1363)

trust-tasks-rs packaged to 9.79 MiB of crates.io's 10 MiB upload limit, and
the `cargo package` job fails above 9.9 MiB, so new spec versions no longer
fit. The largest duplication is the schema text: a shared schema (a family's
_shared key-roles or device-binding schema, the framework's Ext, ...) is
inlined into every version that references it, so the PAYLOAD_SCHEMA
literals held ~9.7 MB of $defs entries of which 2.2 MB was distinct.

trust-tasks-codegen now writes each $defs entry that two or more schema
constants carry once, into src/specs/shared_defs.rs as a macro_rules!
expanding to its string literal, and rewrites each literal into a concat! of
the pieces naming it. concat! expands the macros at compile time, so every
PAYLOAD_SCHEMA is the same &'static str, byte for byte (all 2775 compared
against main); the rewrite reassembles each literal and compares it before
replacing it. Type names, paths and constant values are unchanged, and
trust_tasks_build::generate_module's output is untouched - the pass runs in
trust-tasks-codegen after it.

The .crate goes from 10,260,868 to 9,141,546 bytes (9.79 -> 8.72 MiB).

It is Rust-only: no schema changes, only how one Rust constant is spelled,
and the npm, Go and Dart packages have no upload limit near their size.
check-bindings reads the Rust constants from source, so it now resolves the
concat! and the shared_defs macros the way rustc does.

title: fix(vta-service): answer credential-exchange/query the same way whether or not anything matches
body:
Backport of #2813 to `release/eucalyptus`.

**Conflict resolution / adaptation for this branch**
- The bindings are `trust_tasks_rs::specs::credential_exchange::query::v0_1::error_codes` here (no `vti-specs` crate on this branch).
- `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/error_code_census.rs` does not exist on this branch; that part of #2813 is dropped.
- `helpers::silence()` had no other caller on this branch, so it is removed (dead code under `-D warnings`).
- Locally: `cargo test -p vta-service --lib -- trust_tasks::credential_exchange operations::credential_exchange` → 31 passed.

## What and why

`credential-exchange/query` 0.1, Conformance: *"Never disclose which credentials are held in a refusal — `noMatch` and "held but not consented" MUST be indistinguishable to the verifier, or refusal itself becomes an enumeration primitive."* Answer, defer, or refuse: a verifier that is not pre-trusted *"is told `consentRequired`"*. The task leaves timing to the implementer and suggests varying the `consentRequired` response time.

Until now the VTA answered a query with nothing presentable as `taskFailed` (`not_found`), with a message saying whether nothing matched or context policy withheld the match, and answered a deferred query with no reply at all. The two declared codes were never sent.

Now:

- **Verifier not trusted** → always `credential-exchange/query:consentRequired` (declared `retryable: true`), one fixed message, no `details` — whether the query matched, matched nothing, or matched only credentials their context withholds from this verifier. `present_query` no longer returns early on an empty match; for an untrusted verifier it returns `ConsentRequired` with a possibly empty `requested`, and the handler persists a deferral only when it is non-empty, so `pending-list` / `pending-approve` → `present` work as before. A failed deferral write is logged rather than answered (an error would say something matched). The answer follows a uniform 0–50 ms delay so the deferral write does not separate the two by timing; the reasoning is in the `CONSENT_REQUIRED_JITTER_MS` comment.
- **Trusted verifier** → `present` as before, or `credential-exchange/query:noMatch` with one fixed message (`NO_PRESENTABLE_MATCH`) for both "nothing matched" and "context policy permits none of the matches".
- Codes come from the generated `vti_specs::credential_exchange::query::v0_1::error_codes` constants with their declared `retryable`. The error-code census now witnesses both; its ceiling drops 373 → 371.

No public API change: `PresentOutcome` keeps its variants (a trusted verifier's empty result is still `Err(AppError::NotFound(_))`, now with one fixed reason).

### Other callers

The VTC sends join queries (`join/ops/present.rs`) and does not register a reply waiter for them; an unsolicited `trust-task-error` on that thread was, and still is, dropped (`messaging.rs`, "reply had no waiter"). Nothing in `vta-sdk`, `pnm-cli`, `cnm-cli`, `vta-mobile-core` or `vta-cli-common` sends this task or reads its refusals (`VtaError::ConsentRequired` there is the step-up consent gate, keyed on `details.reason == auth:consent_required`, unrelated).

### Tests

- `an_untrusted_verifier_cannot_tell_held_from_unheld` — from an untrusted DID, a query for an unheld type and one for a held type give identical status, type and payload (code, message, retryable, no `details`; only `inResponseTo` differs), and only the held one leaves a pending record.
- `a_trusted_verifier_gets_one_no_match_for_unheld_and_withheld` — unheld and context-policy-withheld give the same `noMatch`.
- `present_query_excludes_credentials_their_context_forbids_the_verifier` asserts the fixed reason; the existing presentation / defer → approve tests pass unchanged.

## Requirements

Trust Task `credential-exchange/query` 0.1 — Conformance; Answer, defer, or refuse; Security & Privacy → Correlation.

## Backport

`release/eucalyptus` — the same handler is there (vta-service 0.56.x). Label to be added after merge.

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main`
- [x] No `version =` edits in any `Cargo.toml`
- [x] Tests cover the change; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy -p vta-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean

title: chore(deps): move to trql-client 0.32 and retire the trust-tasks-trql alias; release 0.37.0
body:
fix(verify-trust): allow non-public addresses only for an operator-configured registry URL

trql-client 0.32's HTTPS transport refuses loopback, private and other
non-public addresses by default. A registry URL discovered from the
registry's DID document keeps that default (Registry::https); the URL an
operator configures (--registry-url, the bridge's registry override) may
name a private-network or local registry, so new Registry::https_configured
allows them.


chore(deps): move to trql-client 0.32 and retire the trust-tasks-trql alias; release 0.37.0

trql-client 0.32 is on trust-tasks-rs 0.41.2 / affinidi-tdk 0.50, so
verify-trust names the workspace's single trust-tasks-rs directly and the
trust-tasks-trql alias (trust-tasks-rs 0.37) is gone. trql-client 0.32 makes
TransportChoice #[non_exhaustive], so it is built with TransportChoice::new.

The lockfile also takes vti-specs-core 0.7.1, vti-specs-rooms 0.11.1,
vti-specs-vta 0.12.1, vti-specs-vtc 0.8.1 and vti-specs-vtn 0.4.1, which
build with trust-tasks-build 0.2.2, so trust-tasks-build 0.1.4 drops out too.

API of verify-trust (Registry routes, TrqlTransport impls) and vgi-bridge

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.41.3
body:
### Specifications

- **credential-exchange/present**: 0.2 — OID4VP keyed vp_token, either Data Integrity nonce placement ([#1359](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1359))

`credential-exchange/present/0.2` settles the two readings #1358 found in 0.1.

  - `vp_token` is the OID4VP 1.0 DCQL response (§8.1): an object keyed by
    credential query `id`, each value an array of one or more presentations
    (SD-JWT-VC string or Data Integrity VP object). A bare SD-JWT-VC string is
    still accepted for compatibility; producers send the keyed form.
  - Data Integrity nonce and audience: a consumer MUST accept them as the holder
    proof's `challenge`/`domain` (OID4VP §14.1.2) or as the signed presentation's
    own `nonce`/`domain`; where both are stated they MUST agree, and a
    presentation stating neither is refused. Producers SHOULD use the proof's
    members. "The proof's `nonce`" in 0.1 was a wording slip for `challenge`.
  - Worked SD-JWT-VC and Data Integrity examples (the latter using
    `proof.challenge`/`proof.domain`).

  0.1 stays published and is superseded by 0.2 (the libraries deprecate it).

  `vtc/directory/card/present/0.1` takes the same placement rule in place: it is
  a draft whose wire shape does not change (only the presentation member's
  description), which SPEC §5.2 allows within a draft version, as #831 did for
  the same sentence.

  Prose links to present/0.1 in other specs move to 0.2 (fix-stale-references).
  Libraries regenerated.

title: fix(credential-exchange): bind a Data Integrity VP's nonce and audience in the proof or the body
body:
Implements the verifier/holder side of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1358 (registry PR trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1359: `credential-exchange/present/0.2`, `vtc/directory/card/present/0.1` in place).

- **Verifier** (`vtc-service` `verify_di_vp` → new `check_di_binding`): accepts `proof.challenge`/`proof.domain` or the signed body `nonce`/`domain`; both present ⇒ must agree; neither ⇒ refused. Covers credential-exchange/present, directory card present and recognise (all go through `verify_vp_token`).
- **Join present**: a keyed `vp_token` key naming no DCQL credential query of the criterion is refused; bare SD-JWT string still accepted.
- **Holders** (`vta-sdk::vp::build_vp_token`, `vta-vault::present_di_vc`): proof also carries `challenge`/`domain` (signed as eddsa-jcs-2022 proof options); body members kept for older verifiers.
- Tests: body-only, proof-only, both-agreeing accepted; both-disagreeing, neither, wrong proof audience, re-pointed challenge refused; holder output carries both.

Binding pins (present 0.1+0.2) follow in a separate PR once the registry publishes 0.2.

title: fix(credential-exchange): bind a Data Integrity VP's nonce and audience in the proof or the body (#2814)
body:
fix(credential-exchange): bind a Data Integrity VP's nonce and audience in the proof or the body (#2814)

trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1358 settled where a Data Integrity
presentation carries the verifier's nonce and audience
(`credential-exchange/present/0.2`, `vtc/directory/card/present/0.1`): a
consumer accepts the holder proof's `challenge`/`domain` (OID4VP §14.1.2) or
the presentation's own signed `nonce`/`domain`; values stated in both places
must agree; a presentation stating neither is refused. Producers should use
the proof's members.

Verifier (`vtc-service`): `verify_di_vp` checked only the body's
`nonce`/`domain`. The new `check_di_binding` accepts either placement per
value, refuses any proof `challenge`/`domain` (verified or not) or body member
that names another value, and refuses a presentation that binds the nonce or
audience nowhere. A proof's `challenge`/`domain` counts only from a proof that
was verified: affinidi-data-integrity 0.9 hashes them as proof options, so
they are signed (a test re-points a captured challenge and the proof fails).
Card present now relies on it rather than its own pre-check, which stays for
the elections tasks that still require the body members.

Join present: a keyed `vp_token` whose key names no credential query of the
criterion's DCQL query is refused (present/0.2). A bare SD-JWT-VC string is
still accepted.

Holders (`vta-sdk::vp::build_vp_token`, `vta-vault::present_di_vc`): the
holder proof now also carries `challenge` = nonce and `domain` = audience. The
body `nonce`/`domain` stay, so verifiers that read only those keep working.
The keyed DCQL map the VTA produces is unchanged.

Tests: verifier accepts body-only, proof-only and both-agreeing; refuses
both-disagreeing, neither, a proof naming another audience, and a re-pointed
proof challenge; holder output carries both placements.

| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.31.5` → `0.31.6` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.13.7`) | `0.13.6` → `0.13.7` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go/specs` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/specs/v0.1.6`) | `0.1.5` → `0.1.6` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.12.5` → `0.12.6` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the
  tag, which *is* the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,
  `tag-dart` pushes the tag, and `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: refactor(core)!: use vta-sdk's receive_health() in place of vta_receive_leg
body:
refactor(core)!: use vta-sdk's receive_health() in place of vta_receive_leg

vta-sdk 0.94.1 (VTI #2807, closing VTI #2753) counts reply / reply timeout on
every DIDComm request/reply as well as on TSP, into one per-session leg shared
by clones of the session and of the VtaClient built on it. That was the only
reason OpenVTC kept its own counter, so `openvtc_core::vta_receive_leg` is
removed and callers use the SDK:

- The recovery supervisor reads `VtaClient::receive_health()` of the current
  admin session on each tick; the panel shows `ReceiveLegHealth`. A rebuilt
  session is a new client with a fresh leg, which replaces the explicit
  `reset()`.
- device presence (register / list / heartbeat), the launch-time context
  fetch and the post-rebuild probe no longer wrap calls in `observe`: the SDK
  counts every request on the session, not only the wrapped ones.
- `is_reply_timeout` is now `VtaError::is_reply_timeout()` (SDK), replacing the
  message-text match in `errors.rs` and `community_context.rs`.

Behaviour unchanged: the breaker threshold is the SDK's REPLY_TIMEOUT_BREAKER
(2), the same value OpenVTC mirrored; any reply, refusals and problem reports
included, resets it; a send failure counts neither way. Differences: every
request on the admin session now counts (previously only the five wrapped call
sites), and REST calls are not counted (they are answered on their own HTTP
connection, and a REST-only session has no mediator inbox to stall).

Breaking for openvtc-core: the public `vta_receive_leg` module is gone, and
`devices::{register, list, heartbeat}` lose their `ReceiveLegTracker` argument.

Deps: vta-sdk 0.94.1, vta-service 0.87.1, vta-test-support 0.6.1 (built on
test-mediator 0.56), and the vti-specs-* patch releases on trust-tasks-build
0.2.2. The dev graph sheds affinidi-tdk 0.49, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.50,
affinidi-messaging-mediator* / test-mediator 0.55, trust-tasks-rs/-proof
0.40.5 and trust-tasks-build 0.1.4; `cargo tree -d -e normal,build,dev` shows
no duplicate affinidi-*, trust-tasks-* or vta-*/vti-* crates, and no new
duplicates of anything.

Closes #610

title: fix(vta-service): answer credential-exchange/query the same way whether or not anything matches
body:
## What and why

`credential-exchange/query` 0.1, Conformance: *"Never disclose which credentials are held in a refusal — `noMatch` and "held but not consented" MUST be indistinguishable to the verifier, or refusal itself becomes an enumeration primitive."* Answer, defer, or refuse: a verifier that is not pre-trusted *"is told `consentRequired`"*. The task leaves timing to the implementer and suggests varying the `consentRequired` response time.

Until now the VTA answered a query with nothing presentable as `taskFailed` (`not_found`), with a message saying whether nothing matched or context policy withheld the match, and answered a deferred query with no reply at all. The two declared codes were never sent.

Now:

- **Verifier not trusted** → always `credential-exchange/query:consentRequired` (declared `retryable: true`), one fixed message, no `details` — whether the query matched, matched nothing, or matched only credentials their context withholds from this verifier. `present_query` no longer returns early on an empty match; for an untrusted verifier it returns `ConsentRequired` with a possibly empty `requested`, and the handler persists a deferral only when it is non-empty, so `pending-list` / `pending-approve` → `present` work as before. A failed deferral write is logged rather than answered (an error would say something matched). The answer follows a uniform 0–50 ms delay so the deferral write does not separate the two by timing; the reasoning is in the `CONSENT_REQUIRED_JITTER_MS` comment.
- **Trusted verifier** → `present` as before, or `credential-exchange/query:noMatch` with one fixed message (`NO_PRESENTABLE_MATCH`) for both "nothing matched" and "context policy permits none of the matches".
- Codes come from the generated `vti_specs::credential_exchange::query::v0_1::error_codes` constants with their declared `retryable`. The error-code census now witnesses both; its ceiling drops 373 → 371.

No public API change: `PresentOutcome` keeps its variants (a trusted verifier's empty result is still `Err(AppError::NotFound(_))`, now with one fixed reason).

### Other callers

The VTC sends join queries (`join/ops/present.rs`) and does not register a reply waiter for them; an unsolicited `trust-task-error` on that thread was, and still is, dropped (`messaging.rs`, "reply had no waiter"). Nothing in `vta-sdk`, `pnm-cli`, `cnm-cli`, `vta-mobile-core` or `vta-cli-common` sends this task or reads its refusals (`VtaError::ConsentRequired` there is the step-up consent gate, keyed on `details.reason == auth:consent_required`, unrelated).

### Tests

- `an_untrusted_verifier_cannot_tell_held_from_unheld` — from an untrusted DID, a query for an unheld type and one for a held type give identical status, type and payload (code, message, retryable, no `details`; only `inResponseTo` differs), and only the held one leaves a pending record.
- `a_trusted_verifier_gets_one_no_match_for_unheld_and_withheld` — unheld and context-policy-withheld give the same `noMatch`.
- `present_query_excludes_credentials_their_context_forbids_the_verifier` asserts the fixed reason; the existing presentation / defer → approve tests pass unchanged.

## Requirements

Trust Task `credential-exchange/query` 0.1 — Conformance; Answer, defer, or refuse; Security & Privacy → Correlation.

## Backport

`release/eucalyptus` — the same handler is there (vta-service 0.56.x). Label to be added after merge.

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main`
- [x] No `version =` edits in any `Cargo.toml`
- [x] Tests cover the change; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy -p vta-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean

body:
fix(vta-service): answer credential-exchange/query the same way whether or not anything matches (#2813)

credential-exchange/query 0.1 (Conformance): "noMatch and \"held but not
consented\" MUST be indistinguishable to the verifier", and a verifier the
holder has not pre-trusted "is told consentRequired".

- A verifier that is not trusted is now always answered
  `credential-exchange/query:consentRequired`, with one fixed message and no
  details, whether its query matched, matched nothing, or matched only
  credentials their context withholds from it. A deferral is persisted only
  when something matched, so operator approval and the later presentation
  work as before. The answer follows a small random delay (up to 50 ms) so
  the deferral write does not set the two apart by timing.
- A trusted verifier is answered `credential-exchange/query:noMatch`, with
  one fixed message, both when nothing matched and when context policy
  withholds every match.

title: feat(spec): the stage gates of a Trust Ceremony
body:
## Summary

The framework named Trust Ceremonies and gave each step a `ceremony` member, but never described the procedure itself: how a party decides whether a requested transition happens, and what it answers. This adds that description.

**New section: Trust Ceremonies** (last in the Trust Task Documents chapter, so no section number moves)

- A Trust Ceremony is the governed procedure by which a transition is decided and carried out. Each party's decision is reached by a policy engine through seven stage gates: **Trigger → Gather → Verify → Facts → Evaluate → Verdict → Effects**.
- **Why Stage Gates**: the rationale for each boundary. Proof is not permission; policy reads facts, not documents; decisions can be reproduced; "not yet" is a real answer; authority is checked when it is used.
- **The Seven Stage Gates**: what each gate does, tied to the existing Consumer Requirements (items 1–13). The framework still names no authorization model or policy language: `<purpose>.rego` is one convention among Cedar, CEL, XACML or code.
- **Verdicts and the Replies That Carry Them** (normative):

  | Verdict | Reply |
  |---|---|
  | allow | `<type>#response` |
  | deny, requester may not ask | `permissionDenied` |
  | deny, decision task answers no | the task's success response |
  | refer | `trust-task-next-step` |
  | request more | `trust-task-next-step` |

  New rules:
  - A referral decision is evidence the policy re-evaluates. It is never the verdict itself.
  - Evidence and decisions are bound to the held exchange and to the party that supplies them.
  - A hold outlives `expiresAt`, and ends `cancelled` when abandoned.
  - A failed re-check before an effect stops the task.
- **One Procedure, Many Policies**: what the framework fixes against what a community chooses, with four worked purposes.

**Related edits**

- Reserved Response-Type Slugs: the declined-hold paragraph now treats a decline as evidence the policy re-evaluates, and reports a refusal in the form the task defines. This is consistent with "a decision is not a failure" (#46).
- Producer Requirements: a producer answering a held task MUST identify the held exchange.
- Terms: `Trust Ceremony` and `ceremony definition` are rewritten, and `verdict` is added.

Documentation only: no schema changes. The changelog is left for the release PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run render` completes, and every in-document anchor resolves (except the pre-existing `${e.id}` template placeholder)
- [x] Four local review passes, with all findings addressed

title: feat(vta-sdk): receive_health() counts DIDComm request/reply, not only TSP
body:
feat(vta-sdk): receive_health() counts DIDComm request/reply, not only TSP

`VtaClient::receive_health()` counted only Trust Tasks sent over TSP, so a
DIDComm-only admin session (a VTA without `#tsp`) never recorded a reply or a
reply timeout and `replies_not_arriving()` could never trip, although it has
the same failure mode: requests reach the VTA, the client's mediator inbox is
not collected, and every call ends in a reply timeout.

- `DIDCommSession` now owns an `Arc<ReceiveLeg>`, shared by its clones, and
  records into it on every request/reply (`send_and_wait`,
  `send_and_wait_trust_task`): any reply that comes back (result, problem
  report, wrong type) records a reply; a reply timeout records a timeout; a
  send/pickup failure records nothing. `DIDCommSession::receive_health()`
  exposes it.
- A `VtaClient` built on a DIDComm session uses that same leg, so its TSP leg
  (multiplexed or separate) and the DIDComm request/reply count into one
  `receive_health()` — "replies are reaching this client" regardless of
  transport. Clones of the client share it as before.
- Counting only: the D4 re-form/resend and `RepliesNotArriving` stay
  TSP-only. A DIDComm reply timeout is still returned as the same
  `DidcommTransport("timeout waiting for DIDComm response")` error. REST
  replies come back on their own HTTP connection and are not counted.
- New `VtaError::is_reply_timeout()`: true for a TSP or DIDComm reply
  timeout, so consumers no longer match the message text.

Threshold unchanged: `REPLY_TIMEOUT_BREAKER` = 2.

Closes #2753

A page signed in through the wallet can now ask for a shared room as a

- Dtg-credentials 0.16 — a community may declare issuerScope directed ([#2802](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2802))

Moves to dtg-credentials 0.16, after DTG Core Credentials (Correlation
  Scope, VMC; trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#86): a community's grant is
  `directed` at minimum, `public` where the community is open to outsiders.
  Only `pairwise` is refused. The library's `context-v3` (salting) feature is
  not enabled.

  Verifiers now accept a community credential declaring `directed` or
  `public`, and keep refusing anything narrower:

  - vta-sdk `vetting::eligibility` (a vetter's role VAC);
  - vtc-service `members::inbound_vmc` (the grant an acknowledgement binds to).



### Fixed

- **vtc**: Admit v2 DTG credentials at ingress ([#2801](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2801))

Credential ingress (`credentials::ingress::classify_dtg`) required
  `DTG_CONTEXT_V1` at `@context[1]`, so it refused every v2 DTG credential.
  dtg-credentials >= 0.14 lists `DTG_CONTEXT_V2` second on any VAC that
  states `purposes`, so a VAC carrying purposes could not be submitted to a
  VTC at all.

  Ingress now admits either DTG context second (`DTG_CONTEXT_VERSIONS`,
  built from the catalog's own constants), keeps the W3C v2 context first,
  and — as the catalog itself does — refuses `purposes` under the frozen v1
  context. `DTG_CONTEXTS` is replaced by `W3C_CONTEXT` and
  `DTG_CONTEXT_VERSIONS`.

title: vtc-audit-v0.6.0
body: ### Added - **vtc-service**: Store and serve an uploaded community logo ([#2751](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2751)) * feat(vtc-service): store and serve an uploaded community logo A community can now upload its logo, and the VTC serves it from its own origin, so it shows in the console, the member portal, both sign-in pages and the default landing page wherever the VTC is hosted. Before this, the logo was only the profile's `logoUrl`. Those pages are served with `img-src 'self' data:`, so a logo at any other address was never drawn, and a deployment with nowhere on the VTC's own origin to put a file (a hosted VTC, say) had no logo at all: a filesystem website must have its own host, and `admin_ui.members_dir` is a snapshot that stops following the daemon on every upgrade. What it adds: - `vtc/community/logo/update/0.1` (pinned in `vti-specs-vtc`): an administrator (`vtc.surface.admin`) sends a PNG, JPEG or WebP, or `image: null` to remove the logo. The community re-encodes it as a PNG of at most 512 px (`directory::images::reencode_logo`, sharing the directory's decoding and its bounds), dropping all metadata and any bytes after the image data, and stores it in the `community` keyspace, which is backed up. 20 changes per administrator per hour, one re-encoding at a time, audited as `CommunityLogoUpdated` by digest. - `GET /v1/community/logo`: public, like `public-profile`. Served from memory against a small record read, with a fixed `Content-Type`, `nosniff`, `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, an `ETag` and `304`. Bytes that do not match their record are never served. - A `logo` member (`url`, `sha256`, `mediaType`, `width`, `height`) on the public profile and on `/v1/member/me`'s `community`. Every page draws it in preference to `logoUrl`, which is unchanged. - Console: a Logo card on the Community profile page. It rasterizes an SVG in the browser, from a `data:` URL inside an `` where it runs no script, so no SVG is ever sent or stored. The Logo URL field now says when these pages will not draw the address it holds. Design note: docs/05-design-notes/vtc-community-logo.md.

title: Make the VMC and VDC example acknowledgements carry their grants' digests
body:
Two example acknowledgements reference their grant by digest, but the values didn't reproduce from the grants printed above them. Recomputed from each grant as printed (JCS without `proof`, SHA-256, Multihash, base-58-btc), as #89 did for the VAC example:

| Example | Field | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| VMC: member-issued acknowledgement (chess club) | `credentialSubject.digestMultibase` | `zQmZ3zhk4n6yVDrJwbo4FX5ou27L2tgNnuFRxYrQrGQfUUN` | `zQmVravSbajT8mJSuiqzbfkHdHpzsb95eJCXNMeK4Qmkboc` |
| VDC: acceptance | `delegation.accepts` | `zQmdfTbBqBPQ7VNxZEYEj14VmRuZBkqFbiwReogJgS1zR1n` (the digest of the empty string) | `zQmayYjXD6kAGoo7JkNJQZ85XpSn3S1QpKHGvuFC5iJYEDB` |

Two-line change. The same computation reproduces every other computable digest in the spec: the empty-string digest, the salted VMC pair (#87), the VTN-to-VTN pair (#83) and the attenuated VAC's `parent` (#89).

**Left as is:** the VWC example under `dtg:witnessed`. It is labelled illustrative because neither the trust task document nor the witnessed edge credential is printed, so there is nothing to compute its digests from.

Note: once examples move to context `v3` (#87), these digests change again, and that follow-up will recompute them.

`npm run render` completes without errors.

title: feat!: dtg-credentials 0.16 — a community may declare issuerScope directed
body:
Moves to dtg-credentials 0.16, after DTG Core Credentials (Correlation
Scope, VMC; trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#86): a community's grant is
`directed` at minimum, `public` where the community is open to outsiders.
Only `pairwise` is refused. The library's `context-v3` (salting) feature is
not enabled.

Verifiers now accept a community credential declaring `directed` or
`public`, and keep refusing anything narrower:

- vta-sdk `vetting::eligibility` (a vetter's role VAC);
- vtc-service `members::inbound_vmc` (the grant an acknowledgement binds to).

Issuance: a new VTC setting, `[credentials] issuer_scope` (`public`, the
default and what every earlier release declared, or `directed`), sets the
`issuerScope` the community declares on every DTG credential it issues as
itself — VMCs, role VACs, statements (incl. `vetted/1`) and invitations —
and on its acknowledgements and repudiations as a network member.
`pairwise` is not a valid value. VTC has no existing "open to outsiders"
notion to derive the default from, so it stays `public`. It is carried on
`LocalSigner` (`with_issuer_scope` / `issuer_scope`).

vti-vtn: `Party` gains `issuer_scope()` (default `public`), used by
`member::acknowledge_as` / `repudiate_as`; new
`member::acknowledgement_scoped` / `repudiation_scoped`. The network's own
offers and listings stay `public`.

Release note: verifiers on this release accept `directed` community
credentials. A VTC configured `issuer_scope = "directed"` needs its
counterparties (members' clients, other VTCs/VTNs, vetting applicants) on
this release or later — earlier verifiers refuse anything but `public`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.41.2
body:
### Specifications

- **vtc,vetting**: A community's correlation scope is directed or public, and its profile declares it ([#1356](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1356))

DTG Credentials Working Draft 0.7.0 makes a community's own correlation
  scope `directed` at minimum and `public` where the community is open to
  outsiders; it is no longer always `public`.

  - vtc/_shared/0.1 community: CommunityProfile and CommunityProfileView
    gain an optional `correlationScope` (`directed` | `public`), the
    `issuerScope` the community's credentials carry. Absent, implementations
    issue `public`, as before.
  - vtc/community/profile/update 0.1 accepts it (and refuses `pairwise`);
    profile/show 0.1 returns it through the shared view.
  - vetting/request 0.1, vtc/join-requests/decide 0.1, vtc/endorsements/issue
    0.1, vtc/vetting/vetters/grant 0.1, vtc/members/{credentials,rotate,renew}
    0.1, vtc/members/personhood/{assert 0.2,revoke 0.1} and the shared
    endorsement schema: the community-issued credential's `issuerScope` is
    `directed` or `public`, not `public` only.

  All changes are in place: an optional member and descriptions/prose on
  draft versions, which CONTRIBUTING-SPECS allows for a released version
  (check-published-schemas: additive only).

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the
  tag, which *is* the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,
  `tag-dart` pushes the tag, and `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

fix(vtc): admit v2 DTG credentials at ingress (#2801)

Credential ingress (`credentials::ingress::classify_dtg`) required
`DTG_CONTEXT_V1` at `@context[1]`, so it refused every v2 DTG credential.
dtg-credentials >= 0.14 lists `DTG_CONTEXT_V2` second on any VAC that
states `purposes`, so a VAC carrying purposes could not be submitted to a
VTC at all.

Ingress now admits either DTG context second (`DTG_CONTEXT_VERSIONS`,
built from the catalog's own constants), keeps the W3C v2 context first,
and — as the catalog itself does — refuses `purposes` under the frozen v1
context. `DTG_CONTEXTS` is replaced by `W3C_CONTEXT` and
`DTG_CONTEXT_VERSIONS`.

title: Add a privacy consideration for the effective disclosure of an edge
body:
Addresses #23. One paragraph, one file.

The rule proposed in #23 and supported by both @mitchuski and @albertoleon7794: **a choice of identifier constrains only its own holder's disclosure, and an edge's effective disclosure is the wider of its two halves.**

## Why it is missing today

Privacy consideration 2 covers R-DID reuse — an issuer's own failure, which the issuer can avoid. This is the other case: a *correctly* unique R-DID that is correlated to a named party because the counterparty published the opposing half under an M-DID into a readable graph. The party who loses privacy is the one who followed the specification's recommendation, through an action it neither controls nor can discover. Nothing currently warns an implementation that computing an edge's privacy from the half it issued gives the wrong answer.

## Two corrections to the framing in #23

I filed #23 as a cross-community problem. Two people have since improved on that, and the text reflects them rather than my original framing:

- @albertoleon7794's classifier returns **no answer** — not a wrong one — when asked whether a mixed edge is an R-DID or an M-DID edge, and, more usefully, showed the same failure is reachable **inside a single community** passing through the migration consideration 1 recommends. So it is not a cross-community special case, and the text says so.
- @mitchuski's observer reading generalises past two-party edges, so the paragraph closes on joint presentation: what a set of credentials discloses together may exceed what any of them discloses alone.

## Scope

Stated as a consideration rather than a normative requirement: it describes a property an implementation must compute correctly, not behaviour a credential can be checked against.

Written to stand **independently of #22**. If the declared-scope model lands, this falls out of the vocabulary and the paragraph can be shortened to the one-line rule; until then it needs saying in prose. It also does not depend on #26.

`npm run render` clean, dangling-definitions list unchanged from `main`.

title: Define edge verifiability normatively and strike it from the glossary
body:
Closes #21.

#21 asked four questions and offered a PR once the group had a view on Q1 and Q2. Both now have concordant answers from the ZKP task force ([#21 comment](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/issues/21#issuecomment-5427885485)) and from a second implementation with runnable verifiers ([#21 comment](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/issues/21#issuecomment-5432779043)), so here is the text. It is offered for the editors to react to rather than as a settled outcome.

## What changes

A normative **Edge Verifiability** section is added to Edge Credentials, and both glossary entries are reduced to a pointer at it. Three files, +26/−2.

The section defines the property **with respect to a verifier** rather than in the abstract: a credential is an edge to a verifier when its proof verifies and the verifier can establish that the issuer holds a VMC from a VTC in the anchor set that verifier accepts. A VTN is the common case of such an anchor set, but no VTN need exist. That phrasing is @mitchuski's, who reports the reference circuits already state it that way; it should also serve #24, where the two peers anchor in different VTNs or in none.

## Against the four questions

**Q1 — is edge verifiability a defined property at all?** Now yes, in a normative section. Previously it appeared only in two glossary files.

**Q2 — does a VRC carrying R-DIDs with a community-anchored ZKP satisfy it? Yes.** The anchor predicate may be satisfied by disclosure *or* by proof, and the two are equivalent. Glossary condition (a) — M-DIDs for both peers — is dropped. It would have excluded the construction the specification recommends on privacy grounds, and, as @albertoleon7794 noted, it would have made the specification's own VRC example (`did:peer` to `did:peer`, no membership credential) not an edge.

Per Mitch's qualifier, a note records that the linkage the proof route depends on — that the party controlling the R-DID is the party holding the VMC — is not yet encoded, so that route states an intended design goal until #9 lands. That bears on the proof's witness data, not on whether the edge counts, and the note says so.

**Q3 — strike the dual-signature condition? Yes.** The schema defines one `issuer` and one `proof`, so condition (b) could not be satisfied by *any* credential, including the M-DID edges it existed to bless. The section states instead that each half is signed by its own issuer and evaluated independently, and that the halves need not satisfy it by the same route — which is also the seam #23 needs.

**Q4 — the VMC sentence.** Same unsourced construction, same treatment.

## Scope

Deliberately excluded: the framing of M-DID edges as a bootstrapping state rather than a valid terminal form (raised in a [#21 comment](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/issues/21#issuecomment-5424663130)). It is a real problem but a separable one, and only Q1–Q4 have three-party agreement. Happy to follow up if the editors want it in the same pass.

Also excluded: anything that depends on #22. This fix is written to hold whether or not the four VID types survive.

## Validation

`npm run render` is clean; the dangling-definitions list is byte-identical to `main`, and every `[[ref:]]` in the new section resolves. `VTN trust anchor` remains referenced from two other glossary entries, so removing the references here does not orphan it.
